the Board of\\n        Directors of Contracting Authority and resolved to its satisfaction.\\n  2.2)  having a business or family relationship with a Contracting Authority's staff involved in the selection\\n       procedure or the supervision of the resulting contract, unless the stemming conflict of interest has been\\n        brought to the attention of Board of Directors of Contracting },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 63,\n      \"text\": \"us to have or give access to information contained in the respective bids, influencing them or influencing\\n        decisions of the Contracting calculations and other documentation that are subject of the bid;\\n\\n               ii.    having been recruited (or being proposed to be recruited) ourselves or any of our affiliates, to carry\\n              out works supervision or inspection for this contract;\\n\\n3.           If we are a government-owned entity, we certify that we have legal and financial autonomy and that we\\n       operate under commercial laws and regulations.\\n\\n4.    We undertake to bring to the attention of the BMRCL, any change in situation with regard to points 1 to 3\\n       here above.\\n\\n5.       In the context of procurement and performance of the contract:\\n\\n5.1)  We have not and we will not engage in any dishonest conduct (act or omission) deliberately intended to\\n       deceive     quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"5.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"5.0      Designer’s role\\n\\n5.0       Designer’s role in Safety, Health and Environment\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk to health and safety of those\\n               who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle or demolish the\\n                     structures and any one else like adjoining road users/general public, who might be\\n                    affected by the work.\\n\\n\\n          5.2      General philosophy\\n\\n\\n          5.2.1    When considering health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to do\\n                 what  is reasonable at the time the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\\n                   hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to be looked at during\\n                     detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to health and\\n                    safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\\n                   excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\\n                a concern  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\\n                 However, a judgement has to be made by weighing up one consideration against\\n                   another so the cost is counted not just in financial terms, but also those of fitness for\\n                   purpose,  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By  applying  these\\n                      principles, it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will avoid\\n                     or reduce risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\\n                    considerations  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\\n                    important is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\\n                   proper exercise of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues.\\n\\n\\n          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control\\n\\n\\n          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as reasonably practicable, to avoid or reduce risks by\\n                    applying a series of steps known as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of\\n                    prevention and protection. The steps to be adopted shall include the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     consider  if the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be\\n                        avoided (e.g., alter the design to avoid the risk);\\n\\n                                    ii)        if this cannot be achieved, the risk should be combated at source (e.g., ensure\\n                          the design details of items to be lifted include attachment points for lifting);\\n\\n                                     iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will\\n                           protect all people;\\n\\n                          iv)    only as a last resort should measures to control risk by means of personal\\n                           protection be assumed (e.g., use of safety harnesses).\\n\\n          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing itself\\n\\n\\n          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design work and\\n                  concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\\n                     detailed information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\\n                   This information needs to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,\\n                  which they cannot reasonably be expected to know. This is essential for the parties\\n               who have to use the design information.\\n\\n\\n          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\\n                    safety risks are not obvious from the standard design document, the designer shall\\n                   provide additional information. The information shall include a broad indication of the\\n                  assumptions about the precautions for dealing with the risks. The information will\\n                need to be conveyed in a clear manner; it shall be included on drawings, in written\\n                     specifications or outline method statements. The level of detail to be recorded will\\n                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved and the associated level of risk.\\n\\n\\n          5.5      Employer’s approval\\n\\n\\n          5.5.1    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\\n                       etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\\n                      to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions shall approve  all these\\n          designs.\\n\\n\\n5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles made up of re-bars or structures which are\\n          very old, corroded, repaired for many times etc. for which no design calculations can\\n        be made accurately from any national standards, shall not be allowed to be used at\\n           sites even for short duration.\\n\\n\\n5.7           If any of the above-mentioned clauses are not adhered penalty shall be imposed\\n         depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"5.0      Designer’s This is essential for the parties\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 58,\n      \"text\": \"               who have to use the design information.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 61,\n      \"text\": \"          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 62,\n      \"text\": \"                    safety risks are not obvious from the standard design document, the designer shall\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 63,\n      \"text\": \"                   provide additional information. The information shall include a broad indication of the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 64,\n      \"text\": \"                  assumptions about the precautions for dealing with the risks. The information will\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 65,\n      \"text\": \"                need to be conveyed in a clear manner; it shall be included on drawings, in written\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"                     specifications or outline method statements. The level of detail to be recorded will\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 67,\n      \"text\": \"                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved and the associated level of risk.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 68,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 69,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 70,\n      \"text\": \"          5.5      Employer’s approval\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 71,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 72,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 73,\n      \"text\": \"          5.5.1    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 74,\n      \"text\": \"                       etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 75,\n      \"text\": \"                      to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 76,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 77,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"source_line_number\": 78,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"          consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions shall approve  all these\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"          designs.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 5,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 6,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 7,\n      \"text\": \"5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles made up of re-bars or structures which are\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 8,\n      \"text\": \"          very old, corroded, repaired for many times etc. for which no design calculations can\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 9,\n      \"text\": \"        be made accurately from any national standards, shall not be allowed to be used at\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 10,\n      \"text\": \"           sites even for short duration.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 11,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 12,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"         depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n     quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"6.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\\n\\n\\n6.1      Education and Experience\\n\\n\\n6.1.1    The contractor shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed in General\\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 (enclosed at the end) based upon the statutory\\n         requirement and establish the safety organisation based upon the contract value.\\n        The minimum educational  qualification and the work experience are given  in\\n         General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/002\\n\\n\\n6.1.2     In order to effectively interact on labour welfare matters with the Employer and\\n         the  statutory  authorities  enforcing  the  labour  welfare  legislations every\\n         contractor shall employ a full time Labour Welfare Officer duly qualified and\\n         experienced as per clause 6.1.1.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n6.2     Conduct and Competency\\n\\n6. 2.1    The conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored by\\n          the Employer. Any default or deficiency shall attract penalty as per details given\\n         under penalty clause 56.0 of this document.\\n\\n\\n6.2.2    The Contractor shall ensure that  all personnel are competent to perform the job\\n         assigned to them. In the event that the Contractor is unable to demonstrate the\\n        competency of any person whose activities can directly impact on the Works’ SHE\\n         performance, the Employer shall remove that person from the site without any\\n          procedural formalities.\\n\\n\\n6.3      Approval from Employer\\n\\n\\n6.3.1    The name, address, educational qualification, work experience and health condition\\n           of each personnel deployed for SHE jobs shall be submitted to the Employer in the\\n          format prescribed for the purpose for comments and approval well before the start of\\n          the work. Only on approval by the Employer these personnel are authorised to work.\\n           In case any of the SHE personnel leaves the contractor the same shall be intimated\\n           to the Employer. The contractor shall recruit new personnel and fill up the vacancy.\\n\\n\\n6.4      Responsibility of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n6.4.1    For  all works carried out by the contractor and his sub-contractors, the\\n          responsibility of ensuring the required SHE manpower lies with the main\\n         contractor only. The minimum required manpower indicated by the Employer\\n         includes the sub-contractors’ work also. It shall be the responsibility of the\\n        main contractor to provide required SHE manpower for all the works executed\\n        by all contractors. Necessary conditions shall be included in all sub-contract\\n        documents executed by the main contractor.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"6.5     Employment status of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.5.1    No contractor shall engage SHE manpower from any outsourcing agencies in\\n                  which case the effectiveness would be lost.  All SHE manpower shall be on the\\n                      payroll of the main contractor only and not on the payroll of any subcontractor or\\n                   outsourcing manpower agencies etc. This condition does not apply to positions like\\n                          traffic marshals who are engaged almost on a daily requirement basis.\\n\\n\\n          6.6      Reporting of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.6.1      All SHE personnel are to report to the Chief SHE Manager who shall report directly to\\n                    the Chief Project Manager. The Employer shall monitor adherence to this procedure\\n                      at all times. In case of non-adherence penalty shall be levied as indicated in the\\n                    penalty clause.\\n\\n\\n          6.7      Inadequate SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.7.1      In case if the contractor fail to provide the minimum required manpower as\\n                     illustrated in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 or fail to fill up vacancies\\n                  created within 14 days, the same shall be provided by the Employer at\\n                   contractor’s cost. Any administrative expenses involved, providing the same\\n                      like paper advertisement or manpower consultant charges, etc shall also be at\\n                  the cost of contractor.\\n\\n\\n          6.8       Prohibition of performance of other duties\\n\\n\\n          6.8.1    As per Schedule VIII of BOCWR no SHE personnel shall be required or permitted to\\n                 do any work which  is unconnected  to, inconsistent with or detrimental  to the\\n                  performance  of the SHE  duties  for respective category mentioned  in General\\n                    Information BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\\n\\n\\n          6.9       Facilities to be provided to SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.9.1    As per schedule VIII of BOCWR, the contractor shall provide all SHE personnel with\\n                 such  facilities, equipment and information that are necessary to enable him to\\n                    dispatch his duties effectively.\\n\\n\\n          6.9.2    The minimum Employer’s requirements of such facilities / equipments to be provided\\n                       for SHE personnel are given in the General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/003\"\n    }\n  ],\n     quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"5.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"5.0      Designer’s role\\n\\n5.0       Designer’s role in Safety, Health and Environment\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk to health and safety of those\\n               who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle or demolish the\\n                     structures and any one else like adjoining road users/general public, who might be\\n                    affected by the work.\\n\\n\\n          5.2      General philosophy\\n\\n\\n          5.2.1    When considering health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to do\\n                 what  is reasonable at the time the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\\n                   hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to be looked at during\\n                     detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to health and\\n                    safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\\n                   excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\\n                a concern  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\\n                 However, a judgement has to be made by weighing up one consideration against\\n                   another so the cost is counted not just in financial terms, but also those of fitness for\\n                   purpose,  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By  applying  these\\n                      principles, it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will avoid\\n                     or reduce risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\\n                    considerations  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\\n                    important is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\\n                   proper exercise of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues.\\n\\n\\n          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control\\n\\n\\n          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as reasonably practicable, to avoid or reduce risks by\\n                    applying a series of steps known as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of\\n                    prevention and protection. The steps to be adopted shall include the following:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     consider  if the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be\\n                        avoided (e.g., alter the design to avoid the risk);\\n\\n                                    ii)        if this cannot be achieved, the risk should be combated at source (e.g., ensure\\n                          the design details of items to be lifted include attachment points for lifting);\\n\\n                                     iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will\\n                           protect all people;\\n\\n                          iv)    only as a last resort should measures to control risk by means of personal\\n                           protection be assumed (e.g., use of safety harnesses).\\n\\n          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing itself\\n\\n\\n          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design work and\\n                  concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\\n                     detailed information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\\n                   This information needs to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,\\n                  which they cannot reasonably be expected to know. This is essential for the parties\\n               who have to use the design information.\\n\\n\\n          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\\n                    safety risks are not obvious from the standard design document, the designer shall\\n                   provide additional information. The information shall include a broad indication of the\\n                  assumptions about the precautions for dealing with the risks. The information will\\n                need to be conveyed in a clear manner; it shall be included on drawings, in written\\n                     specifications or outline method statements. The level of detail to be recorded will\\n                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved and the associated level of risk.\\n\\n\\n          5.5      Employer’s approval\\n\\n\\n          5.5.1    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\\n                       etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\\n                      to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions shall approve  all these\\n          designs.\\n\\n\\n5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles made up of re-bars or structures which are\\n          very old, corroded, repaired for many times etc. for which no design calculations can\\n        be made accurately from any national standards, shall not be allowed to be used at\\n           sites even for short duration.\\n\\n\\n5.7           If any of the above-mentioned clauses are not adhered penalty shall be imposed\\n         depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"5.0      Designer’s     quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"6.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\\n\\n\\n6.1      Education and Experience\\n\\n\\n6.1.1    The contractor shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed in General\\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 (enclosed at the end) based upon the statutory\\n         requirement and establish the safety organisation based upon the contract value.\\n        The minimum educational  qualification and the work experience are given  in\\n         General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/002\\n\\n\\n6.1.2     In order to effectively interact on labour welfare matters with the Employer and\\n         the  statutory  authorities  enforcing  the  labour  welfare  legislations every\\n         contractor shall employ a full time Labour Welfare Officer duly qualified and\\n         experienced as per clause 6.1.1.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n6.2     Conduct and Competency\\n\\n6. 2.1    The conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored by\\n          the Employer. Any default or deficiency shall attract penalty as per details given\\n         under penalty clause 56.0 of this document.\\n\\n\\n6.2.2    The Contractor shall ensure that  all personnel are competent to perform the job\\n         assigned to them. In the event that the Contractor is unable to demonstrate the\\n        competency of any person whose activities can directly impact on the Works’ SHE\\n         performance, the Employer shall remove that person from the site without any\\n          procedural formalities.\\n\\n\\n6.3      Approval from Employer\\n\\n\\n6.3.1    The name, address, educational qualification, work experience and health condition\\n           of each personnel deployed for SHE jobs shall be submitted to the Employer in the\\n          format prescribed for the purpose for comments and approval well before the start of\\n          the work. Only on approval by the Employer these personnel are authorised to work.\\n           In case any of the SHE personnel leaves the contractor the same shall be intimated\\n           to the Employer. The contractor shall recruit new personnel and fill up the vacancy.\\n\\n\\n6.4      Responsibility of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n6.4.1    For  all works carried out by the contractor and his sub-contractors, the\\n          responsibility of ensuring the required SHE manpower lies with the main\\n         contractor only. The minimum required manpower indicated by the Employer\\n         includes the sub-contractors’ work also. It shall be the responsibility of the\\n        main contractor to provide required SHE manpower for all the works executed\\n        by all contractors. Necessary conditions shall be included in all sub-contract\\n        documents executed by the main contractor.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"6.5     Employment status of SHE personnel\\n\\n\\n          6.5.1    No contractor shall engage SHE manpower from any outsourcing agencies in\\n                  which case the effectiveness would be lost. authorities  enforcing  the  labour  welfare  legislations every\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 32,\n      \"text\": \"         contractor shall employ a full {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 34,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 35,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n \"text\": \"6. 2.1    The conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored by\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 42,\n      \"text\": \"          the Employer. Any default or deficiency shall attract penalty as per details given\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 43,\n      \"text\": \"         under penalty clause 56.0 of this document.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 44,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 45,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 46,\n      \"text\": \"6.2.2    The Contractor shall ensure that  all personnel are competent to perform the job\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 47,\n      \"text\": \"         assigned to them. In the event that the Contractor is unable to demonstrate the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 48,\n      \"text\": \"        competency of any person whose activities can directly impact on the Works’ SHE\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 49,\n      \"text\": \"         performance, the Employer shall remove that person from the site without any\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 50,\n      \"text\": \"          procedural formalities.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 51,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 53,\n      \"text\": \"6.3      Approval from Employer\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 54,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 55,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"6.3.1    The name, address, educational qualification, work experience and health condition\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"           of each personnel deployed for SHE jobs shall be submitted to the Employer in the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 58,\n      \"text\": \"          format prescribed for the purpose for comments and approval well before the start of\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"          the work. Only on approval by the Employer these personnel are authorised to work.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"           In case any of the SHE personnel leaves the contractor the same shall be intimated\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 61,\n      \"text\": \"           to the Employer. The contractor shall recruit new personnel and fill up the vacancy.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 62,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 63,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 64,\n      \"text\": \"6.4      Responsibility of SHE personnel\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 65,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 67,\n      \"text\": \"6.4.1    For  all works carried out by the contractor and his sub-contractors, the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 68,\n      \"text\": \"          responsibility of ensuring the required SHE manpower lies with the main\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 69,\n      \"text\": \"         contractor only. The minimum required manpower indicated by the Employer\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 70,\n      \"text\": \"         includes the sub-contractors’ work also. It shall be the responsibility of the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 71,\n      \"text\": \"        main contractor to provide required SHE manpower for all the works executed\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 72,\n      \"text\": \"        by all contractors. Necessary conditions shall be included in all sub-contract\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 73,\n      \"text\": \"        documents executed by the main contractor.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 74,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 75,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 76,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 77,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 16,\n      \"source_line_number\": 78,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"          6.5     Employment status of SHE personnel\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 5,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 6,\n      \"text\": \"          6.5.1    No contractor shall engage SHE manpower from any outsourcing agencies in\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 7,\n      \"text\": \"                  which case the effectiveness would be lost.  All SHE manpower shall be on the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 8,\n      \"text\": \"                      payroll of the main contractor only and not on the payroll of any subcontractor or\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 9,\n      \"text\": \"                   outsourcing manpower agencies etc. This condition does not apply to positions like\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 10,\n      \"text\": \"                          traffic marshals who are engaged almost on a daily requirement basis.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 11,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 12,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"          6.6      Reporting of SHE personnel\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"          6.6.1      All SHE personnel are to report to the Chief SHE Manager who shall report directly to\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"                    the Chief Project Manager. The Employer shall monitor adherence to this procedure\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"                      at all times. In case of non-adherence penalty shall be levied as indicated in the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"                    penalty clause.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 20,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"          6.7      Inadequate SHE personnel\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 23,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 24,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 25,\n      \"text\": \"          6.7.1      In case if the contractor fail to provide the minimum required manpower as\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 26,\n      \"text\": \"                     illustrated in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 or fail to fill up vacancies\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 27,\n      \"text\": \"                  created within 14 days, the same shall be provided by the Employer at\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 28,\n      \"text\": \"                   contractor’s cost. Any administrative expenses involved, providing the same\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 29,\n      \"text\": \"                      like paper advertisement or manpower consultant charges, etc shall also be at\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 30,\n      \"text\": \"                  the cost of contractor.\"\n      Facilities to be provided to SHE personnel\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n      \"source_line_number\": 43,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 17,\n and programs.\\n\\n\\n          10.3      Following SHE inspections program shall be adopted.\\n\\n                                 i)    Planned General Inspection\\n\\n                                    ii)    Routine Inspection\\n\\n                                     iii)    Specific Inspection\\n\\n                          iv)   Other Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1   Planned General Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections are performed at predetermined intervals and  it usually\\n                    involves the representation from both Contractor and safety committee Inspection.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly safety inspection by construction supervisors (Contractors and Sub-\\n                            contractors).\\n\\n                                     iii)    Daily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.2    Routine Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.2.1  Routine hand tools by competent electrical supervisor\\n\\n                          iv)    Quarterly Inspection of temporary electrical systems by competent electrical\\n                          supervisor\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances, equipment and\\n              gears by Govt. approved Contractor may add additional categories.\\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants, equipment, powered  tools and any other\\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators and workmen.\\n\\n\\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\\n\\n\\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections for ensuring an activity whether it\\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules; method statement submitted or\\n         developed procedures.\\n\\n\\n        The following are examples that will be commonly performed as required on the\\n          construction site:\\n\\n\\n                i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\\n\\n                  ii)    Inspection performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\\n\\n                  iii)    Inspection performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\\n\\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork before concreting by formwork erector.\\n\\n\\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor shall ensure that a\\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\\n\\n\\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\\n\\n         Other inspections include the following:\\n\\n                i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\\n\\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE management team\\n\\n\\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist for  all activity\\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian standards,\\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements.     quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"11.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"11.0    SHE Audit\\n\\n\\n11.1     General\\n\\n\\n11.1.1   The purpose and scope of SHE audit is to assess potential risk, liabilities and the\\n         degree of compliance of construction Safety, Health and Environmental plan and its\\n         supplementary  procedures and programs  against  applicable and  current SHE\\n           legalisation regulations and requirements of the employer.\\n\\n\\n11.1.2    Project Manager holds the ultimate responsibility in ensuring implementation of SHE\\n          audit program during the construction work.\\n\\n\\n11.2     Monthly Audit Rating Score (M A R S)\\n\\n\\n11.2.1   Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) will be performed once in a month. A team\\n         consisting of Project manager and Employer representative based on the pre-\\n        designed score-rating format will conduct  it. The details of the pre-designed\\n        monthly audit score rating formats are given in the Project SHE manual.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 23,\n      \"text\": \"11.2.2    This Monthly SHE Audit Rating Score (MARS) report will enable the Employer to\\n                   evaluate the general compliance by the Contractor with the Conditions of Contract, the\\n                  Employer’s Project SHE Manual and the Contractor’s site specific SHE Plan.\\n\\n\\n          11.2.3   Monthly Audits  will be conducted in accordance with BMRC Guidelines.  The\\n                    Project Manager accompanied by the Employer’s representatives shall carry out\\n                    the Audit. The Contractor’s senior manager and SHE in-charge should also be\\n                      invited to attend.\\n\\n\\n          11.2.4   Timing\\n\\n\\n                The Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) should be conducted at least 7 days\\n                       prior to the scheduled date of Monthly SHE Committee meeting.\\n\\n\\n          11.2.5   Evaluation\\n\\n\\n          11.2.5.1  The numerical scoring has been weighed on a 1-10 scale. The audit team will use\\n                        their observations noted in evaluating the points to be awarded against each of\\n                    the elements of the audited section. Wherever some topics and sub-topics are not\\n                    applicable the score rating need not be given. The overall audit ratings shall be\\n                  achieved by:\\n\\n\\n                    Overall Audit rating  =    Actual Score Achieved   X 100\\n\\n                                  Maximum Possible Score\\n\\n\\n          11.2.5.2  The criticality of the required actions for the respective sections of the Audit will be\\n                      classified as:\\n\\n\\n                          Sl.   Score          Description                          Action\\n                   No.\\n\\n                 1    < 60%   Immediate               Require Contractor to rectify within 24\\n                                                          hours\\n\\n                 2    < 75%   Improvement             Contractor rectification within 7 days and\\n                                Necessary               confirmed in writing to Employer\\n\\n                 3    < 90%   Improvement Desirable    Contractor rectification within one month\\n                                                    and confirmed in writing to Employer\\n\\n\\n          11.2.6   Report\\n\\n              A copy of each Audit Report will be sent to Employer and to all subcontractors,\\n                     with whom  it  will then be discussed in detail at the Monthly SHE Committee\\n                  Meeting in order to ensure that any corrective actions are agreed upon.\\n\\n\\n          11.3     Monthly Electrical Safety Audit\\n\\n\\n          11.3.1   A team comprising of contractor’s senior SHE (Electrical) engineer and Employer’s\\n                    representative shall conduct monthly electrical safety audit covering the following and\\n                  submit the report to Employer.\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Electrical accidents investigation findings and remedy\\n\\n                                    ii)   Adequacy of power generation and power requirements\\n\\n                                     iii)   Power distribution and transmission system in place\\n\\n                          iv)   Updated electrical single line diagram showing the current condition of power\\n                        source and distribution including the IP44 DBs arrangement.\\n\\n                      v)     Electrical protection devices – selection, installation and maintenance.\\n\\n                          vi)   Earth or ground connection and earth pit maintenance details\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 24,\n      \"text\": \"vii)   Education and training of electrical personnel undertaken\\n\\n               viii)  Routine electrical inspection details\\n\\n             ix)    Electrical maintenance system and register.\\n\\n           x)   Name plate details of major electrical equipment\\n\\n             xi)    Classified zones in the site, if any.\\n\\n11.4   External SHE Audi\\n\\n\\n11.4.1    External SHE audits are  to be conducted by  external agencies  that are\\n        competent with ISO qualified auditors with the prior approval of the Employer.\\n\\n\\n11.4.2   Areas of competence of Audit team\\n\\n\\n11.4.2.1  Practical understanding of BOCW Act and Rules, statutory requirements on\\n         health/medical and welfare of workmen, construction hazards and its prevention\\n        and control, traffic management, electrical safety, rigging, safety of construction\\n        equipment and environment management.\\n\\n\\n11.4.2.2  Audit shall be conducted as per the guidelines of ISO, ILO, and national\\n         standards. Audit report shall also be presented as per the above formats.\\n\\n\\n11.4.3    External SHE audit shall be conducted on a quarterly basis throughout the\\n         currency of the contract.\\n\\n\\n11.4.4    Targets of SHE Audit:\\n\\n\\n        The contents and coverage of the external audit shall include the following items\\n\\n\\n11.4.4.1 SHE management:\\n\\n\\n                i)     Organization\\n\\n                  ii)    Communication and Motivation\\n\\n                  iii)   Time office\\n\\n             iv)    Inspection\\n\\n           v)   Emergency preparedness\\n\\n             vi)   Budget allocation\\n\\n              vii)   Education and Training\\n\\n               viii)  Work permit system\\n\\n\\n11.4.4.2  Technical:\\n\\n\\n                i)     Building and Structure\\n\\n                  ii)    Construction operational safety\\n\\n                  iii)    Material safety\\n\\n             iv)   Hand tools and Power tools\\n\\n           v)     Electrical system\\n\\n             vi)    Safety Appliances\\n\\n              vii)   Fire prevention and control\\n\\n               viii)  Housekeeping\\n\\n             ix)   Maintenance and Machinery safety\\n\\n           x)     First-aid and Medical Facilities\\n\\n             xi)   Welfare measures\\n\\n              xii)   Environmental Management\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 25,\n      \"text\": \"11.4.5   Audit Documents:\\n\\n\\n          11.4.5.1  Contractor shall make the below listed documents available for the review by\\n                  the Audit team.\\n\\n\\n                                 i)   SHE policy\\n\\n                                    ii)   SHE manual\\n\\n                                     iii)   SHE Rules and Regulation\\n\\n                          iv)  SHE organization chart\\n\\n                      v)    Annual SHE objectives / programs\\n\\n                          vi)   Accident / near miss statistics and analysis\\n\\n                             vii)  SHE Training program / records for all personnel\\n\\n                               viii)  Operating manuals and maintenance manual of all equipments\\n\\n                          ix)   Safe worthiness certificates of all lifting appliances and gears\\n\\n                      x)    Medical fitness record for all personnel\\n\\n                          xi)   Risk identification, assessment and control details\\n\\n                             xii)   Environmental management reports\\n\\n                               xiii)  Emergency management records including mock drill\\n\\n\\n          11.4.6    Audit Preparation:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Audit team members are required to gather information by observations through\\n                           interviews and by checks of hardware and documentation.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Audit team shall prepare checklist to cover all parts based on SHE legislations\\n                           rules and regulations and BMRC requirements.\\n\\n                                     iii)    Audit team members shall verify the facts and findings leading to the identified\\n                      gaps and weakness.\\n\\n                          iv)    Audit leader has overall responsibility for reaching a conclusion.\\n\\n\\n          11.4.7    Reporting:\\n\\n\\n          11.4.7.1  Audit report shall be prepared and directly sent to the Employer within 7 days of\\n                   conducting the audit with a copy to the contractor.\\n\\n\\n          11.4.8   Report contents:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    Executing summary - based on the finalized checklists as written the findings to\\n                          the Employer by the audit team members, the audit leader  will compile a\\n                        concise and accurate summary of observations and findings.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Introduction  -  this  will contain basic information regarding the  facilities or\\n                          organization audited, the specific audit dates (inclusion of those for preparation\\n                     and post-audit activities).\\n\\n                                     iii)    Principal positive findings - This will contain the summary of positive aspects as\\n                       observed by the auditors.   It will also contain highlights of those issue, which\\n                   may warrant dissemination as best practice regarding methodology used or\\n                        achievement.\\n\\n\\n                          iv)    Audit Findings - All audit findings as detailed in the audit checklists shall be\\n                       grouped together as priority 1 and 2 as detailed below in a separate listing.\\n\\n                          a)      Priority  1: Actions  to  rectify gaps or weakness should generally be\\n                            implemented within 2 – weeks, if risk potential is high or unacceptable.\\n\\n                          b)      Priority 2: Actions should be generally implemented or rectified with a\\n                       maximum of 3 – 4 weeks, if not rectified would create a likelihood of minor\\n                                    injury or business loss.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 26,\n      \"text\": \"11.4.9    Conformity Report & Action by Employer\\n\\n\\n11.4.9.1  The auditor shall inspect the site after 14 days of conducting initial audit for checking\\n          the adequacy of implementation of items maintained under priority 1 by the contractor\\n        and shall submit a conformity / non-conformity report to the Employer with a copy to the\\n          contractor.\\n\\n\\n11.4.9.2  The auditor shall again inspect after 28 days of conducting initial audit for checking the\\n        adequacy of implementation of items mentioned under priority 2 by the contractor and\\n           shall submit a conformity / non-conformity report to the Employer with a copy to the\\n          contractor.\\n\\n\\n11.4.9.3  In case of non-conformity of items mentioned by auditor, the Employer shall take\\n         necessary steps including stoppage of work and or imposing any penalty for getting the\\n          item implemented.\\n\\n\\n11.4.10   Failure of contractor to conduct External SHE Audit\\n\\n\\n11.4.10.1 If the contractor fails to conduct the external SHE audit in time, the Employer at\\n         the cost of contractor shall get it done.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\":     quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"14.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"text\": \"14.0     Accident reporting and investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.1     Reporting to Employer\\n\\n\\n          14.1.1    All accidents and dangerous occurrences  shall immediately be informed\\n                   verbally to the Employer. This will enable the Employer to reach to the scene of\\n                  accident  / dangerous occurrences to monitor/assist any rescue work and/or\\n                     start conducting the investigation process so that the evidences are not lost.\\n\\n\\n          14.1.2   Reports of all accidents (fatal / injury) and dangerous occurrences shall also be\\n                  sent within 24 hours as per format provided in the Employer’s Project SHE\\n                 manual.\\n\\n          14.1.3   No accident   / dangerous occurrences  is exempted from reporting to the\\n                 Employer.\\n\\n\\n          14.1.4   Any wilful delay in verbal and written reporting to the Employer shall be\\n                  penalised as per relevant clause.\\n\\n\\n          14.2     Reporting to Govt. organisations\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 28,\n      \"text\": \"14.2.1    In addition to the above verbal and written reporting to the Employer, as per Rule 210\\n           of BOCWR, notice of any accident to a worker at the building or construction site that:\\n\\n\\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\\n\\n          b)    disables a worker from working for a period of 48 hours or more immediately\\n                 following the accident;\\n\\n           c)     shall forthwith be sent by telegram, telephone, fax, or similar other means\\n                including special messenger within four hours in case of fatal accidents and 72\\n              hours in case of other accidents, to:\\n\\n                          i)     the Regional Labour Commissioner, wherein the contractor has registered\\n                     the firm/work\\n\\n                            ii)    the board with which the worker involved was registered as a beneficiary;\\n\\n                             iii)    Director General and\\n\\n                     iv)    the next of kin or other relative of the worker involved in the accident;\\n\\n\\n14.2.2    Further, notice of accident shall be sent in respect of an accident which\\n\\n\\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\\n\\n          b)    disables the injured worker from work for more than 10 days to\\n\\n                          i)     the officer-in-charge of the nearest police station;\\n\\n                            ii)    the District Magistrate or, if the District Magistrate by order so desires, to\\n\\n                             iii)    the Sub-Divisional Magistrate\\n\\n\\n14.2.3    In case of an accident causing minor injury, first-aid shall be administered and the\\n           injured worker shall be immediately transferred to a hospital or other place for medical\\n          treatment.\\n\\n14.2.4   Where any accident causing disablement that subsequently results in death, notice in\\n           writing of such death, shall be sent to the authorities mentioned in clause 14.2.1 and\\n          14.2.2 above within 72 hours of such death.\\n\\n\\n14.2.5    Reporting of dangerous occurrences:\\n\\n\\n14.2.5.1  The following classes of dangerous occurrences shall be reported to the Inspector\\n         having jurisdiction, whether or not any disablement or death caused to the worker,\\n         namely:\\n\\n\\n          a)    collapse or  failure  of  lifting appliances,  or  hoist,  or conveyors, or  similar\\n              equipment for handling of building or construction material or breakage or failure\\n                 of rope, chain or loose gears; or overturning of cranes used in construction\\n               work;\\n\\n          b)     falling of objects from height;\\n\\n           c)    collapse or subsidence of soil, tunnel, pipe lines, any wall, floor, gallery, roof or\\n             any other part of any structure, launching girder, platform, staging, scaffolding or\\n            means of access including formwork;\\n\\n          d)    explosion of receiver or vessel used  for storage of pressure greater than\\n               atmospheric pressure, of any gas or gases or any liquid or solid used as\\n                 building material;\\n\\n          e)     fire and explosion causing damage to any place on construction site where\\n                 building workers are employed;\\n\\n               f)     spillage or leakage of any hazardous substance and damage to their container;\\n\\n          g)    collapse, capsizing, toppling or collision of transport equipment;\\n\\n          h)    leakage or release of harmful toxic gases at the construction site;\\n\\n\\n14.2.6    In case of failure of launching girder, lifting appliance, loose gear, hoist or building and\\n          other construction work, machinery and transport equipment at a construction site,\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"text\": \"such appliances, gear, hoist, machinery or equipment and the site of such occurrence\\n                       shall, as far as practicable, be kept undisturbed until inspected by the Authorities;\\n\\n\\n          14.2.7   Every notice given for fatal accidents or dangerous occurrences shall be followed by a\\n                      written report to the concerned Authorities under Section 39 of BOCWA and the\\n                     Director General in the specified Form XIV of BOCWR.\\n\\n\\n          14.3     Accident investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1   General\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1.1  Investigations  should be  conducted  in an open and  positive atmosphere  that\\n                 encourages the witnesses to talk freely. The primary objective is to ascertain the facts\\n                     with a view to prevent future and possibly more serious occurrences\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1.2  Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which result in death, serious injury or serious\\n               damage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find out the cause of the\\n                   accident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1.3  Near misses and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as\\n                 soon as possible as they are signals  that there are inadequacies  in the safety\\n                management system.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2   Procedure of incident investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2.1   It is important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to\\n                    the incident is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed;\\n\\n                     a)    take photographs and make sketches\\n\\n                     b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the environmental\\n                          conditions\\n\\n                      c)    interview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties\\n\\n                     d)    consult expert opinion where necessary\\n\\n                     e)    identify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2.2  Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident\\n\\n                     a)    establish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident\\n\\n                     b)    find out at what stage the accident took place\\n\\n                      c)    consider all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to\\n                         the accident, and identify the most probable cause The cause of an accident\\n                        should never be classified as carelessness. The specific act or omission that\\n                      caused the accident must be identified.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2.3  The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up action\\n\\n                     a)    report on the findings and conclusions\\n\\n                     b)    formulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence\\n\\n                      c)    publicise the findings and the remedial actions taken\\n\\n\\n          14.4     Employers’ independent incident investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.4.1    In case of fatal / dangerous occurrence the Employer shall also conduct independent\\n                      investigation. Contractor and his staff shall extend necessary co-operation and testify\\n                  about the accident.\\n\\n\\n          14.4.2   The contractor shall take every effort to preserve the scene of accident till the Employer\\n                  completes the investigation.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"text\": \"14.4.3     All persons summoned by the Employer in connection to witness recording shall obey\\n          the instructions without delay. Any wilful suppression of information by any person shall\\n        be removed from the site immediately and  / or punishable as per relevant penalty\\n          clause.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          14.0     Accident reporting and investigation\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"          14.0     Accident reporting and investigation\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 61,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 62,\n      \"text\": \"          14.1     Reporting to Employer\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 63,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 64,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 65,\n      \"text\": \"          14.1.1    All accidents and dangerous occurrences  shall immediately be informed\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"                   verbally to the Employer.     quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"14.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"text\": \"14.0     Accident reporting and investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.1     Reporting to Employer\\n\\n\\n          14.1.1    All accidents and dangerous occurrences  shall immediately be informed\\n                   verbally to the Employer. This will enable the Employer to reach to the scene of\\n                  accident  / dangerous occurrences to monitor/assist any rescue work and/or\\n                     start conducting the investigation process so that the evidences are not lost.\\n\\n\\n          14.1.2   Reports of all accidents (fatal / injury) and dangerous occurrences shall also be\\n                  sent within 24 hours as per format provided in the Employer’s Project SHE\\n                 manual.\\n\\n          14.1.3   No accident   / dangerous occurrences  is exempted from reporting to the\\n                 Employer.\\n\\n\\n          14.1.4   Any wilful delay in verbal and written reporting to the Employer shall be\\n                  penalised as per relevant clause.\\n\\n\\n          14.2     Reporting to Govt. organisations\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 28,\n      \"text\": \"14.2.1    In addition to the above verbal and written reporting to the Employer, as per Rule 210\\n           of BOCWR, notice of any accident to a worker at the building or construction site that:\\n\\n\\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\\n\\n          b)    disables a worker from working for a period of 48 hours or more immediately\\n                 following the accident;\\n\\n           c)     shall forthwith be sent by telegram, telephone, fax, or similar other means\\n                including special messenger within four hours in case of fatal accidents and 72\\n              hours in case of other accidents, to:\\n\\n                          i)     the Regional Labour Commissioner, wherein the contractor has registered\\n                     the firm/work\\n\\n                            ii)    the board with which the worker involved was registered as a beneficiary;\\n\\n                             iii)    Director General and\\n\\n                     iv)    the next of kin or other relative of the worker involved in the accident;\\n\\n\\n14.2.2    Further, notice of accident shall be sent in respect of an accident which\\n\\n\\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\\n\\n          b)    disables the injured worker from work for more than 10 days to\\n\\n                          i)     the officer-in-charge of the nearest police station;\\n\\n                            ii)    the District Magistrate or, if the District Magistrate by order so desires, to\\n\\n                             iii)    the Sub-Divisional Magistrate\\n\\n\\n14.2.3    In case of an accident causing minor injury, first-aid shall be administered and the\\n           injured worker shall be immediately transferred to a hospital or other place for medical\\n          treatment.\\n\\n14.2.4   Where any accident causing disablement that subsequently results in death, notice in\\n           writing of such death, shall be sent to the authorities mentioned in clause 14.2.1 and\\n          14.2.2 above within 72 hours of such death.\\n\\n\\n14.2.5    Reporting of dangerous occurrences:\\n\\n\\n14.2.5.1  The following classes of dangerous occurrences shall be reported to the Inspector\\n         having jurisdiction, whether or not any disablement or death caused to the worker,\\n         namely:\\n\\n\\n          a)    collapse or  failure  of  lifting appliances,  or  hoist,  or conveyors, or  similar\\n              equipment for handling of building or construction material or breakage or failure\\n                 of rope, chain or loose gears; or overturning of cranes used in construction\\n               work;\\n\\n          b)     falling of objects from height;\\n\\n           c)    collapse or subsidence of soil, tunnel, pipe lines, any wall, floor, gallery, roof or\\n             any other part of any structure, launching girder, platform, staging, scaffolding or\\n            means of access including formwork;\\n\\n          d)    explosion of receiver or vessel used  for storage of pressure greater than\\n               atmospheric pressure, of any gas or gases or any liquid or solid used as\\n                 building material;\\n\\n          e)     fire and explosion causing damage to any place on construction site where\\n                 building workers are employed;\\n\\n               f)     spillage or leakage of any hazardous substance and damage to their container;\\n\\n          g)    collapse, capsizing, toppling or collision of transport equipment;\\n\\n          h)    leakage or release of harmful toxic gases at the construction site;\\n\\n\\n14.2.6    In case of failure of launching girder, lifting appliance, loose gear, hoist or building and\\n          other construction work, machinery and transport equipment at a construction site,\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"text\": \"such appliances, gear, hoist, machinery or equipment and the site of such occurrence\\n                       shall, as far as practicable, be kept undisturbed until inspected by the Authorities;\\n\\n\\n          14.2.7   Every notice given for fatal accidents or dangerous occurrences shall be followed by a\\n                      written report to the concerned Authorities under Section 39 of BOCWA and the\\n                     Director General in the specified Form XIV of BOCWR.\\n\\n\\n          14.3     Accident investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1   General\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1.1  Investigations  should be  conducted  in an open and  positive atmosphere  that\\n                 encourages the witnesses to talk freely. The primary objective is to ascertain the facts\\n                     with a view to prevent future and possibly more serious occurrences\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1.2  Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which result in death, serious injury or serious\\n               damage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find out the cause of the\\n                   accident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1.3  Near misses and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as\\n                 soon as possible as they are signals  that there are inadequacies  in the safety\\n                management system.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2   Procedure of incident investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2.1   It is important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to\\n                    the incident is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed;\\n\\n                     a)    take photographs and make sketches\\n\\n                     b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the environmental\\n                          conditions\\n\\n                      c)    interview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties\\n\\n                     d)    consult expert opinion where necessary\\n\\n                     e)    identify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2.2  Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident\\n\\n                     a)    establish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident\\n\\n                     b)    find out at what stage the accident took place\\n\\n                      c)    consider all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to\\n                         the accident, and identify the most probable cause The cause of an accident\\n                        should never be classified as carelessness. The specific act or omission that\\n                      caused the accident must be identified.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2.3  The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up action\\n\\n                     a)    report on the findings and conclusions\\n\\n                     b)    formulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence\\n\\n                      c)    publicise the findings and the remedial actions taken\\n\\n\\n          14.4     Employers’ independent incident investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.4.1    In case of fatal / dangerous occurrence the Employer shall also conduct independent\\n                      investigation. Contractor and his staff shall extend necessary co-operation and testify\\n                  about the accident.\\n\\n\\n          14.4.2   The contractor shall take every effort to preserve the scene of accident till the Employer\\n                  completes the investigation.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 30,\n      \"text\": \"14.4.3     All persons summoned by the Employer in connection to witness recording shall obey\\n          the instructions without delay. Any wilful suppression of information by any person shall\\n        be removed from the site immediately and  / or punishable as per relevant penalty\\n          clause.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          14.0     Accident reporting and investigation\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"          14.0     Accident reporting and investigation\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 61,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 62,\n      \"text\": \"          14.1     Reporting to Employer\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 63,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 64,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 65,\n      \"text\": \"          14.1.1    All accidents and dangerous occurrences  shall immediately be informed\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"source_line_number\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"                   verbally to the Employer. 37,\n      \"text\": \"                    the incident is gathered in an organised way. \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 41,\n      \"text\": \"                     b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 51,\n      \"text\": \"          14.3.2.2  Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 53,\n      \"text\": \"                     a)    establish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"source_line_number\": 54,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n classified as carelessness.     quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 22,\n  \"review_status\": \"pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n                                                          206\\n           v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances, equipment and\\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\\n\\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants, equipment, powered  tools and any other\\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators and workmen.\\n\\n\\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\\n\\n\\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections for ensuring an activity whether it\\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules; method statement submitted or\\n         developed procedures.\\n\\n\\n        The following are examples that will be commonly performed as required on the\\n          construction site:\\n\\n\\n                i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\\n\\n                  ii)    Inspection performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\\n\\n                  iii)    Inspection performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\\n\\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork before concreting by formwork erector.\\n\\n\\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor shall ensure that a\\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\\n\\n\\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\\n\\n         Other inspections include the following:\\n\\n                i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\\n\\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE management team\\n\\n\\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist for  all activity\\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian standards,\\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\\n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\\n\\n\\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection and Routine Inspection will be used\\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings.\\n\\n\\n11.0    SHE Audit\\n\\n\\n11.1     General\\n\\n\\n11.1.1   The purpose and scope of SHE audit is to assess potential risk, liabilities and the\\n         degree of compliance of construction Safety, Health and Environmental plan and its\\n         supplementary  procedures and programs  against  applicable and  current SHE\\n           legalisation regulations and requirements of the employer.\\n\\n\\n11.1.2    Project Manager holds the ultimate responsibility in ensuring implementation of SHE\\n          audit program during the construction work.\\n\\n\\n11.2     Monthly Audit Rating Score (M A R S)\\n\\n\\n11.2.1   Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) will be performed once in a month.
