Contractor shall make the below listed documents available for the review by\\n                  the Audit team.\\n\\n\\n                                 i)   SHE policy\\n\\n                                    ii)   SHE manual\\n\\n                                     iii)   SHE Rules and Regulation\\n\\n                          iv)  SHE organization chart\\n\\n                      v)    Annual SHE objectives / programs\\n\\n                          vi)   Accident / near miss statistics and analysis\\n\\n                             vii)  SHE Training program / records for all personnel\\n\\n                               viii)  Operating manuals and maintenance manual of all equipments\\n\\n                          ix)   Safe worthiness certificates of all lifting appliances and gears\\n\\n                      x)    Medical fitness record for all personnel\\n\\n                          xi)   Risk identification, assessment and control details\\n\\n                             xii)   Environmental management reports\\n\\n                               xiii)  Emergency management records including mock drill\\n\\n\\n          11.4.6    Audit Preparation:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Audit team members are required to gather information by observations through\\n                           interviews and by checks of hardware and documentation.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Audit team shall prepare checklist to cover all parts based on SHE legislations\\n                           rules and regulations and BMRC requirements.\\n\\n                                     iii)    Audit team members shall verify the facts and findings leading to the identified\\n                      gaps and weakness.\\n\\n                          iv)    Audit leader has overall responsibility for reaching a conclusion.\\n\\n\\n          11.4.7    Reporting:\\n\\n\\n          11.4.7.1  Audit report shall be prepared and directly sent to the Employer within 7 days of\\n                   conducting the audit with a copy to the contractor.\\n\\n\\n          11.4.8   Report contents:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    Executing summary - based on the finalized checklists as written the findings to\\n                          the Employer by the audit team members, the audit leader  will compile a\\n                        concise and accurate summary of observations and findings.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Introduction  -  this  will contain basic information     quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 29,\n  \"review_status\": \"pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n213\\n                 such appliances, gear, hoist, machinery or equipment and the site of such occurrence\\n                       shall, as far as practicable, be kept undisturbed until inspected by the Authorities;\\n\\n\\n          14.2.7   Every notice given for fatal accidents or dangerous occurrences shall be followed by a\\n                      written report to the concerned Authorities under Section 39 of BOCWA and the\\n                     Director General in the specified Form XIV of BOCWR.\\n\\n\\n          14.3     Accident investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1   General\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1.1  Investigations  should be  conducted  in an open and  positive atmosphere  that\\n                 encourages the witnesses to talk freely. The primary objective is to ascertain the facts\\n                     with a view to prevent future and possibly more serious occurrences\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1.2  Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which result in death, serious injury or serious\\n               damage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find out the cause of the\\n                   accident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.1.3  Near misses and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as\\n                 soon as possible as they are signals  that there are inadequacies  in the safety\\n                management system.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2   Procedure of incident investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2.1   It is important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to\\n                    the incident is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed;\\n\\n                     a)    take photographs and make sketches\\n\\n                     b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the environmental\\n                          conditions\\n\\n                      c)    interview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties\\n\\n                     d)    consult expert opinion where necessary\\n\\n                     e)    identify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2.2  Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident\\n\\n                     a)    establish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident\\n\\n                     b)    find out at what stage the accident took place\\n\\n                      c)    consider all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to\\n                         the accident, and identify the most probable cause The cause of an accident\\n                        should never be classified as carelessness. The specific act or omission that\\n                      caused the accident must be identified.\\n\\n\\n          14.3.2.3  The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up action\\n\\n                     a)    report on the findings and conclusions\\n\\n                     b)    formulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence\\n\\n                      c)    publicise the findings and the remedial actions taken\\n\\n\\n          14.4     Employers’ independent incident investigation\\n\\n\\n          14.4.1    In case of fatal / dangerous occurrence the Employer shall also conduct independent\\n                      investigation. Contractor and his staff shall extend necessary co-operation and testify\\n                  about the accident.\\n\\n\\n          14.4.2   The contractor shall take every effort to preserve the scene of accident till the Employer\\n                  completes the investigation.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. The primary objective is to ascertain the facts \\nwith a view to prevent future and possibly more serious occurrences \\n \\n14.3.1.2 Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which result in death, serious injury or serious \\ndamage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find out the cause of the \\naccident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence. \\n \\n14.3.1.3 Near misses and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as \\nsoon as possible as they are signals that there are inadequacies in the safety \\nmanagement system. \\n \\n14.3.2 \\nProcedure of incident investigation \\n \\n14.3.2.1 It is important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to \\nthe incident is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed; \\na) \\ntake photographs and make sketches \\nb) \\nexamine involved equipment, workplace or material and the environmental \\nconditions \\nc) \\ninterview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties \\nd) \\nconsult expert opinion where necessary \\ne) \\nidentify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved. \\n \\n14.3.2.2 Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident \\na) \\nestablish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident  \\nb) \\nfind out at what stage the accident took place \\nc) \\nconsider all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to \\nthe accident, and identify the most probable cause The cause of an accident \\nshould never be classified as carelessness. The specific act or omission that \\ncaused the accident must be identified. \\n \\n14.3.2.3 The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up action \\na) \\nreport on the findings and conclusions \\nb) \\nformulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence \\nc) \\npublicise the findings and the remedial actions taken \\n \\n14.4 \\nEmployers’ independent incident investigation \\n \\n14.4.1 \\nIn case of fatal / dangerous occurrence the Employer shall also conduct independent \\ninvestigation. Contractor and his staff shall extend necessary co-operation and testify \\nabout the accident. \\n \\n14.4.2 \\nThe contractor shall take every effort to preserve the scene of accident till the Employer \\ncompletes the investigation. \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        39.599998474121094,\n        24.479991912841797,\n        63.57600021362305,\n        41.38799285888672\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"213\\n\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"

or\\n\\n          b)    disables a worker from working for a period of 48 hours or more immediately\\n                 following the accident;\\n\\n           c)     shall forthwith be sent by telegram, telephone, fax, or similar other means\\n                including special messenger within four hours in case of fatal accidents and 72\\n              hours in case of other accidents, to:\\n\\n                          i)     the Regional Labour Commissioner, wherein the contractor has registered\\n                     the firm/work\\n\\n                            ii)    the board with which the worker involved was registered as a beneficiary;\\n\\n                             iii)    Director General and\\n\\n                     iv)    the next of kin or other relative of the worker involved in the accident;\\n\\n\\n14.2.2    Further, notice of accident shall be sent in respect of an accident which\\n\\n\\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\\n\\n          b)    disables the injured worker from work for more than 10 days to\\n\\n                          i)     the officer-in-charge of the nearest police station;\\n\\n                            ii)    the District Magistrate or, if the District Magistrate by order so desires, to\\n\\n                             iii)    the Sub-Divisional Magistrate\\n\\n\\n14.2.3    In case of an accident causing minor injury, first-aid shall be administered and the\\n           injured worker shall be immediately transferred to a hospital or other place for medical\\n          treatment.\\n\\n14.2.4   Where any accident causing disablement that subsequently results in death, notice in\\n           writing of such death, shall be sent to the authorities mentioned in clause 14.2.1 and\\n          14.2.2 above within 72 hours of such death.\\n\\n\\n14.2.5    Reporting of dangerous occurrences:\\n\\n\\n14.2.5.1  The following classes of dangerous occurrences shall be reported to the Inspector\\n         having jurisdiction, whether or not any disablement or death caused to the worker,\\n         namely:\\n\\n\\n          a)    collapse or  failure  of  lifting appliances,  or  hoist,  or conveyors, or  similar\\n              equipment for handling of building or construction material or breakage or failure\\n                 of rope, chain or loose gears; or overturning of cranes used in construction\\n               work;\\n\\n          b)     falling of objects from height;\\n\\n           c)    collapse or subsidence of soil, tunnel, pipe lines, any wall, floor, gallery, roof or\\n             any other part of any structure, launching girder, platform, staging, scaffolding or\\n            means of access including formwork;\\n\\n          d)    explosion of receiver or vessel used  for storage of pressure greater than\\n               atmospheric pressure, of any gas or gases or any liquid or solid used as\\n                 building material;\\n\\n          e)     fire and explosion causing damage to any place on construction site where\\n                 building workers are employed;\\n\\n               f)     spillage or leakage of any hazardous substance and damage to their container;\\n\\n          g)    collapse, capsizing, toppling or collision of transport equipment;\\n\\n          h)    leakage or release of harmful toxic gases at the construction site;\\n\\n\\n14.2.6    In case of failure of launching girder, lifting appliance, loose gear, hoist or building and\\n          other construction work, machinery and transport equipment at a construction site,\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. \\n \\n14.2.6 \\nIn case of failure of launching girder, lifting appliance, loose gear, hoist or building and \\nother construction work, machinery and transport equipment at a construction site, \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        546.0439453125,\n        24.479991912841797,\n        570.0199584960938,\n        41.38799285888672\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 7,\n      \"text\": \"212\\n\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 48,\n  \"text\": \"26.7      Electrical protection circuits\\n\\n26.7.1    Precautions shall be taken, either by earthing or by other suitable means, to prevent\\n         danger arising when any conductor (other than a  circuit conductor) which may\\n         reasonably foreseeable become charged as a result of either the use of a system, or a\\n            fault in a system, becomes so charged. A conductor shall be regarded as earthed\\n        when conductors of sufficient strength and current-carrying capability to discharge\\n           electrical energy to earth connect it to the general mass of earth.\\n\\n                If a circuit conductor is connected to earth or to any other reference point, nothing\\n         which might reasonably be expected to give rise to danger by breaking the electrical\\n           continuity or introducing high impedance shall be placed in that conductor unless\\n          suitable precautions are taken to prevent that danger.\\n\\n\\n26.7.2    Appropriate electrical protection shall be provided for all circuits, against over load,\\n          short circuit and earth fault current.\\n\\n\\n26.7.3   The contractor shall provide sufficient ELCBs (maintain sensitivity 30 mA) / RCCBs for\\n              all the equipments (including Potable equipments), electrical switchboards, distribution\\n         panels etc. to prevent electrical shocks to the workers.\\n\\n\\n26.7.4     All protection devices shall be capable of interrupting the circuit without damage to any\\n         equipments and circuits in case of any fault may occur.\\n\\n\\n26.7.5    Rating of fuses and circuit breakers used for the protection of circuits should be\\n          coordinate with equipment power ratings.\\n\\n\\n26.7.6    Protection against lightning shall be ensured to all equipment kept in open at sites.\\n\\n\\n26.8     Cables:\\n\\n\\n26.8.1   Cables shall be selected after full consideration of the condition to which they shall be\\n        exposed and the duties for which they are required. Supply cable up to 3.3 kV shall be\\n            in accordance with BS 6346.\\n\\n\\n26.8.2   For supplies to mobile or transportable equipment where operating of the equipment\\n          subjects the cable to flexing, the cable shall conform to any of these codes BS 6007 /\\n       BS 6500 / BS 7375.\\n\\n\\n26.8.3    Flexible cords with a conductor cross sectional area smaller than 1.5 mm2 shall not be\\n        used and insulated flexible cable shall conform to BS 6500 and BS 7375.\\n\\n\\n26.8.4   Where low voltage cables are to be used, reference shall be made to BS 7375. The\\n          following standards shall also be referred to particularly for under ground cables BS\\n        6346 and BS 6708\\n\\n\\n26.8.5   Cables buried directly in the ground shall be of a type incorporating armour or metal\\n         sheath or both. Such cables shall be marked by cable covers or a suitable marking\\n         tape and be buried at a  sufficient depth to avoid  their being damaged by any\\n          disturbance of the ground. Cable routes shall be marked on the plans kept in the site\\n           electrical register.\\n\\n26.8.6    Cabling passing under the walk way and across way  for transport and mobile\\n         equipment shall be laid in ducts at a minimum depth of 0.6 meters.\\n\\n26.8.7   Cables that need to cross open areas, or where span of 3m or more are involved, a\\n         catenary wire on poles or other supports shall be provided for convenient means of\\n         suspension. Minimum height shall be 6 m above ground.\\n\\n\\n26.8.8   Cables carrying a voltage to earth in excess of 65V other than supply for welding\\n         process shall have metal armour or sheath, which has been effectively earthed and\\n         monitored by the contractor. In case of flexible and trailing cables such earthed metal\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"23.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"text\": \"23.0     Construction machinery\\n\\n\\n          23.1     Construction machineries may include dumpers and dump trucks,  lift trucks and\\n                     telescopic handlers piling rigs, vibro hammers, rail welding equipments, mobile\\n                    elevating work platforms, cranes, tipper lorries, lorry loaders, skip wagons, 360°\\n                    excavators, 180° backhoe loaders, crawler tractors, scrapers, graders, loading\\n                    shovels,  trenchers,  side  booms,  pavers,  planers,  chippers,  road  rollers,\\n                    locomotives, tankers and bowsers, trailers, hydraulic and mechanical breakers\\n                       etc.\\n\\n\\n          23.2     Safe worthiness certificate\\n\\n\\n          23.2.1   Every construction equipment shall be in sound mechanical working condition and\\n                       certified by  either competent person under Factories Act  or manufacturers’\\n                   warranty in case of brand new equipments or authorized persons / firms approved\\n                 by Employer before induction to any site.\\n\\n\\n          23.2.2   Every such  certificate  shall have  the  date  of  purchase, main  overhauling\\n                  undertaken in the past, any accident to the equipment, visual examination details,\\n                          critical components safety check, list of safety devises and its working condition,\\n                   manufacturer’s maintenance checklist, past projects wherein the equipments were\\n                 used etc as its minimum content.\\n\\n\\n          23.3     Reverse Horns\\n\\n\\n          23.3.1    All Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse alarms and maintained in\\n               good working condition. Reversing  shall be done only when there  is\\n                 adequate rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman\\n\\n\\n          23.4     General operating procedures\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Drivers entering site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on\\n                                site. These shall be verbal instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing\\n                          the relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc.\\n\\n                                    ii)   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided  in\\n                       accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations.\\n\\n                                     iii)   Working on gradients beyond any equipments capability shall not be allowed.\\n\\n                          iv)   Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed by providing\\n                       wheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits,\\n                             etc.\\n\\n                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded in excavators.\\n\\n                          vi)      If excavators operating on a gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be ensured\\n                            that the working cycle is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far in the\\n                          downhill direction, and that travel  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large\\n                         excavator must never be permitted to travel in a confined area, or around people,\\n                          without a banksman to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment\\n                         close in to the machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled\\n                         excavators, it is essential that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated.\\n                                           If stabilizing devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is\\n                          excavating.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"text\": \"vii)  When the front shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe\\n               attachment shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking device in place.\\n\\n               viii)  When operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink\\n                  into the surface of the ground, reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be\\n           made for the stability of the machine. The loading shovel should always be lowered\\n                 to the ground to stabilise the machine when the backhoe is employed.\\n\\n             ix)   The netting operation of the skip wagons should be carried out prior to lifting the\\n                skip to reduce the risks of working on the rear platform\\n\\n           x)       If a tractor dozer is employed on clearing scrub or felling trees, it shall be provided\\n                with adequate driver protection.\\n\\n             xi)   When two or more scrapers are working on the same job, a minimum distance of at\\n                 least 25m shall be kept between them.\\n\\n              xii)   Incase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses shall be in good working\\n                condition\\n\\n\\n23.5       All wood working machines shall be fitted with suitable guards and devices such as top\\n          guard, riving knife, push stick, guards for drive belts and chains, and emergency stop\\n          switch easily accessible by the operator.\\n\\n\\n23.6     Penalty\\n\\n\\n23.6.1      If any of the above clauses are not adhered, penalty shall be imposed as per\\n         relevant clause depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          23.0     Construction machinery\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n     quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 47,\n  \"text\": \"26.2.1   The contractor shall assess the size and location of the electrical loads and the\\n                manner in which they vary with time during the currency of the contract.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.2   The contractor shall elaborate as to how the total supply is to be obtained  /\\n                   generated. The  details  of  the  source  of  electricity,  earthing  requirement,\\n                    substation  / panel boards, distribution system shall be prepared and necessary\\n                   approval from Employer obtained before proceeding of the execution of the job.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.3   The main contractor shall take consideration, the requirements of the sub /\\n                   petty contractors’ electric power supply and arrive at the capacity of main\\n                 source of power supply from diesel generators.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.4   As the sub / petty contractors’ small capacity generators create more noise\\n               and safety hazard, no small capacity diesel generators shall be allowed for\\n                 whatsoever the type of job to be executed under this contract.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.5      If any unsafe noise making small capacity diesel generators are found used\\n                by sub / petty contractors the main contractor shall only be penalised.\\n\\n\\n          26.3    Work on site\\n\\n\\n          26.3.1   The contractor shall also submit electrical single line diagram, schematic\\n                diagram and the  details of the equipment  for  all temporary  electrical\\n                     installation and these diagrams together with the temporary  electrical\\n                equipment shall be submitted to the Employer’s for necessary approval.\\n                   Failure to do so shall invite penalty as per relevant clause.\\n\\n\\n          26.4     Strength and capability of electrical equipment\\n\\n\\n          26.4.1   No electrical equipment shall be put into use where its strength and capability may\\n                be exceeded in such a way as may give rise to danger.\\n\\n\\n          26.5     Adverse or hazardous environments\\n\\n          26.5.1    Electrical equipment, which may reasonably foreseably be exposed to-\\n\\n                      (a)   mechanical damage;\\n                      (b)   the effects of the weather, natural hazards, temperature or pressure;\\n                       (c)   the effects of wet, dirty, dusty or corrosive conditions; or\\n                      (d)   any flammable or explosive substance, including dusts, vapours or gases,\\n                             shall be of such construction or as necessary protected as to prevent, so far\\n                      as is reasonably practicable, danger arising from such exposure.\\n\\n\\n\\n          26.6      Distribution system:\\n\\n\\n          26.6.1   The contractor shall provide distribution system for control and distribution of\\n                        electricity from a main AC supply of 50Hz for typical appliances,\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    Fixed plant – 400V 3 phase\\n\\n                                    ii)    Movable plant fed via trailing cable over 3.75 kW – 400 3 phase\\n\\n                                     iii)    Installation in site buildings – 230V single phase\\n\\n                          iv)   Fixed flood lighting – 230V single phase\\n\\n                      v)    Portable and hand tools – 115V single phase\\n\\n                          vi)    Site lighting  - 115V single phase\\n\\n                             vii)   Portable hand lamps – 115V single phase\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"23.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"text\": \"23.0     Construction machinery\\n\\n\\n          23.1     Construction machineries may include dumpers and dump trucks,  lift trucks and\\n                     telescopic handlers piling rigs, vibro hammers, rail welding equipments, mobile\\n                    elevating work platforms, cranes, tipper lorries, lorry loaders, skip wagons, 360°\\n                    excavators, 180° backhoe loaders, crawler tractors, scrapers, graders, loading\\n                    shovels,  trenchers,  side  booms,  pavers,  planers,  chippers,  road  rollers,\\n                    locomotives, tankers and bowsers, trailers, hydraulic and mechanical breakers\\n                       etc.\\n\\n\\n          23.2     Safe worthiness certificate\\n\\n\\n          23.2.1   Every construction equipment shall be in sound mechanical working condition and\\n                       certified by  either competent person under Factories Act  or manufacturers’\\n                   warranty in case of brand new equipments or authorized persons / firms approved\\n                 by Employer before induction to any site.\\n\\n\\n          23.2.2   Every such  certificate  shall have  the  date  of  purchase, main  overhauling\\n                  undertaken in the past, any accident to the equipment, visual examination details,\\n                          critical components safety check, list of safety devises and its working condition,\\n                   manufacturer’s maintenance checklist, past projects wherein the equipments were\\n                 used etc as its minimum content.\\n\\n\\n          23.3     Reverse Horns\\n\\n\\n          23.3.1    All Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse alarms and maintained in\\n               good working condition. Reversing  shall be done only when there  is\\n                 adequate rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman\\n\\n\\n          23.4     General operating procedures\\n\\n\\n                                 i)     Drivers entering site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on\\n                                site. These shall be verbal instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing\\n                          the relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc.\\n\\n                                    ii)   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided  in\\n                       accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations.\\n\\n                                     iii)   Working on gradients beyond any equipments capability shall not be allowed.\\n\\n                          iv)   Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed by providing\\n                       wheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits,\\n                             etc.\\n\\n                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded in excavators.\\n\\n                          vi)      If excavators operating on a gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be ensured\\n                            that the working cycle is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far in the\\n                          downhill direction, and that travel  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large\\n                         excavator must never be permitted to travel in a confined area, or around people,\\n                          without a banksman to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment\\n                         close in to the machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled\\n                         excavators, it is essential that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated.\\n                                           If stabilizing devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is\\n                          excavating.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"text\": \"vii)  When the front shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe\\n               attachment shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking device in place.\\n\\n               viii)  When operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink\\n                  into the surface of the ground, reducing stability.          manufacturer’s maintenance checklist, past projects wherein the equipments were\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 39,\n      \"text\": \"                 used etc as its minimum content.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 40,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 41,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 42,\n      \"text\": \"          23.3     Reverse Horns\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 43,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 44,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 45,\n      \"text\": \"          23.3.1    All Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse alarms and maintained in\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 46,\n      \"text\": \"               good working condition. Reversing  shall be done only when there  is\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 47,\n      \"text\": \"                 adequate rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 48,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 49,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 50,\n      \"text\": \"          23.4     General operating procedures\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 51,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 52,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 53,\n      \"text\": \"                                 i)     Drivers entering site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 54,\n      \"text\": \"                                site. These shall be verbal instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 55,\n      \"text\": \"                          the relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 56,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 57,\n      \"text\": \"                                    ii)   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided  in\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 58,\n      \"text\": \"                       accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"                                     iii)   Working on gradients beyond any equipments capability shall not be allowed.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 61,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 62,\n      \"text\": \"                          iv)   Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed by providing\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 63,\n      \"text\": \"                       wheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits,\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 64,\n      \"text\": \"                             etc.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 65,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded in excavators.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 67,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 68,\n      \"text\": \"                          vi)      If excavators operating on a gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be ensured\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 69,\n      \"text\": \"                            that the working cycle is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far in the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 70,\n      \"text\": \"                          downhill direction, and that travel  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 71,\n      \"text\": \"                         excavator must never be permitted to travel in a confined area, or around people,\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 72,\n      \"text\": \"                          without a banksman to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 73,\n      \"text\": \"                         close in to the machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 74,\n      \"text\": \"                         excavators, it is essential that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 75,\n      \"text\": \"                                           If stabilizing devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 76,\n      \"text\": \"                          excavating.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 77,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 78,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 79,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 45,\n      \"source_line_number\": 80,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"              vii)  When the front shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"               attachment shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking device in place.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 5,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 6,\n      \"text\": \"               viii)  When operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 7,\n      \"text\": \"                  into the surface of the ground, reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 8,\n      \"text\": \"           made for the stability of the machine. The loading shovel should always be lowered\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 9,\n      \"text\": \"                 to the ground to stabilise the machine when the backhoe is employed.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 10,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 11,\n      \"text\": \"             ix)   The netting operation of the skip wagons should be carried out prior to lifting the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 12,\n      \"text\": \"                skip to reduce the risks of working on the rear platform\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"           x)       If a tractor dozer is employed on clearing scrub or felling trees, it shall be provided\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 15,\n      \"text\": \"                with adequate driver protection.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"             xi)   When two or more scrapers are working on the same job, a minimum distance of at\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"                 least 25m shall be kept between them.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 20,\n      \"text\": \"              xii)   Incase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses shall be in good working\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 21,\n      \"text\": \"                condition\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 46,\n      \"source_line_number\": 23,\n      \"text\":     quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 49,\n  \"text\": \"sheath and/or armour should be in addition to the earth core in the cable and shall not\\n                be used as the protective conductor.\\n\\n\\n          26.8.9   Armoured cables having an over-sheath of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) or an  oil\\n                      resisting and flame retardant compound shall be used whenever there is a risk of\\n                  mechanical damage occurring\\n\\n\\n          26.9     Plugs, socket-outlets and couplers:\\n\\n\\n          26.9.1   The contractor shall ensure plugs, socket-outlets, and couplers available in\\n                  the construction  site as “splash proof” type. The minimum degree of\\n                  Ingress Protection should be of IP44 in accordance with BS EN 60529.\\n\\n\\n          26.9.2   Only plugs and fittings of the weatherproof type shall be used and they should be colour\\n                 coded in accordance with the Internationally recognised standards for example as detailed\\n                 as follows:\\n\\n                      (a)   110 volts : Yellow.\\n\\n                      (b)   240 volts : Blue.\\n\\n                       (c)   415 volts : Red.\\n\\n         26.10    Connections\\n\\n          26.10.1  Every joint and connection in a system shall be mechanically and electrically\\n                   suitable  for  use  to  prevent  danger.  Proper  cable  connectors  as  per\\n                    national/international standards shall only be used to connect cables.\\n\\n          26.10.2  No loose connections or tapped joints shall be allowed any where in the work\\n                       site, office area, stores and other areas. Penalty as per relevant clause shall be\\n                  put in case of observation of any tapped joints.\\n\\n\\n         26.11    Portable and hand-held equipments:\\n\\n\\n          26.11.1  The contractor shall ensure the use of double insulated or all-insulated portable\\n                       electrical hand equipment may be used without earthing (i.e. two core cables), but\\n                   they shall still be used only on 110V because of the risk of damage to trailing leads.\\n\\n\\n         26.12    Other equipments:\\n\\n\\n          26.12.1   All equipment shall have the provision for major switch/cut-off switch in the equipment\\n                           itself.\\n\\n\\n          26.12.2   All non-current carrying metal parts of electrical equipment shall be earthed through\\n                    insulated cable\\n\\n\\n          26.12.3   Isolate exposed high-voltage (over 415 Volts) equipment, such as transformer banks,\\n                open switches, and similar equipment with exposed energized parts and prevent\\n                   unauthorised access.\\n\\n\\n          26.12.4  Approved perimeter markings shall be used to isolate restricted areas from designated\\n                 work areas and entryways and shall be erected before work begins and maintained for\\n                      entire duration of work. Approved perimeter marking shall be installed  with either red\\n                      barrier tape printed with the words \\\"DANGER—HIGH VOLTAGE\\\" or a barrier of yellow\\n                     or orange synthetic rope, approximately 1 to 1.5 meter above the floor or work\\n                    surface.\\n\\n\\n         26.13   Work on or near live conductors\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 47,\n  \"text\": \"26.2.1   The contractor shall assess the size and location of the electrical loads and the\\n                manner in which they vary with time during the currency of the contract.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.2   The contractor shall elaborate as to how the total supply is to be obtained  /\\n                   generated. The  details  of  the  source  of  electricity,  earthing  requirement,\\n                    substation  / panel boards, distribution system shall be prepared and necessary\\n                   approval from Employer obtained before proceeding of the execution of the job.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.3   The main contractor shall take consideration, the requirements of the sub /\\n                   petty contractors’ electric power supply and arrive at the capacity of main\\n                 source of power supply from diesel generators.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.4   As the sub / petty contractors’ small capacity generators create more noise\\n               and safety hazard, no small capacity diesel generators shall be allowed for\\n                 whatsoever the type of job to be executed under this contract.\\n\\n\\n          26.2.5      If any unsafe noise making small capacity diesel generators are found used\\n                by sub / petty contractors the main contractor shall only be penalised.\\n\\n\\n          26.3    Work on site\\n\\n\\n          26.3.1   The contractor shall also submit electrical single line diagram, schematic\\n                diagram and the  details of the equipment  for  all temporary  electrical\\n                     installation and these diagrams together with the temporary  electrical\\n                equipment shall be submitted to the Employer’s for necessary approval.\\n                   Failure to do so shall invite penalty as per relevant clause.\\n\\n\\n          26.4     Strength and capability of electrical equipment\\n\\n\\n          26.4.1   No electrical equipment shall be put into use where its strength and capability may\\n                be exceeded in such a way as may give rise to danger.\\n\\n\\n          26.5     Adverse or hazardous environments\\n\\n          26.5.1    Electrical equipment, which may reasonably foreseably be exposed to-\\n\\n                      (a)   mechanical damage;\\n                      (b)   the effects of the weather, natural hazards, temperature or pressure;\\n                       (c)   the effects of wet, dirty, dusty or corrosive conditions; or\\n                      (d)   any flammable or explosive substance, including dusts, vapours or gases,\\n                             shall be of such construction or as necessary protected as to prevent, so far\\n                      as is reasonably practicable, danger arising from such exposure.\\n\\n\\n\\n          26.6      Distribution system:\\n\\n\\n          26.6.1   The contractor shall provide distribution system for control and distribution of\\n                        electricity from a main AC supply of 50Hz for typical appliances,\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    Fixed plant – 400V 3 phase\\n\\n                                    ii)    Movable plant fed via trailing cable over 3.75 kW – 400 3 phase\\n\\n                                     iii)    Installation in site buildings – 230V single phase\\n\\n                          iv)   Fixed flood lighting – 230V single phase\\n\\n                      v)    Portable and hand tools – 115V single phase\\n\\n                          vi)    Site lighting  - 115V single phase\\n\\n                             vii)   Portable hand lamps – 115V single phase\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"38.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"text\": \"38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    The batching plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of\\n                         unloading and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\\n                             plant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\\n                          loading the segments to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be\\n                         avoided.\\n\\n                                    ii)   The batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a compulsory\\n                  PPE zone\\n\\n                                     iii)      If in case of material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same\\n                             shall be segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate\\n                            barrications.\\n\\n                          iv)    Electrical system  shall also be suitably planned so that location  of diesel\\n                          generator,  if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning of area\\n                              lighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and pose danger.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"v)    Drainage shall be effectively provided and waste water shall be disposed after\\n               proper treatment\\n\\n             vi)   Time office, canteen, drinking water,  toilet and rest place shall be suitably\\n                located  for the easy access to workers.  All the  facilities shall be properly\\n              cleaned and maintained during the entire period of operation.\\n\\n              vii)   Manual handling of cement shall be avoided to a larger extent. Whenever  it is\\n                absolutely necessary the workmen shall be given  full body protection, hand\\n                protection and respiratory protection as a basic measure of ensuring better\\n                 health.\\n\\n               viii)  The PPEs provided to cement handling workmen shall conform to international\\n               standards.\\n\\n             ix)   Access roads and internal circulation roads shall be well laid and maintained\\n                properly at all time.\\n\\n           x)    Non-adherence to any of the above provision shall be penalised as per relevant\\n                penalty clause.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"          38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"source_line_number\": 60,\n      \"text\": \"          38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"source_line_number\": 61,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"source_line_number\": 62,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"source_line_number\": 63,\n      \"text\": \"                                 i)    The batching plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"source_line_number\": 64,\n      \"text\": \"                         unloading and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"source_line_number\": 65,\n      \"text\": \"                             plant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 59,\n      \"source_line_number\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"                          loading the segments to the trucks. and\\n\\n                  ii)     in the view of such Inspector, the lifting appliance, lifting gear or any other\\n                material  handling  appliance  is  not  safe  for use  in  building  or  other\\n                construction work; and\\n\\n                  iii)   no pulley block is used in building or other construction work unless the safe\\n               working load and its identification are clearly marked on such block.\\n\\n\\n21.9      Qualification of operator of lifting appliances and of signaller etc\\n\\n\\n21.9.1   The contractor shall not employ any person to drive or operate a lifting machine\\n            like crane, hydra etc whether driven by mechanical power or otherwise or to give\\n          signals to work as a operator of a rigger or derricks unless he\\n\\n                i)      is above twenty-one years of age and possesses a valid heavy transport\\n                vehicle driving licence as per Motor Vehicle Act and Rules.\\n\\n                  ii)     is absolutely competent and reliable\\n\\n                  iii)   possesses the knowledge of the inherent risks involved in the operation of\\n                      lifting appliances by undergoing a formal  training  at any  institution  of\\n                national importance acceptable to Employer\\n\\n             iv)     is medically examined periodically as specified in schedule VII of BOCW\\n               Rules.\\n\\n\\n21.10    General requirements of appliances\\n\\n\\n21.10.1   Out-of level\\n\\n\\n21.10.1.1 One of the most severe effects of being out-of fit level is that side loads develop in\\n          the boom. The fencing of dangerous part of machinery is not removed\\n          while such machinery is in motion or in use.\\n\\n\\n25.0    Manual lifting and carrying of excessive weight\\n\\n\\n25.1    The  contractor  shall ensure  at  his  construction  site  of a  building  or other\\n          construction work that no building worker lifts by hand or carries overhead or over\\n           his back or shoulders any material, article, tool or appliances exceeding in weight\\n         as said below as per Rule 38 of BOCWR, Unless aided by another building worker\\n          or device.\\n\\n                      Person      Maximum weight in\\n                                                 kg.\\n\\n                          Adult man             55\\n\\n                          Adult                 30\\n                  woman\\n\\n\\n25.2    No building worker aided by other building worker shall lift or carry weight higher\\n         than or exceeding the sum of total of maximum limits set out for each building\\n         worker separately as mentioned in the table above.\\n\\n\\n26.0      Site Electricity\\n\\n26.1     Competency of Electrical personnel:\\n\\n26.1.1   The contractor shall employ qualified and competent electrical personnel as\\n         specified in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001.\\n\\n\\n26.2     Assessment of power\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.     quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 44,\n  \"review_status\": \"pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n                                                          228\\n21.11.9  No close working to any  live overhead power  line  is permitted without the\\n         operation of a strict Permit to Work.\\n\\n\\n21.11.10 Minimum lighting is to be ensured at all lifting operations.\\n\\n\\n21.12    Failure to do any of the above shall attract penalty from the Employer as per\\n         relevant clause\\n\\n\\n22.0     Launching Operation\\n\\n22.1    As launching operation  is one of the  riskiest job, the contractor shall take utmost\\n          precaution  at  all stages  like; planning, establishing casing yard, casting segments,\\n          transporting segments,  fabrication and  erection  of launching  girders, launching  of\\n         segments, pre-stressing, auto launching of girders and dismantling of launching girders.\\n\\n\\n22.2    The contractor shall prepare a comprehensive Method Statement  for the launching\\n          operation, adhering to the SHE conditions laid down in conditions of contract on SHE and\\n          project SHE manual. Particular reference shall be made to the provisions on working at\\n           height. As the entire process of launching has to be undertaken at an elevated level, the\\n          safety of workers and the girder is paramount important. The following general guidelines\\n           shall be adhered throughout the launching operation.\\n\\n\\n                i)    Necessary ‘working platforms’ and fall protection anchorage arrangement shall be\\n               provided in the launching girder itself.\\n\\n                  ii)    Provisions for mounting light fittings shall also be made available in the launching\\n                  girder.\\n\\n                  iii)   The casting yard shall be established ensuring the provision given in clause 38.0\\n\\n             iv)   The workmen engaged in fabrication of reinforcement, concreting the segment\\n                  shall be provided with necessary PPEs including compulsory hand protection\\n                gloves.\\n\\n           v)    Casting and curing of segment shall be undertaken under the direct supervision of\\n                the responsible engineer of the contractor.\\n\\n             vi)   Trucks  with  valid  registration,  licence, safe worthiness  certificate, Employer’s\\n               approval certificate, and pollution under check certificate shall only be used for\\n                transport of segments\\n\\n              vii)   Drivers engaged for driving these trucks, shall be trained once in 6 months at\\n                specified locations as directed by the employer on defensive driving.\\n\\n               viii)   Drivers shall also have undergone proper medical examination as per relevant\\n               clause mentioned under ‘Medical Facilities’.\\n\\n             ix)   The segments shall rigidly secured to the truck with necessary wooden wedges\\n             and necessary red indicators/safety tapes provided so that the vehicle is clearly\\n             seen by other road users both in day / night time.\\n\\n           x)    Every launching girder shall have a responsible engineer on duty all the time.\\n\\n             xi)    All the time from erection to dismantling the area between the two piers\\n              wherein launching is in progress shall always be barricaded.\\n\\n              xii)   Unloading  of  segments  from  trucks,  lifting  of  segments,  shifting  of\\n              segments, gluing shall be done under the direct supervision of the approved\\n               engineer of the contractor.\\n\\n               xiii)  Auto launching shall be done only after approval from the Employer. After\\n               every auto launching the stability of launching girder shall be ensured.\\n\\n            xiv)  The vertical deflection of launching girder shall be monitored at all critical\\n               stages like with/without loads and after every auto launching.\\n\\n          xv)  A  register containing  all important operational  details from erection  to\\n                dismantling of launching girders shall be maintained and made available to\\n              Employer whenever called for.\\n\\n            xvi)  Test  certificate  for  all  lifting  gears  including  Macalloy  bars  shall be\\n               maintained at a location closer to the launching girder itself so that it can be\\n                referred during all inspections.\\n\\n             xvii)  Adequate lighting at all time shall be ensured in the entire area of operation.\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. Particular reference shall be made to the provisions on working at \\nheight.  As the entire process of launching has to be undertaken at an elevated level, the \\nsafety of workers and the girder is paramount important. The following general guidelines \\nshall be adhered throughout the launching operation.  \\n \\ni) \\nNecessary ‘working platforms’ and fall protection anchorage arrangement shall be \\nprovided in the launching girder itself. \\nii) \\nProvisions for mounting light fittings shall also be made available in the launching \\ngirder. \\niii) \\nThe casting yard shall be established ensuring the provision given in clause 38.0   \\niv) \\nThe workmen engaged in fabrication of reinforcement, concreting the segment \\nshall be provided with necessary PPEs including compulsory hand protection \\ngloves. \\nv) \\nCasting and curing of segment shall be undertaken under the direct supervision of \\nthe responsible engineer of the contractor. \\nvi) \\nTrucks with valid registration, licence, safe worthiness certificate, Employer’s \\napproval certificate, and pollution under check certificate shall only be used for \\ntransport of segments \\nvii) \\nDrivers engaged for driving these trucks, shall be trained once in 6 months at \\nspecified locations as directed by the employer on defensive driving.   \\nviii) \\nDrivers shall also have undergone proper medical examination as per relevant \\nclause mentioned under ‘Medical Facilities’. \\nix) \\nThe segments shall rigidly secured to the truck with necessary wooden wedges \\nand necessary red indicators/safety tapes provided so that the vehicle is clearly \\nseen by other road users both in day / night time.  \\nx) \\nEvery launching girder shall have a responsible engineer on duty all the time. \\nxi) \\nAll the time from erection to dismantling the area between the two piers \\nwherein launching is in progress shall always be barricaded. \\nxii) \\nUnloading of segments from trucks, lifting of segments, shifting of \\nsegments, gluing shall be done under the direct supervision of the approved \\nengineer of the contractor. \\nxiii) \\nAuto launching shall be done only after approval from the Employer. After \\nevery auto launching the stability of launching girder shall be ensured. \\nxiv) \\nThe vertical deflection of launching girder shall be monitored at all critical \\nstages like with/without loads and after every auto launching.  \\nxv) \\nA register containing all important operational details from erection to \\ndismantling of launching girders shall be maintained and made available to \\nEmployer whenever called for.  \\nxvi) \\nTest certificate for all lifting gears including Macalloy bars shall be \\nmaintained at a location closer to the launching girder itself so that it can be \\nreferred during all inspections. \\nxvii) Adequate lighting at all time shall be ensured in the entire area of operation. \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        546.0439453125,\n        24.479991912841797,\n        570.0199584960938,\n        41.38799285888672\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"228\\n\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"

An adequate water supply is provided at ample pressure as\\n         per national standard.\\n\\n\\n31.2     Recharging of fire extinguishers and their proper maintenance should be ensured and\\n         as a minimum should meet Indian National Standards\\n\\n\\n31.3       All drivers  of vehicles, foreman, supervisors and managers  shall be trained on\\n          operating the fire extinguishers and fire fighting equipment.\\n\\n31.4    The contractor shall also give consideration to the provision of adequate fire fighting\\n         arrangements within the underground and tunnelling operations including the provision\\n           of Fire Service compatible hose connections and emergency lighting\\n\\n\\n31.5    As per the BOCWK Rules 2006, Rule 79(a)(vii), all lifting appliances’ driver cabin\\n         should be provided with a suitable portable fire extinguisher.\\n\\n\\n31.6     Combustible scrap and other construction debris should be disposed off site on a\\n          regular basis. If scrap is to be burnt on site, the burning site should be specified and\\n          located at a distance no less than 12 metres from any construction work or any other\\n         combustible material.\\n\\n\\n31.7     Every fire, including those extinguished by contractor personnel, shall be reported to\\n          the Employer representatives.\\n\\n\\n31.8     Emergency plans and Fire Evacuation plans shall be prepared and issued. Mock drills\\n         should be held on a regular basis to ensure the effectiveness of the arrangements and\\n         as a part of the programme, the Telephone Number of the local fire brigade should be\\n          prominently displayed near each telephone on site.\\n\\n\\n32.0     Corrosive substances\\n\\n\\n32.1    As per BOCWR Rule 44, corrosive substances including alkalis and acids shall be\\n          stored and used by a person dealing with such substances at a building / construction\\n            site in a manner that it does not endanger the building worker and suitable PPE shall\\n        be provided by the contractor to the worker during such handling and work. In case of\\n           spillage of such substances on building worker, the contractor shall take immediate\\n         remedial measures.\\n\\n\\n33.0     Demolition\\n\\n33.1    The Contractor shall ensure that\\n\\n                i)       all  demolition  works be  carried  out  in a  controlled manner  under  the\\n            management of experienced and competent supervision.\\n\\n                  ii)    the concerned department of the Government or local authority be informed and\\n               permission obtained wherever required. Media shall also be informed regarding\\n                   this concern.\\n\\n\\n                  iii)     all glass or similar materials or articles in exterior openings are removed\\n              before commencing any demolition work and all water, steam, electric,\\n             gas and other similar supply lines are put-off and such lines so located or\\n            capped with substantial coverings so as to protect it from damage and to\\n               afford safety to the building workers and public..\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. September 2026         Section Page 50 of 114 \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        82.4399642944336,\n        37.989418029785156,\n        512.7689819335938,\n        616.491943359375\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"31.0 \\nFire prevention, protection and fighting system \\n \\n31.1  \\nThe contractor shall ensure that construction site is provided with fire \\nextinguishing equipment sufficient to extinguish any probable fire at \\nconstruction site. An adequate water supply is provided at ample pressure as \\nper national standard. \\n \\n31.2 \\nRecharging of fire extinguishers and their proper maintenance should be ensured and \\nas a minimum should meet Indian National Standards \\n \\n31.3  \\nAll drivers of vehicles, foreman, supervisors and managers shall be trained on \\noperating the fire extinguishers and fire fighting equipment.  \\n31.4 \\nThe contractor shall also give consideration to the provision of adequate fire fighting \\narrangements within the underground and tunnelling operations including the provision \\nof Fire Service compatible hose connections and emergency lighting \\n \\n31.5  \\nAs per the BOCWK Rules 2006, Rule 79(a)(vii), all lifting appliances’ driver cabin \\nshould be provided with a suitable portable fire extinguisher. \\n \\n31.6 \\nCombustible scrap and other construction debris should be disposed off site on a \\nregular basis. If scrap is to be burnt on site, the burning site should be specified and \\nlocated at a distance no less than 12 metres from any construction work or any other \\ncombustible material. \\n \\n31.7  \\nEvery fire, including those extinguished by contractor personnel, shall be reported to \\nthe Employer representatives. \\n \\n31.8 \\nEmergency plans and Fire Evacuation plans shall be prepared and issued. Mock drills \\nshould be held on a regular basis to ensure the effectiveness of the arrangements and \\nas a part of the programme, the Telephone Number of the local fire brigade should be \\nprominently displayed near each telephone on site. \\n \\n32.0 \\nCorrosive substances \\n \\n32.1 \\nAs per BOCWR Rule 44, corrosive substances including alkalis and acids shall be \\nstored and used by a person dealing with such substances at a building / construction \\nsite in a manner that it does not endanger the building worker and suitable PPE shall \\nbe provided by the contractor to the worker during such handling and work. In case of \\nspillage of such substances on building worker, the contractor shall take immediate \\nremedial measures. \\n \\n33.0 \\nDemolition \\n \\n33.1 \\nThe Contractor shall ensure that  \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        127.4414291381836,\n        618.5394897460938,\n        512.76953125,\n        771.8919067382812\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"i) \\nall demolition works be carried out in a controlled manner under the \\nmanagement of experienced and competent supervision. \\n \\nii) \\nthe concerned department of the Government or local authority be informed and \\npermission obtained wherever required. Media shall also be informed regarding \\nthis concern. \\n \\niii) \\nall glass or similar materials or articles in exterior openings are removed \\nbefore commencing any demolition work and all water, steam, electric, \\ngas and other similar supply lines are put-off and such lines so located or \\ncapped with substantial coverings so as to protect it from damage and to \\nafford safety to the building workers and public.. \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        546.0439453125,\n        24.479991912841797,\n        570.0199584960938,\n        41.38799285888672\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 5,\n      \"text\": \"238\\n\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"

It is essential, therefore, that\\n         they are used only after consulting the local police and traffic authorities.\\n\\n\\n36.8     Warning signs\\n\\n\\n36.8.1   Warning signs in the traffic control zone shall be utilised to warn the drivers of specific\\n         hazards that may be encountered.\\n\\n\\n36.8.2   The contractor shall place detour signage at strategic locations and install appropriate\\n         warning signs.  In order to minimize disruption of access to residences and business,\\n          the contractor shall maintain at least one entrance to a property where multiple\\n         entrances exist.\\n\\n\\n36.8.3   A warning sign as given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/012 shall be installed\\n        an at all secondary road which merges with the primary road where the construction\\n         work is in progress at sufficient distance before it merges with the primary road so as\\n           to alert the road users regarding the ‘Metro Work in Progress’.\\n\\n\\n36.8.4    Materials hanging over / protruded from the chassis / body of any vehicle especially\\n          during material handling shall be indicated by red indicator (red light/flag) to indicate\\n          the caution to the road users.\\n\\n\\n36.9      Delineators\\n\\n        The delineators are the elements of a total system of traffic control and have two\\n            distinct purposes:\\n\\n                i)    To delineate and guide the driver to and along a safe path\\n\\n                  ii)   As a taper to move traffic from one lane to another.\\n\\n\\n36.9.1   These channelizing devices such as cones, traffic cylinders, tapes and drums shall be\\n         placed in or adjacent to the roadway to control the flow of  traffic. These should\\n          normally be retro-reflectors complying to IRC: 79 - Recommended Practice for Road\\n          Delineators.\\n\\n\\n36.9.2    Traffic cones and cylinders\\n\\n\\n36.9.2.1  Traffic cones of 500mm, 750mm and 1000mm high and 300mm to 500mm in diameter\\n          or in square shape at base and are often made of plastic or rubber and normally have\\n           retro-reflectorised red and white band shall be used wherever required.\\n\\n36.9.3   Drums\\n\\n36.9.3.1  Drums about 800mm to 1000mm high and 300mm in diameter can be used either as\\n          channelising or warning devices. These are highly visible, give the appearance of\\n         being formidable objects and therefore command the respect of drivers.\\n\\n\\n36.9.4    Barricades\\n\\n\\n36.9.4.1  Full height fence, barriers, barricades etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\\n         prevent the working area from  the  risk  of  accidents due  to speedy  vehicular\\n        movement.     quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 60,\n  \"review_status\": \"pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n                                                          244\\n           v)    Drainage shall be effectively provided and waste water shall be disposed after\\n               proper treatment\\n\\n             vi)   Time office, canteen, drinking water,  toilet and rest place shall be suitably\\n                located  for the easy access to workers.  All the  facilities shall be properly\\n              cleaned and maintained during the entire period of operation.\\n\\n              vii)   Manual handling of cement shall be avoided to a larger extent. Whenever  it is\\n                absolutely necessary the workmen shall be given  full body protection, hand\\n                protection and respiratory protection as a basic measure of ensuring better\\n                 health.\\n\\n               viii)  The PPEs provided to cement handling workmen shall conform to international\\n               standards.\\n\\n             ix)   Access roads and internal circulation roads shall be well laid and maintained\\n                properly at all time.\\n\\n           x)    Non-adherence to any of the above provision shall be penalised as per relevant\\n                penalty clause.\\n\\n39.0     Personal Protective Equipments (PPEs)\\n\\n\\n39.1    The contractor shall provide required PPEs to workmen to protect against safety and /\\n          or health hazards. Primarily PPEs are required for the following protection\\n\\n\\n                i)    Head Protection (Safety helmets)\\n                  ii)    Foot Protection (Safety footwear, Gumboot, etc)\\n                  iii)   Body Protection (High visibility clothing (waistcoat/jacket), Apron, etc)\\n             iv)   Personal fall protection (Full body harness, Rope-grap fall arrester, etc)\\n           v)   Eye Protection (Goggles, Welders glasses, etc)\\n             vi)   Hand Protection (Gloves, Finger coats, etc)\\n              vii)   Respiratory Protection. (Nose mask, SCBAs, etc)\\n               viii)  Hearing Protection (Ear plugs, Ear muffs, etc)\\n\\n\\n39.2    The PPEs and safety appliances provided by the contractor shall be of the\\n         standard as prescribed by Bureau of Indian Standards  (BIS).  If materials\\n        conforming to BIS standards are not available, the contractor as approved by\\n         the Employer shall procure PPE and safety appliances.\\n\\n\\n39.3      All construction workers should be provided with high visibility jackets with\\n          reflective tapes confirming to the requirement specified under BS EN 471: 1994\\n        as most of viaduct /tunnelling/station and depot works are executed either\\n        above or under right-of-way.
