Conspicuity. shall be ensured by\\n                     affixing retro reflective stripes of required size and shape at appropriate angle at\\n                  the bottom and middle portion of the barricade at a minimum gap of 1000mm. In\\n                   addition minimum one red light or red light blinker should be placed at the top\\n                   of each barricade.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.5   The contractor shall ensure that all his construction vehicles plying on public roads\\n                         (like dump trucks, trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads from the\\n                    State Transport Authority. Drivers holding proper valid license as per the requirements\\n                      of Motor Vehicles Act shall drive these vehicles\\n\\n\\n          36.9.6   The contractor shall not undertake loading and unloading at carriageways obstructing\\n                    the free flow of vehicular traffic and encroachment of existing roads by the contractor\\n                    applying the excuse of work execution.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.7   Tow away vehicle\\n\\n\\n          36.9.7.1  The contractor shall make arrangements keeping tow away van / manpower to\\n                tow away any breakdown vehicle in the traffic flow without loosing any time at\\n                   his cost.\\n\\n          36.9.8   Cleaning of roads\\n\\n\\n          36.9.8.1  The contractor shall ensure the cleanliness of roads and footpaths by deploying\\n                 proper manpower for the same. The contractor shall have to ensure proper\\n                 brooming, cleaning washing of roads and footpaths on all the time throughout\\n                  the entire stretch till the currency of the contract including disposal of seepage.\\n\\n          37.0    Work to adjacent railways\\n\\n          37.1     Whenever work is to be conducted in close proximity to the live railways then the\\n                     following measures shall need to be addressed:\\n\\n                      (a)  The rules provided for in the Railway’s manual should be followed.\\n\\n                      (b)  No persons are allowed to encroach onto the railway unless the owner has\\n                         given specific authority.\\n\\n                       (c)   Adequate protection in accordance with the railway owner’s requirements shall\\n                     be followed. (Provision of Block Inspectors, Flagmen and Lookouts)\\n\\n                      (d)    All persons shall wear high visibility clothing at all times.\\n\\n                      (e)  Any induction training requirements of the railways shall be strictly observed\\n\\n\\n          38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    The batching plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of\\n                         unloading and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\\n                             plant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\\n                          loading the segments to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be\\n                         avoided.\\n\\n                                    ii)   The batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a compulsory\\n                  PPE zone\\n\\n                                     iii)      If in case of material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same\\n                             shall be segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate\\n                            barrications.\\n\\n                          iv)    Electrical system  shall also be suitably planned so that location  of diesel\\n                          generator,  if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning of area\\n                              lighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and pose danger.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.     quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 58,\n  \"review_status\": \"pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n                                                          242\\n\\n36.7     Regulatory signs\\n\\n\\n36.7.1    Regulatory signs impose legal restriction on all traffic.  It is essential, therefore, that\\n         they are used only after consulting the local police and traffic authorities.\\n\\n\\n36.8     Warning signs\\n\\n\\n36.8.1   Warning signs in the traffic control zone shall be utilised to warn the drivers of specific\\n         hazards that may be encountered.\\n\\n\\n36.8.2   The contractor shall place detour signage at strategic locations and install appropriate\\n         warning signs.  In order to minimize disruption of access to residences and business,\\n          the contractor shall maintain at least one entrance to a property where multiple\\n         entrances exist.\\n\\n\\n36.8.3   A warning sign as given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/012 shall be installed\\n        an at all secondary road which merges with the primary road where the construction\\n         work is in progress at sufficient distance before it merges with the primary road so as\\n           to alert the road users regarding the ‘Metro Work in Progress’.\\n\\n\\n36.8.4    Materials hanging over / protruded from the chassis / body of any vehicle especially\\n          during material handling shall be indicated by red indicator (red light/flag) to indicate\\n          the caution to the road users.\\n\\n\\n36.9      Delineators\\n\\n        The delineators are the elements of a total system of traffic control and have two\\n            distinct purposes:\\n\\n                i)    To delineate and guide the driver to and along a safe path\\n\\n                  ii)   As a taper to move traffic from one lane to another.\\n\\n\\n36.9.1   These channelizing devices such as cones, traffic cylinders, tapes and drums shall be\\n         placed in or adjacent to the roadway to control the flow of  traffic. These should\\n          normally be retro-reflectors complying to IRC: 79 - Recommended Practice for Road\\n          Delineators.\\n\\n\\n36.9.2    Traffic cones and cylinders\\n\\n\\n36.9.2.1  Traffic cones of 500mm, 750mm and 1000mm high and 300mm to 500mm in diameter\\n          or in square shape at base and are often made of plastic or rubber and normally have\\n           retro-reflectorised red and white band shall be used wherever required.\\n\\n36.9.3   Drums\\n\\n36.9.3.1  Drums about 800mm to 1000mm high and 300mm in diameter can be used either as\\n          channelising or warning devices. These are highly visible, give the appearance of\\n         being formidable objects and therefore command the respect of drivers.\\n\\n\\n36.9.4    Barricades\\n\\n\\n36.9.4.1  Full height fence, barriers, barricades etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\\n         prevent the working area from  the  risk  of  accidents due  to speedy  vehicular\\n        movement. Same the way barricades protect the road users from the danger due to\\n          construction equipment and other temporary structures.\\n\\n\\n36.9.4.2  The structure dimension of the barricade, material and composition, its colour scheme,\\n      BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications laid down in\\n          tender document.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.     quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 59,\n  \"review_status\": \"pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n243\\n          36.9.4.3  All barricades shall be erected as per the design requirements of the Employer,\\n                 numbered, painted and maintained in good condition and also Barricade in-charge\\n                   maintains a barricade register in site.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.4.4  All barricades shall be conspicuously seen in the dark/night time by the road\\n                 users so that no vehicle hits the barricade. Conspicuity. shall be ensured by\\n                     affixing retro reflective stripes of required size and shape at appropriate angle at\\n                  the bottom and middle portion of the barricade at a minimum gap of 1000mm. In\\n                   addition minimum one red light or red light blinker should be placed at the top\\n                   of each barricade.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.5   The contractor shall ensure that all his construction vehicles plying on public roads\\n                         (like dump trucks, trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads from the\\n                    State Transport Authority. Drivers holding proper valid license as per the requirements\\n                      of Motor Vehicles Act shall drive these vehicles\\n\\n\\n          36.9.6   The contractor shall not undertake loading and unloading at carriageways obstructing\\n                    the free flow of vehicular traffic and encroachment of existing roads by the contractor\\n                    applying the excuse of work execution.\\n\\n\\n          36.9.7   Tow away vehicle\\n\\n\\n          36.9.7.1  The contractor shall make arrangements keeping tow away van / manpower to\\n                tow away any breakdown vehicle in the traffic flow without loosing any time at\\n                   his cost.\\n\\n          36.9.8   Cleaning of roads\\n\\n\\n          36.9.8.1  The contractor shall ensure the cleanliness of roads and footpaths by deploying\\n                 proper manpower for the same. The contractor shall have to ensure proper\\n                 brooming, cleaning washing of roads and footpaths on all the time throughout\\n                  the entire stretch till the currency of the contract including disposal of seepage.\\n\\n          37.0    Work to adjacent railways\\n\\n          37.1     Whenever work is to be conducted in close proximity to the live railways then the\\n                     following measures shall need to be addressed:\\n\\n                      (a)  The rules provided for in the Railway’s manual should be followed.\\n\\n                      (b)  No persons are allowed to encroach onto the railway unless the owner has\\n                         given specific authority.\\n\\n                       (c)   Adequate protection in accordance with the railway owner’s requirements shall\\n                     be followed. (Provision of Block Inspectors, Flagmen and Lookouts)\\n\\n                      (d)    All persons shall wear high visibility clothing at all times.\\n\\n                      (e)  Any induction training requirements of the railways shall be strictly observed\\n\\n\\n          38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    The batching plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of\\n                         unloading and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\\n                             plant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\\n                          loading the segments to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be\\n                         avoided.\\n\\n                                    ii)   The batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a compulsory\\n                  PPE zone\\n\\n                                     iii)      If in case of material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same\\n                             shall be segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate\\n                            barrications.\\n\\n                          iv)    Electrical system  shall also be suitably planned so that location  of diesel\\n                          generator,  if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning of area\\n                              lighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and pose danger.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. Conspicuity. shall be ensured by \\naffixing retro reflective stripes of required size and shape at appropriate angle at \\nthe bottom and middle portion of the barricade at a minimum gap of 1000mm. In \\naddition minimum one red light or red light blinker should be placed at the top \\nof each barricade. \\n \\n36.9.5  \\nThe contractor shall ensure that all his construction vehicles plying on public roads \\n(like dump trucks, trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads from the \\nState Transport Authority. Drivers holding proper valid license as per the requirements \\nof Motor Vehicles Act shall drive these vehicles \\n \\n36.9.6 \\nThe contractor shall not undertake loading and unloading at carriageways obstructing \\nthe free flow of vehicular traffic and encroachment of existing roads by the contractor \\napplying the excuse of work execution.   \\n \\n36.9.7 \\nTow away vehicle \\n \\n36.9.7.1 The contractor shall make arrangements keeping tow away van / manpower to \\ntow away any breakdown vehicle in the traffic flow without loosing any time at \\nhis cost. \\n36.9.8 \\nCleaning of roads \\n \\n36.9.8.1 The contractor shall ensure the cleanliness of roads and footpaths by deploying \\nproper manpower for the same. The contractor shall have to ensure proper \\nbrooming, cleaning washing of roads and footpaths on all the time throughout \\nthe entire stretch till the currency of the contract including disposal of seepage. \\n37.0 \\nWork to adjacent railways \\n37.1 \\nWhenever work is to be conducted in close proximity to the live railways then the \\nfollowing measures shall need to be addressed: \\n(a) \\nThe rules provided for in the Railway’s manual should be followed. \\n(b) \\nNo persons are allowed to encroach onto the railway unless the owner has \\ngiven specific authority. \\n(c) \\nAdequate protection in accordance with the railway owner’s requirements shall \\nbe followed. (Provision of Block Inspectors, Flagmen and Lookouts) \\n(d) \\nAll persons shall wear high visibility clothing at all times. \\n(e) \\nAny induction training requirements of the railways shall be strictly observed \\n \\n38.0 \\nBatching Plant and Casting Yard layout \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        130.55909729003906,\n        616.1395263671875,\n        515.8872680664062,\n        772.4920043945312\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"i) \\nThe batching plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of \\nunloading and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching \\nplant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and \\nloading the segments to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be \\navoided. \\nii) \\nThe batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a compulsory \\nPPE zone \\niii) \\nIf in case of material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same \\nshall be segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate \\nbarrications. \\niv) \\nElectrical system shall also be suitably planned so that location of diesel \\ngenerator, if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning of area \\nlighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and pose danger. \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        39.599998474121094,\n        24.479991912841797,\n        63.57600021362305,\n        41.38799285888672\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 5,\n      \"text\": \"243\\n\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"42.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 64,\n      \"text\": \"42.0     Medical Facilities\\n\\n\\n42.1     Medical Examination\\n\\n\\n42.1.1   The contractor shall arrange a medical examination of all his employees including his\\n          sub-contractor employees employed as drivers, operators of  lifting appliances and\\n          transport equipment before employing, after illness or injury,  if  it appears that the\\n           illness or injury might have affected his fitness and, thereafter, once in every two years\\n        up to the age of 40 and once in a year, thereafter.\\n\\n\\n                i)    The Contractor shall maintain the confidential records of medical examination or\\n                the physician authorized by the Employer.\\n\\n                  ii)   No building or other construction worker is charged for the medical examination\\n             and the cost of such examination is borne by contractor employing such building\\n               worker.\\n\\n                  iii)   The medical examination shall include: -\\n\\n\\n                a)     Full medical and occupational history.\\n\\n                b)     Clinical examination with particular reference to\\n\\n                                    i)    General Physique;\\n\\n                                       ii)     Vision:- Total visual performance using standard orthorator  like\\n                         Titmus  Vision  Tester  should be  estimated and  suitability  for\\n                         placement  ascertained  in accordance  with  the  prescribed  job\\n                           standards.\\n\\n                                        iii)    Hearing:  - Persons with normal must be able to hear a forced\\n                          whisper at twenty-four feet. Persons using hearing aids must be\\n                           able to hear a warning shout under noisy working conditions.\\n\\n                             iv)    Breathing:- Peak flow rate using standard peak flow meter and the\\n                        average peak flow rate determined out of these readings of the test\\n                          performed.  The  results  recorded  at  pre-placement  medical\\n                          examination could be used as a standard for the same individual at\\n                           the same altitude for reference during subsequent examination.\\n\\n                        v)   Upper Limbs: - Adequate arm function and grip\\n\\n                             vi)    Spine: - Adequately flexible for the job concerned.\\n\\n                               vii)   Lower Limbs: - Adequate leg and foot concerned.\\n\\n                                 viii)   General: - Mental alertness and stability with good eye, hand and\\n                              foot coordination.\\n\\n                 c)   Any other tests which the examining doctor considers necessary\\n\\n\\n42.1.2.     If the contractor fails to get the medical examination conducted as mentioned above,\\n          the employer will have the right to get the same conducted by through an agency with\\n           intimation to the contractor and deduct the cost and overhead charges.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n      \"text\": \"42.2     Occupational Health Centre\\n\\n          42.2.1   The contractor shall ensure at a construction site an occupational health centre,\\n                 mobile or static is provided and maintained in good order. and the copy of the policy is given in\\n                Appendix No.: 4.\\n\\n          42.5.2   The Employer will engage a professional agency for implementing the guidelines laid\\n               down in the policy and communicate to the contractor.\\n\\n          42.5.3   The Contractor shall extend necessary support to the appointed agency by deputing\\n                    the workmen to educators (1 for every 100\\n                   workers) and refer them for professional training to the Employers’ appointed agency\\n                       for the purpose.\\n\\n          42.5.6 throughout the contract period.\\n\\n          42.5.7   The peer educators will be paid a monthly honorarium as fixed by the Employer for\\n                   rendering his services in addition to his regular duty.\\n\\n          42.5.8   The total number of peer educators (1 for 100 workers) shall always be maintained by\\n                    the contractor.\\n\\n          42.5.9    In case if these peer educators leave the contractor by creating vacancy, then\\n                  the contractor at his own expense train the new replacement peer educator from\\n                  the \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"42.6.1   Measures shall be taken to prevent mosquito breeding at site. The measures to be\\n         taken shall include:\\n\\n\\n                i)    Empty cans, oil drums, packing and other receptacles, which may retain water\\n                  shall be deposited at a central collection point and shall be removed from the\\n                   site regularly.\\n\\n                  ii)      Still waters shall be treated at least once every week with oil in order to prevent\\n              mosquito breeding.\\n\\n                  iii)    Contractor’s equipment and other items on the site, which may retain water,\\n                  shall be stored, covered or treated in such a manner that water could not be\\n                 retained.\\n\\n             iv)   Water storage tanks shall be provided.\\n\\n\\n42.6.2    Posters in both Hindi, English and local language which draw attention to the dangers\\n           of permitting mosquito breeding, shall be displayed prominently on the site.\\n\\n\\n42.6.3   The contractor at periodic interval shall arrange to prevent mosquito breeding\\n        by fumigation  / spraying of insecticides. \"text\": \"          42.5.5   As laid down in the policy the contractor shall identify peer educators (1 for every 100\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n      \"source_line_number\": 51,\n \"text\": \"          42.5.9    In case if these peer educators leave the contractor by creating vacancy, then\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n      \"source_line_number\": 65,\n      \"text\": \"                  the contractor at his own expense train the new replacement peer educator from\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n      \"source_line_number\": 66,\n      \"text\": \"                  the Employers’ appointed agency for the purpose.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n      \"source_line_number\": 67,\n      \"text\": \"          42.5.10    It educators from among the group of workmen so that they remain with the contractor\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n      \"source_line_number\": 69,\n      \"text\": \"                   throughout the contract period.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n      \"source_line_number\": 70,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n  },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n      \"source_line_number\": 73,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n      \"source_line_number\": 74,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 65,\n      \"source_line_number\": 75,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"42.6.1   Measures shall be taken to prevent mosquito breeding at site. \"source_line_number\": 8,\n      \"text\": \"                  shall be deposited at a central collection point and shall be removed from the\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n  \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 11,\n      \"text\": \"                  ii)      Still waters shall be treated at least once every week with oil in order to prevent\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 12,\n      \"text\": \"              mosquito breeding.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 13,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 14,\n      \"text\": \"                  iii)    Contractor’s equipment and other items on the site, which may not be\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 16,\n      \"text\": \"                 retained.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 17,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 18,\n      \"text\": \"             iv)   Water storage tanks shall be provided.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 19,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 20,\n      \"text\":  },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 22,\n      \"text\": \"           of permitting mosquito breeding, shall be displayed prominently on the site.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 23,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 66,\n      \"source_line_number\": 24,\n      \"text\": \"\"\n    },\n    {\n     quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 70,\n  \"review_status\": \"pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n                                                          254\\n                  ii)   Keep noise to the lowest reasonably practicable level.  Appropriate measures\\n                     will be taken to ensure that construction works will not cause any unnecessary\\n                or excessive noise, which may disturb the occupants of any nearby dwellings,\\n                schools, hospitals, or premises with similar sensitivity to noise. Use equipment\\n                with  effective  noise-suppression  devices and employ  other  noise  control\\n             measures as to protect the public.\\n\\n                  iii)   Schedule and conduct operations in a manner that will minimize, to the greatest\\n                extent  feasible,  the  disturbance  to  the  public  in  areas  adjacent  to  the\\n                construction  activities and  to occupants  of  buildings  in the  vicinity  of the\\n                construction activities.\\n\\n             iv)   The Contractor shall submit to the Employer a Noise Monitoring and Control\\n              Plan (NMCP) under contract specific Site Environmental Plan.   It shall include\\n                       full and comprehensive details of all powered mechanical equipment, which he\\n              proposes to use during daytime and night - time, and of his proposed working\\n             methods and noise level reduction measures. The NMCP shall include detailed\\n               noise calculations and vibration levels to demonstrate the anticipated noise\\n               generation and vibrations by the Contractor.\\n\\n           v)   The NMCP prepared by the Contractor  shall guide the implementation  of\\n                construction  activity. The NMCP  will be reviewed on a regular basis and\\n              updated  as  necessary  to  assure  that  current  construction  activities  are\\n               addressed.  It may appear as a regular agenda item in project coordination\\n               meetings, if noise is an issue at any location in the contract.\\n\\n\\n43.4     Occupational Noise\\n\\n\\n                i)     Protection  against  the  effects  of  occupational  noise exposure should be\\n               provided when the sound level exceeds the threshold values as provided in\\n                Project SHE Manual.\\n\\n                  ii)   When employees are subjected to sound levels exceeding those listed in the\\n                Table, feasible administrative or engineering controls should be utilized as given\\n                   in this document and BMRC’s Project SHE Manual.\\n\\n                  iii)      If such controls fail to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table, personal\\n                 protective equipment shall be provided and used to reduce sound levels within\\n                the levels of the table.\\n\\n             iv)   When the daily noise exposure is composed of two or more periods of noise\\n              exposure of different levels, their combined effect should be considered, rather\\n               than the individual effect of each. Exposure to different levels for various periods\\n                 of time shall be computed according to the formula and sample computations,\\n              as given in project SHE Manual.\\n\\n\\n43.4      Vibration Level\\n\\n\\n43.4.1    In locations where the alignment  is close to  historical  / heritage structures, the\\n          contractor shall prepare a monitoring scheme prior to construction at such locations.\\n          This scheme for monitoring vibration level at such historical / heritage sites shall be\\n         submitted to Employer for his approval. This scheme shall include:\\n\\n                i)     Monitoring requirements  for  vibrations  at  regular  intervals  throughout  the\\n                construction period.\\n\\n                  ii)    Pre-construction  structural  integrity  inspections  of  historic  and  sensitive\\n                structures in project activity.\\n\\n                  iii)    Information dissemination about the construction method, probable  effects,\\n                 quality control measures and precautions to be used.\\n\\n             iv)   The vibration level limits at work sites adjacent to the alignment shall conform to\\n                the permitted values of peak p velocity as given in article project SHE Manual.\\n\\n\\n44.0      Ventilation and illumination\\n\\n\\n44.1      Ventilation\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n\\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. September 2026         Section Page 66 of 114 \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        82.44075775146484,\n        38.09945297241211,\n        512.76806640625,\n        341.4522705078125\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 3,\n      \"text\": \"ii) \\nKeep noise to the lowest reasonably practicable level.  Appropriate measures \\nwill be taken to ensure that construction works will not cause any unnecessary \\nor excessive noise, which may disturb the occupants of any nearby dwellings, \\nschools, hospitals, or premises with similar sensitivity to noise. Use equipment \\nwith effective noise-suppression devices and employ other noise control \\nmeasures as to protect the public.   \\niii) \\nSchedule and conduct operations in a manner that will minimize, to the greatest \\nextent feasible, the disturbance to the public in areas adjacent to the \\nconstruction activities and to occupants of buildings in the vicinity of the \\nconstruction activities. \\niv) \\nThe Contractor shall submit to the Employer a Noise Monitoring and Control \\nPlan (NMCP) under contract specific Site Environmental Plan.  It shall include \\nfull and comprehensive details of all powered mechanical equipment, which he \\nproposes to use during daytime and night - time, and of his proposed working \\nmethods and noise level reduction measures. The NMCP shall include detailed \\nnoise calculations and vibration levels to demonstrate the anticipated noise \\ngeneration and vibrations by the Contractor.  \\nv) \\nThe NMCP prepared by the Contractor shall guide the implementation of \\nconstruction activity. The NMCP will be reviewed on a regular basis and \\nupdated as necessary to assure that current construction activities are \\naddressed. It may appear as a regular agenda item in project coordination \\nmeetings, if noise is an issue at any location in the contract. \\n \\n43.4  \\nOccupational Noise \\n \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        82.4400863647461,\n        346.61981201171875,\n        512.7677001953125,\n        768.8919067382812\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 4,\n      \"text\": \"i) \\nProtection against the effects of occupational noise exposure should be \\nprovided when the sound level exceeds the threshold values as provided in \\nProject SHE Manual. \\nii) \\nWhen employees are subjected to sound levels exceeding those listed in the \\nTable, feasible administrative or engineering controls should be utilized as given \\nin this document and BMRC’s Project SHE Manual. \\niii) \\nIf such controls fail to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table, personal \\nprotective equipment shall be provided and used to reduce sound levels within \\nthe levels of the table.  \\niv) \\nWhen the daily noise exposure is composed of two or more periods of noise \\nexposure of different levels, their combined effect should be considered, rather \\nthan the individual effect of each. Exposure to different levels for various periods \\nof time shall be computed according to the formula and sample computations, \\nas given in project SHE Manual.  \\n \\n43.4  \\nVibration Level  \\n \\n43.4.1  \\nIn locations where the alignment is close to historical / heritage structures, the \\ncontractor shall prepare a monitoring scheme prior to construction at such locations. \\nThis scheme for monitoring vibration level at such historical / heritage sites shall be \\nsubmitted to Employer for his approval. This scheme shall include: \\ni) \\nMonitoring requirements for vibrations at regular intervals throughout the \\nconstruction period. \\nii) \\nPre-construction structural integrity inspections of historic and sensitive \\nstructures in project activity. \\niii) \\nInformation dissemination about the construction method, probable effects, \\nquality control measures and precautions to be used. \\niv) \\nThe vibration level limits at work sites adjacent to the alignment shall conform to \\nthe permitted values of peak p velocity as given in article project SHE Manual. \\n \\n44.0 \\nVentilation and illumination  \\n \\n44.1  \\nVentilation \\n\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"bbox\": [\n        546.0439453125,\n        24.479991912841797,\n        570.0199584960938,\n        41.38799285888672\n      ],\n      \"block_number\": 5,\n      \"text\": \"254\\n\"\n    }\n  ]\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"54.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 79,\n      \"text\": \"54.0     Hazardous Waste Management\\n\\n          54.1         If encountered or generated as a result of Contractor’s activity, then waste classified\\n                 as hazardous under the “Hazardous Wastes (Management & Handling) Rules, 1989,\\n                amendments 2000, 2003” shall be disposed off in a manner in compliance with the\\n                  procedure given in the rules under the aforesaid act.\\n\\n\\n          54.2     Chemicals classified as hazardous chemicals under “Manufacture, Storage and Import\\n                      of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 of Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 shall be\\n                  disposed off in a manner in compliance with the procedure given in the rules under the\\n                    aforesaid act.\\n\\n\\n          54.3    The contractor shall identify the nature and quantity of hazardous waste generated as\\n                a result of his activities and shall file a ‘Request for Authorisation’ with Bangalore\\n                     Pollution Control Board along with a map showing the location of storage area.\\n\\n\\n          54.4     Outside the storage area, the contractor shall place a ‘display board’, which  will\\n                    display quantity and nature of hazardous waste, on date. Hazardous Waste needs to\\n                be stored in a secure place\\n\\n\\n          54.5         It shall be the responsibility of the contractor to ensure that hazardous wastes are\\n                     stored, based on the composition, in a manner suitable for handling, storage and\\n                      transport. Environmental     Tyre wash facility not provided (clause 47.12)      Rs.10,000 per single\\n           Management       Spillage from vehicles not arrest (clause 48.9)       violation Compounded\\n                                                                                            to a maximum of\\n                                      Air monitoring not practiced (clause 47.17)\\n                                                                            Rs.50,000 at any single\\n                              Noise monitoring not practiced (clause 43.2.1)      instance\\n                          The values of air monitoring and noise monitoring\\n                                 not with in acceptable limits (clause 47.17, 43.2.1)\\n\\n                              Dust  control measures  at  sites  not  practiced\\n                                 (clause 47.13)\\n\\n                              Improper disposal of debris / residues\\n\\n                         Non compliance of clause 53.0 & 54.0\\n\\n\\n          56.4     Without limiting to the unsafe acts and or conditions mentioned above in clause 56.3\\n                  the Employer shall have the right to deduct charges for any other unsafe act and or\\n                  condition depending upon the gravity of the situation on a case-to-case basis. The\\n                 charges shall be in comparison with that of the similar offence indicated in clause\\n                     56.3.\\n\\n\\n          57.0     Stoppage of work\\n\\n\\n          57.1    The Employer shall have the right to stop the work at his sole discretion, if in his opinion the\\n                 work is being carried out in such a way that  it may cause accidents and endanger the\\n                    safety of the persons and / or property, and / or equipments. In such cases, the contractor\\n                      shall be informed in writing about the nature of hazards and possible injury / accident.\\n\\n\\n          57.2    The contractor shall not proceed with the work until he has complied with each direction to\\n                    the satisfaction of Employer.\\n\\n          57.3    The Contractor shall not be entitled for any damages / compensation for stoppage of work,\\n                due to safety reasons and the period of such stoppage of work shall not be taken as an\\n                   extension of time for Completion of the Facilities and will not be the ground for waiver of\\n                    levy of liquidated damages.\\n\\n\\n          58.0    Awards\\n\\n                The following categories will be considered for awards as per the scheme in practice of\\n                 Employer\\n\\n                                 i)    For every safe million man hour working without any reportable incidents\\n\\n                                    ii)    Zero fatality contracts\\n\\n                                     iii)   100% adherence to voluntary reporting of all accidents throughout the currency of\\n                           contract\\n\\n                          iv)    Safest project team of the year.\\n\\n                      v)    Best SHE team of the year.\\n\\n                          vi)    Safest Contractor of the year.\\n\\n\\n\\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.     quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 80,\n  \"text\": \"56.0     Charges to be recovered from contractor for unsafe act or condition\\n\\n\\n   56.1    BMRC has built an image of safety conscious organisation meticulously over a period\\n              of seven years. These accidents not only result in loss of life but also damage the\\n             reputation of BMRC. Most of the accidents are avoidable and caused preliminary due\\n              to contractors’ negligence. Hence BMRC shall recover the cost of damages from the\\n             contractors for every reportable incident (fatality / injury).\\n\\n\\n   56.2      In addition every BMRC work  site  is exposed to public scrutiny as the work  is\\n            executed just on the right-of-way.     quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 80,\n  \"text\": \"56.0     Charges to be recovered from contractor for unsafe act or condition\\n\\n\\n   56.1    BMRC has built an image of safety conscious organisation meticulously over a period\\n              of seven years. Any reportable accident (fatality / injury) results in loss of life and/or\\n             property damage. These accidents not only result in loss of life but also damage the\\n             reputation of BMRC. Most of the accidents are avoidable and caused preliminary due\\n              to contractors’ negligence. Hence BMRC shall recover the cost of damages from the\\n             contractors for every reportable incident (fatality / injury).\\n\\n\\n   56.2      In addition every BMRC work  site  is exposed to public scrutiny as the work  is\\n            executed just on the right-of-way. Any unsafe act  / unsafe condition observed by\\n              public further damages our reputation. Because of the non-voluntary compliance of\\n             contractors to the condition of contract on SHE and project SHE manual, BMRC has\\n           been forced to establish safety-enforcing organisation. # Safety and Penalty Network (Vol 3 Part V) - Additional Schedules

> Draft source synthesis. Pending PDF and human review; no compliance or applicability decision.

## Summary

BMRCL enforces strict bid security forfeiture conditions if a tenderer withdraws its bid during validity, refuses arithmetical price corrections, misrepresents facts, or fails to sign the contract and furnish performance guarantees upon award. [^e1]

Failure to comply with contract award formalization requirements, including submission of performance security and contract signing, constitutes grounds for award annulment and tender security forfeiture. [^e2] [^e3]

## Additional source statements

- Attachment 14 requires tenderers to submit an outline for their Safety, Health and Environmental plan in compliance with the SHE Manual as part of their technical details. [^e39] [^e40]
- Attachment 16 requires tenderers to sign a Statement of Integrity, Eligibility and Social and Environmental Responsibility, committing to international labour and environmental standards and audit cooperation. [^e41] [^e42]
- The safety and penalty network connects contractual safety obligations, statutory enactments under the SHE manual, and employer oversight mechanisms for BMRCL Tender Package P1. [^e43] [^e6]
- The safety and penalty network connects safety obligations, designer duties, contractor organization requirements, and default penalties specified across the tender documentation. [^e7] [^e8]
- SHE inspections under Vol 3 Part 1 Clause 10 serve as the primary mechanism to identify variations and non-compliance against the approved contractor SHE plan across all operational sites. [^e44]
- Under Vol 3 Part 1 Clause 11.4.9.3, non-conformity with external audit findings empowers the Employer to take necessary steps including stoppage of work and/or imposing penalties to enforce implementation. [^e45]
- The safety and penalty network connects reporting obligations, statutory accident notifications, and independent investigations to enforce contractor accountability under the SHE manual. [^e46] [^e9]
- The safety and penalty network links periodic SHE inspections, monthly audits, audit rating scores (MARS), and mandatory corrective action timelines for BMRCL Tender Package P1. [^e10] [^e11] [^e12]
- The SHE Manual mandates strict audit regimes, including external quarterly audits by ISO-qualified independent agencies, internal electrical safety audits, and specific audit finding prioritisation where Priority 1 gaps are rectified within 2 weeks and Priority 2 gaps within 3 to 4 weeks. [^e13] [^e47]
- The Contractor must report total workmen strength within 2 hours of shift start, submit monthly SHE reports by the 7th of the following month, and immediately report all accidents and dangerous occurrences verbally followed by written reports within 24 hours. [^e48] [^e49] [^e50]
- The safety and penalty network connects safety obligations across construction machinery, electrical installations, machine guarding, and lifting operations to contractor liabilities and penalties. [^e51] [^e52] [^e14] [^e16]
- The SHE Manual establishes that non-adherence to safety provisions, such as layout rules for batching plants and casting yards, is subject to penalties under relevant penalty clauses. [^e53]
- The safety network details specific operational restrictions, equipment certification regimes, and inspection duties for lifting appliances, gear, and tools under the SHE Manual Part II. [^e54] [^e17]
- Non-adherence to safety, machinery, launching, electrical, and operational clauses in Part II of the SHE Manual attracts penalties from the Employer depending on gravity. [^e55] [^e56] [^e57]
- The SHE Manual Part II establishes strict prohibitions and operational restrictions where non-compliance directly triggers penalties or mandatory safety interventions. [^e19] [^e58]
- The Safety and Penalty Network maps specific hazard controls, operational safety protocols, and the enforcement of penalties for non-adherence across construction zones, batching plants, and public interfaces. [^e21] [^e20] [^e22]
- Failure to maintain the required minimum 10% spare PPE stock invites appropriate penalties as per the provisions of the contract. [^e59]
- Failure by the contractor to conduct mandatory medical examinations permits the employer to arrange them through an agency and deduct costs and overhead charges. [^e60]
- The contractor is required to submit a Noise Monitoring and Control Plan under the site Environmental Quality Management Plan to monitor construction noise, calculate future noise levels, and specify abatement measures. [^e61] [^e62]
- Volume 3 Part V of the SHE Manual establishes BMRCL's recovery mechanism for contractor safety violations, unsafe acts, and unsafe conditions, operating alongside provisions for work stoppage and contractor safety awards. [^e63] [^e64] [^e65]
- Clause 57.0 establishes the Employer's right to order work stoppage for safety reasons without entitling the contractor to damages or extension of time. [^e66]
- Clause 58.0 establishes award categories for safety milestones including safe million man-hours and zero fatality contracts. [^e67]
- Volume 3 Part V of the Safety, Health and Environment (SHE) Manual establishes BMRCL's financial recovery mechanism and penalty schedules for contractor safety violations, unsafe acts, and unsafe conditions at work sites. [^e27]
- Volume 3 Part V of the SHE Manual establishes financial penalties, work stoppage powers, and safety award categories for BMRCL Tender Package P1. [^e31] [^e32] [^e33]
- The Employer holds absolute discretion to order work stoppages for safety hazards without granting time extensions or waiving liquidated damages. [^e33]
- Safety awards are established for achievements such as safe million man-hours, zero fatality contracts, and best safety teams. [^e33]
- Volume 3 Part V specifies recovery charges for launching operations, site electrical safety, hand and power tools, gas cutting, and welding infractions, featuring tiered compounding limits up to Rs. 1,00,000 or Rs. 50,000 per instance. [^e37]
- Bentonite mishandling and tyre cleaning omissions are penalized with progressive observations of Rs. 1,00,000 on first, Rs. 2,00,000 on second, and Rs. 3,00,000 on third and subsequent observations. [^e38]
- Clause 56.4 grants the Employer the right to deduct charges for any other unlisted unsafe act or condition on a case-to-case basis, scaled in comparison with similar offences indicated in clause 56.3. [^e68]

>       "text": "13.0     TENDER SECURITY (EMD)\n\n\n  13.1      The Tenderer shall submit a Tender Security (Earnest Money Deposit – EMD) for the amount\n               specified in the Notice Inviting Tender (NIT). The Tender Security shall be furnished in the\n             form of an irrevocable and unconditional Bank Guarantee (Physical or e-BG; Preferably e-\n           BG) or an Insurance Surety Bond or Demand Draft or Banker’s Cheque or online payment\n            by NEFT/RTGS, in accordance with the provisions set out below.\n\n                       i.     Bank Guarantee (Physical or e-BG):\n\n           The Bank Guarantee (Physical or e-BG) shall be issued by an Indian Scheduled Bank or a\n            Scheduled Foreign Bank (as defined in Section 2(e) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934),\n              excluding Co-operative Banks. In the case of a Foreign Bank having no branch in India, the\n         BG (Physical or e-BG) shall be accompanied by a counter-guarantee from a Scheduled\n          Bank in India.\n\n           The Bank Guarantee (Physical or e-BG) shall be payable in India in favour of Bangalore\n            Metro Rail Corporation Limited (BMRCL) and shall conform to the prescribed format provided\n                 in Attachment–12 of the Letter of Technical Bid.\n\n           The Bank Guarantee (Physical or e-BG) shall remain valid for a period of sixty (60) days\n           beyond the Tender Validity Period, including any extensions under ITT Sub-Clause 12.2\n            and shall have been issued prior to Tender submission deadline (in case of e-BG,  it shall\n              also be fully accessible on the NeSL portal prior to Tender submission deadline).\n\n           The Bank that is issuing the BG shall be on the “Structured Financing Messaging System\n            (SFMS)” platform. Separate advice of the BG shall be sent by the issuing Bank to the\n             Employer’s Bank through SFMS to ensure a secure BG. For “SFMS” the following details are\n               to be considered:\n\n                 Name: BANGALORE METRO RAIL CORPORATION LIMITED\n               Name of the Bank: BANK OF INDIA\n                     Branch: CANTONMENT BRANCH, BENGALURU.\n                    Account No. 840420110000760\n                  RTGS/IFSC: BKID0008404\n           Copy of Bank Guarantee along with a copy of MT760COV (for Bank Guarantee message) /\n          MT767COV (for Bank Guarantee amendment message) report sent by the issuing Bank shall\n            be submitted by the Tenderer as a part of their Bidding documents on e-Procurement Portal."

Contractor is strongly advised to practice the principle\n         of voluntary compliance.\n\n\n 3.3.1.2 In order to facilitate the contractor for better understanding on the various provisions of\n         the above Act and Rules, a tabulated information highlighting the Sections/Rules\n          referring to the corresponding registration of contractors, maintenance of registers and\n         records, hours of work and wages, cess & welfare, medical  facilities and safety\n        requirements are given in Appendix No. 2. > {
>   "clause_id": "5.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 14,
>       "text": "5.0      Designer’s role\n\n5.0       Designer’s role in Safety, Health and Environment"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 15,
>       "text": "5.1       Designer’s primary role includes to minimise the risk to health and safety of those\n               who are going to construct, maintain, clean, repair, dismantle or demolish the\n                     structures and any one else like adjoining road users/general public, who might be\n                    affected by the work.\n\n\n          5.2      General philosophy\n\n\n          5.2.1    When considering health and safety in designer’s work, they shall be expected to do\n                 what  is reasonable at the time the design  is prepared.  It may be possible for\n                   hazards, which cannot be addressed at the feasibility stage to be looked at during\n                     detailed design. In deciding what is reasonably practicable, the risk to health and\n                    safety produced by a feature of the design has to be weighed against the cost of\n                   excluding the feature. The overall design process does not need to be dominated by\n                a concern  to avoid  all  risks during the construction phase and maintenance.\n                 However, a judgement has to be made by weighing up one consideration against\n                   another so the cost is counted not just in financial terms, but also those of fitness for\n                   purpose,  aesthetics,  buildability  or  environmental  impact. By  applying  these\n                      principles, it may be possible to make decisions at the design stage, which will avoid\n                     or reduce risks during construction work. In many cases, the large number of design\n                    considerations  will allow a number  of equally valid design  solutions. What  is\n                    important is the approach to the solutions of design problems. This should involve a\n                   proper exercise of judgement, which takes account of health and safety issues.\n\n\n          5.3      Hierarchy of Risk Control\n\n\n          5.3.1     Designers shall need, so far as reasonably practicable, to avoid or reduce risks by\n                    applying a series of steps known as the hierarchy of risk control or principles of\n                    prevention and protection. The steps to be adopted shall include the following:\n\n\n                                 i)     consider  if the hazard can be prevented from arising so that the risk can be\n                        avoided (e.g., alter the design to avoid the risk);\n\n                                    ii)        if this cannot be achieved, the risk should be combated at source (e.g., ensure\n                          the design details of items to be lifted include attachment points for lifting);\n\n                                     iii)     failing this, priority should be given to measures to control the risk that will\n                           protect all people;\n\n                          iv)    only as a last resort should measures to control risk by means of personal\n                           protection be assumed (e.g., use of safety harnesses).\n\n          5.4      Duty to provide health and safety risks in the drawing itself\n\n\n          5.4.1      In case of situations were the designers have carried out the design work and\n                  concluded that there are  risks, which are not reasonably practicable to avoid,\n                     detailed information shall be given about the health and safety risks, which remain.\n                   This information needs to be included with the design to alert others to the risks,\n                  which they cannot reasonably be expected to know. This is essential for the parties\n               who have to use the design information.\n\n\n          5.4.2        If the designers’ basic design assumptions affect health or safety, or health and\n                    safety risks are not obvious from the standard design document, the designer shall\n                   provide additional information. The information shall include a broad indication of the\n                  assumptions about the precautions for dealing with the risks. The information will\n                need to be conveyed in a clear manner; it shall be included on drawings, in written\n                     specifications or outline method statements. The level of detail to be recorded will\n                be determined by the nature of the hazards involved and the associated level of risk.\n\n\n          5.5      Employer’s approval\n\n\n          5.5.1    Every structure like scaffold, false work, launching girder, earth retaining structures\n                       etc. shall have its design calculations included in the method statements in addition\n                      to health and safety  risks. Employers’ designer or  his approved proof check"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 16,
>       "text": "consultants as applicable as per the contract conditions shall approve  all these\n          designs.\n\n\n5.6     Any non-standard structures like trestles made up of re-bars or structures which are\n          very old, corroded, repaired for many times etc. for which no design calculations can\n        be made accurately from any national standards, shall not be allowed to be used at\n           sites even for short duration.\n\n\n5.7           If any of the above-mentioned clauses are not adhered penalty shall be imposed\n         depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition"
>     }

>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 16,
>       "text": "6.0      Contractor SHE Organisation\n\n\n6.1      Education and Experience\n\n\n6.1.1    The contractor shall appoint the required SHE personnel as prescribed in General\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 (enclosed at the end) based upon the statutory\n         requirement and establish the safety organisation based upon the contract value.\n        The minimum educational  qualification and the work experience are given  in\n         General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/002\n\n\n6.1.2     In order to effectively interact on labour welfare matters with the Employer and\n         the  statutory  authorities  enforcing  the  labour  welfare  legislations every\n         contractor shall employ a full time Labour Welfare Officer duly qualified and\n         experienced as per clause 6.1.1.\n\n\n\n\n\n6.2     Conduct and Competency\n\n6. 2.1    The conduct and functioning of the contractor SHE personnel shall be monitored by\n          the Employer. Any default or deficiency shall attract penalty as per details given\n         under penalty clause 56.0 of this document.\n\n\n6.2.2    The Contractor shall ensure that  all personnel are competent to perform the job\n         assigned to them. In the event that the Contractor is unable to demonstrate the\n        competency of any person whose activities can directly impact on the Works’ SHE\n         performance, the Employer shall remove that person from the site without any\n          procedural formalities.\n\n\n6.3      Approval from Employer\n\n\n6.3.1    The name, address, educational qualification, work experience and health condition\n           of each personnel deployed for SHE jobs shall be submitted to the Employer in the\n          format prescribed for the purpose for comments and approval well before the start of\n          the work. Only on approval by the Employer these personnel are authorised to work.\n           In case any of the SHE personnel leaves the contractor the same shall be intimated\n           to the Employer. The contractor shall recruit new personnel and fill up the vacancy.\n\n\n6.4      Responsibility of SHE personnel\n\n\n6.4.1    For  all works carried out by the contractor and his sub-contractors, the\n          responsibility of ensuring the required SHE manpower lies with the main\n         contractor only. The minimum required manpower indicated by the Employer\n         includes the sub-contractors’ work also. It shall be the responsibility of the\n        main contractor to provide required SHE manpower for all the works executed\n        by all contractors. Necessary conditions shall be included in all sub-contract\n        documents executed by the main contractor."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 17,
>       "text": "6.5     Employment status of SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.5.1    No contractor shall engage SHE manpower from any outsourcing agencies in\n                  which case the effectiveness would be lost.  All SHE manpower shall be on the\n                      payroll of the main contractor only and not on the payroll of any subcontractor or\n                   outsourcing manpower agencies etc. This condition does not apply to positions like\n                          traffic marshals who are engaged almost on a daily requirement basis.\n\n\n          6.6      Reporting of SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.6.1      All SHE personnel are to report to the Chief SHE Manager who shall report directly to\n                    the Chief Project Manager. The Employer shall monitor adherence to this procedure\n                      at all times. In case of non-adherence penalty shall be levied as indicated in the\n                    penalty clause.\n\n\n          6.7      Inadequate SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.7.1      In case if the contractor fail to provide the minimum required manpower as\n                     illustrated in General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001 or fail to fill up vacancies\n                  created within 14 days, the same shall be provided by the Employer at\n                   contractor’s cost. Any administrative expenses involved, providing the same\n                      like paper advertisement or manpower consultant charges, etc shall also be at\n                  the cost of contractor.\n\n\n          6.8       Prohibition of performance of other duties\n\n\n          6.8.1    As per Schedule VIII of BOCWR no SHE personnel shall be required or permitted to\n                 do any work which  is unconnected  to, inconsistent with or detrimental  to the\n                  performance  of the SHE  duties  for respective category mentioned  in General\n                    Information BMRC/SHE/CEO/001\n\n\n          6.9       Facilities to be provided to SHE personnel\n\n\n          6.9.1    As per schedule VIII of BOCWR, the contractor shall provide all SHE personnel with\n                 such  facilities, equipment and information that are necessary to enable him to\n                    dispatch his duties effectively.\n\n\n          6.9.2    The minimum Employer’s requirements of such facilities / equipments to be provided\n                       for SHE personnel are given in the General Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/003"
>     }

>   "clause_id": "14.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 27,
>       "text": "14.0     Accident reporting and investigation\n\n\n          14.1     Reporting to Employer\n\n\n          14.1.1    All accidents and dangerous occurrences  shall immediately be informed\n                   verbally to the Employer. This will enable the Employer to reach to the scene of\n                  accident  / dangerous occurrences to monitor/assist any rescue work and/or\n                     start conducting the investigation process so that the evidences are not lost.\n\n\n          14.1.2   Reports of all accidents (fatal / injury) and dangerous occurrences shall also be\n                  sent within 24 hours as per format provided in the Employer’s Project SHE\n                 manual.\n\n          14.1.3   No accident   / dangerous occurrences  is exempted from reporting to the\n                 Employer.\n\n\n          14.1.4   Any wilful delay in verbal and written reporting to the Employer shall be\n                  penalised as per relevant clause.\n\n\n          14.2     Reporting to Govt. organisations"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "text": "14.2.1    In addition to the above verbal and written reporting to the Employer, as per Rule 210\n           of BOCWR, notice of any accident to a worker at the building or construction site that:\n\n\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\n\n          b)    disables a worker from working for a period of 48 hours or more immediately\n                 following the accident;\n\n           c)     shall forthwith be sent by telegram, telephone, fax, or similar other means\n                including special messenger within four hours in case of fatal accidents and 72\n              hours in case of other accidents, to:\n\n                          i)     the Regional Labour Commissioner, wherein the contractor has registered\n                     the firm/work\n\n                            ii)    the board with which the worker involved was registered as a beneficiary;\n\n                             iii)    Director General and\n\n                     iv)    the next of kin or other relative of the worker involved in the accident;\n\n\n14.2.2    Further, notice of accident shall be sent in respect of an accident which\n\n\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\n\n          b)    disables the injured worker from work for more than 10 days to\n\n                          i)     the officer-in-charge of the nearest police station;\n\n                            ii)    the District Magistrate or, if the District Magistrate by order so desires, to\n\n                             iii)    the Sub-Divisional Magistrate\n\n\n14.2.3    In case of an accident causing minor injury, first-aid shall be administered and the\n           injured worker shall be immediately transferred to a hospital or other place for medical\n          treatment.\n\n14.2.4   Where any accident causing disablement that subsequently results in death, notice in\n           writing of such death, shall be sent to the authorities mentioned in clause 14.2.1 and\n          14.2.2 above within 72 hours of such death.\n\n\n14.2.5    Reporting of dangerous occurrences:\n\n\n14.2.5.1  The following classes of dangerous occurrences shall be reported to the Inspector\n         having jurisdiction, whether or not any disablement or death caused to the worker,\n         namely:\n\n\n          a)    collapse or  failure  of  lifting appliances,  or  hoist,  or conveyors, or  similar\n              equipment for handling of building or construction material or breakage or failure\n                 of rope, chain or loose gears; or overturning of cranes used in construction\n               work;\n\n          b)     falling of objects from height;\n\n           c)    collapse or subsidence of soil, tunnel, pipe lines, any wall, floor, gallery, roof or\n             any other part of any structure, launching girder, platform, staging, scaffolding or\n            means of access including formwork;\n\n          d)    explosion of receiver or vessel used  for storage of pressure greater than\n               atmospheric pressure, of any gas or gases or any liquid or solid used as\n                 building material;\n\n          e)     fire and explosion causing damage to any place on construction site where\n                 building workers are employed;\n\n               f)     spillage or leakage of any hazardous substance and damage to their container;\n\n          g)    collapse, capsizing, toppling or collision of transport equipment;\n\n          h)    leakage or release of harmful toxic gases at the construction site;\n\n\n14.2.6    In case of failure of launching girder, lifting appliance, loose gear, hoist or building and\n          other construction work, machinery and transport equipment at a construction site,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "text": "such appliances, gear, hoist, machinery or equipment and the site of such occurrence\n                       shall, as far as practicable, be kept undisturbed until inspected by the Authorities;\n\n\n          14.2.7   Every notice given for fatal accidents or dangerous occurrences shall be followed by a\n                      written report to the concerned Authorities under Section 39 of BOCWA and the\n                     Director General in the specified Form XIV of BOCWR.\n\n\n          14.3     Accident investigation\n\n\n          14.3.1   General\n\n\n          14.3.1.1  Investigations  should be  conducted  in an open and  positive atmosphere  that\n                 encourages the witnesses to talk freely. The primary objective is to ascertain the facts\n                     with a view to prevent future and possibly more serious occurrences\n\n\n          14.3.1.2  Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which result in death, serious injury or serious\n               damage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find out the cause of the\n                   accident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence.\n\n\n          14.3.1.3  Near misses and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as\n                 soon as possible as they are signals  that there are inadequacies  in the safety\n                management system.\n\n\n          14.3.2   Procedure of incident investigation\n\n\n          14.3.2.1   It is important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to\n                    the incident is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed;\n\n                     a)    take photographs and make sketches\n\n                     b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the environmental\n                          conditions\n\n                      c)    interview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties\n\n                     d)    consult expert opinion where necessary\n\n                     e)    identify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved.\n\n\n          14.3.2.2  Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident\n\n                     a)    establish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident\n\n                     b)    find out at what stage the accident took place\n\n                      c)    consider all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to\n                         the accident, and identify the most probable cause The cause of an accident\n                        should never be classified as carelessness. The specific act or omission that\n                      caused the accident must be identified.\n\n\n          14.3.2.3  The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up action\n\n                     a)    report on the findings and conclusions\n\n                     b)    formulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence\n\n                      c)    publicise the findings and the remedial actions taken\n\n\n          14.4     Employers’ independent incident investigation\n\n\n          14.4.1    In case of fatal / dangerous occurrence the Employer shall also conduct independent\n                      investigation. Contractor and his staff shall extend necessary co-operation and testify\n                  about the accident.\n\n\n          14.4.2   The contractor shall take every effort to preserve the scene of accident till the Employer\n                  completes the investigation."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 30,
>       "text": "14.4.3     All persons summoned by the Employer in connection to witness recording shall obey\n          the instructions without delay. Any wilful suppression of information by any person shall\n        be removed from the site immediately and  / or punishable as per relevant penalty\n          clause."
>     }
