>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 69,
>       "text": "               atmospheric pressure, of any gas or gases or any liquid or solid used as"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 70,
>       "text": "                 building material;"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 71,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 72,
>       "text": "          e)     fire and explosion causing damage to any place on construction site where"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 73,
>       "text": "                 building workers are employed;"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 74,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 75,
>       "text": "               f)     spillage or leakage of any hazardous substance and damage to their container;"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 76,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 77,
>       "text": "          g)    collapse, capsizing, toppling or collision of transport equipment;"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 78,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 79,
>       "text": "          h)    leakage or release of harmful toxic gases at the construction site;"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 80,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 81,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 82,
>       "text": "14.2.6    In case of failure of launching girder, lifting appliance, loose gear, hoist or building and"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 83,
>       "text": "          other construction work, machinery and transport equipment at a construction site,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 84,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 85,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 86,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 87,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 28,
>       "source_line_number": 88,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 3,
>       "text": "                 such appliances, gear, hoist, machinery or equipment and the site of such occurrence"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 4,
>       "text": "                       shall, as far as practicable, be kept undisturbed until inspected by the Authorities;"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 5,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 6,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 7,
>       "text": "          14.2.7   Every notice given for fatal accidents or dangerous occurrences shall be followed by a"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 8,
>       "text": "                      written report to the concerned Authorities under Section 39 of BOCWA and the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 9,
>       "text": "                     Director General in the specified Form XIV of BOCWR."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 10,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 11,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 12,
>       "text": "          14.3     Accident investigation"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 13,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 14,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 15,
>       "text": "          14.3.1   General"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 16,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 17,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 18,
>       "text": "          14.3.1.1  Investigations  should be  conducted  in an open and  positive atmosphere  that"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 19,
>       "text": "                 encourages the witnesses to talk freely. The primary objective is to ascertain the facts"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 20,
>       "text": "                     with a view to prevent future and possibly more serious occurrences"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 21,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 22,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 23,
>       "text": "          14.3.1.2  Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which result in death, serious injury or serious"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 24,
>       "text": "               damage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find out the cause of the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 25,
>       "text": "                   accident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 26,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 27,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 28,
>       "text": "          14.3.1.3  Near misses and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 29,
>       "text": "                 soon as possible as they are signals  that there are inadequacies  in the safety"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 30,
>       "text": "                management system."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 31,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 32,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 33,
>       "text": "          14.3.2   Procedure of incident investigation"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 34,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 35,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 36,
>       "text": "          14.3.2.1   It is important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 37,
>       "text": "                    the incident is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed;"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 38,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 39,
>       "text": "                     a)    take photographs and make sketches"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 40,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 41,
>       "text": "                     b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the environmental"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 42,
>       "text": "                          conditions"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 43,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 44,
>       "text": "                      c)    interview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 45,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 46,
>       "text": "                     d)    consult expert opinion where necessary"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 47,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 48,
>       "text": "                     e)    identify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 49,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 50,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 51,
>       "text": "          14.3.2.2  Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 52,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 53,
>       "text": "                     a)    establish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 54,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 55,
>       "text": "                     b)    find out at what stage the accident took place"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 56,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 57,
>       "text": "                      c)    consider all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 58,
>       "text": "                         the accident, and identify the most probable cause The cause of an accident"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 59,
>       "text": "                        should never be classified as carelessness. The specific act or omission that"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 60,
>       "text": "                      caused the accident must be identified."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 61,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 62,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 63,
>       "text": "          14.3.2.3  The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up action"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 64,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 65,
>       "text": "                     a)    report on the findings and conclusions"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 66,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 67,
>       "text": "                     b)    formulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 68,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 69,
>       "text": "                      c)    publicise the findings and the remedial actions taken"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 70,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 71,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 72,
>       "text": "          14.4     Employers’ independent incident investigation"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 73,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 74,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 75,
>       "text": "          14.4.1    In case of fatal / dangerous occurrence the Employer shall also conduct independent"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 76,
>       "text": "                      investigation. Contractor and his staff shall extend necessary co-operation and testify"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 77,
>       "text": "                  about the accident."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 78,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 79,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 80,
>       "text": "          14.4.2   The contractor shall take every effort to preserve the scene of accident till the Employer"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 81,
>       "text": "                  completes the investigation."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 82,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 83,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 84,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 29,
>       "source_line_number": 85,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 30,
>       "source_line_number": 3,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 30,
>       "source_line_number": 4,
>       "text": "14.4.3     All persons summoned by the Employer in connection to witness recording shall obey"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 30,
>       "source_line_number": 5,
>       "text": "          the instructions without delay. Any wilful suppression of information by any person shall"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 30,
>       "source_line_number": 6,
>       "text": "        be removed from the site immediately and  / or punishable as per relevant penalty"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 30,
>       "source_line_number": 7,
>       "text": "          clause."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 30,

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n207\n          11.2.2    This Monthly SHE Audit Rating Score (MARS) report will enable the Employer to\n                   evaluate the general compliance by the Contractor with the Conditions of Contract, the\n                  Employer’s Project SHE Manual and the Contractor’s site specific SHE Plan.\n\n\n          11.2.3   Monthly Audits  will be conducted in accordance with BMRC Guidelines.  The\n                    Project Manager accompanied by the Employer’s representatives shall carry out\n                    the Audit. The Contractor’s senior manager and SHE in-charge should also be\n                      invited to attend.\n\n\n          11.2.4   Timing\n\n\n                The Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) should be conducted at least 7 days\n                       prior to the scheduled date of Monthly SHE Committee meeting.\n\n\n          11.2.5   Evaluation\n\n\n          11.2.5.1  The numerical scoring has been weighed on a 1-10 scale. The audit team will use\n                        their observations noted in evaluating the points to be awarded against each of\n                    the elements of the audited section. Wherever some topics and sub-topics are not\n                    applicable the score rating need not be given. The overall audit ratings shall be\n                  achieved by:\n\n\n                    Overall Audit rating  =    Actual Score Achieved   X 100\n\n                                  Maximum Possible Score\n\n\n          11.2.5.2  The criticality of the required actions for the respective sections of the Audit will be\n                      classified as:\n\n\n                          Sl.   Score          Description                          Action\n                   No.\n\n                 1    < 60%   Immediate               Require Contractor to rectify within 24\n                                                          hours\n\n                 2    < 75%   Improvement             Contractor rectification within 7 days and\n                                Necessary               confirmed in writing to Employer\n\n                 3    < 90%   Improvement Desirable    Contractor rectification within one month\n                                                    and confirmed in writing to Employer\n\n\n          11.2.6   Report\n\n              A copy of each Audit Report will be sent to Employer and to all subcontractors,\n                     with whom  it  will then be discussed in detail at the Monthly SHE Committee\n                  Meeting in order to ensure that any corrective actions are agreed upon.\n\n\n          11.3     Monthly Electrical Safety Audit\n\n\n          11.3.1   A team comprising of contractor’s senior SHE (Electrical) engineer and Employer’s\n                    representative shall conduct monthly electrical safety audit covering the following and\n                  submit the report to Employer.\n\n\n                                 i)     Electrical accidents investigation findings and remedy\n\n                                    ii)   Adequacy of power generation and power requirements\n\n                                     iii)   Power distribution and transmission system in place\n\n                          iv)   Updated electrical single line diagram showing the current condition of power\n                        source and distribution including the IP44 DBs arrangement.\n\n                      v)     Electrical protection devices – selection, installation and maintenance.\n\n                          vi)   Earth or ground connection and earth pit maintenance details\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          206\n           v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances, equipment and\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\n\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants, equipment, powered  tools and any other\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators and workmen.\n\n\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\n\n\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections for ensuring an activity whether it\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules; method statement submitted or\n         developed procedures.\n\n\n        The following are examples that will be commonly performed as required on the\n          construction site:\n\n\n                i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\n\n                  ii)    Inspection performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\n\n                  iii)    Inspection performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\n\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork before concreting by formwork erector.\n\n\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor shall ensure that a\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\n\n\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\n\n         Other inspections include the following:\n\n                i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\n\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE management team\n\n\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist for  all activity\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian standards,\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\n\n\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection and Routine Inspection will be used\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings.\n\n\n11.0    SHE Audit\n\n\n11.1     General\n\n\n11.1.1   The purpose and scope of SHE audit is to assess potential risk, liabilities and the\n         degree of compliance of construction Safety, Health and Environmental plan and its\n         supplementary  procedures and programs  against  applicable and  current SHE\n           legalisation regulations and requirements of the employer.\n\n\n11.1.2    Project Manager holds the ultimate responsibility in ensuring implementation of SHE\n          audit program during the construction work.\n\n\n11.2     Monthly Audit Rating Score (M A R S)\n\n\n11.2.1   Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) will be performed once in a month. A team\n         consisting of Project manager and Employer representative based on the pre-\n        designed score-rating format will conduct  it. The details of the pre-designed\n        monthly audit score rating formats are given in the Project SHE manual.\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n209\n          11.4.5   Audit Documents:\n\n\n          11.4.5.1  Contractor shall make the below listed documents available for the review by\n                  the Audit team.\n\n\n                                 i)   SHE policy\n\n                                    ii)   SHE manual\n\n                                     iii)   SHE Rules and Regulation\n\n                          iv)  SHE organization chart\n\n                      v)    Annual SHE objectives / programs\n\n                          vi)   Accident / near miss statistics and analysis\n\n                             vii)  SHE Training program / records for all personnel\n\n                               viii)  Operating manuals and maintenance manual of all equipments\n\n                          ix)   Safe worthiness certificates of all lifting appliances and gears\n\n                      x)    Medical fitness record for all personnel\n\n                          xi)   Risk identification, assessment and control details\n\n                             xii)   Environmental management reports\n\n                               xiii)  Emergency management records including mock drill\n\n\n          11.4.6    Audit Preparation:\n\n\n                                 i)     Audit team members are required to gather information by observations through\n                           interviews and by checks of hardware and documentation.\n\n                                    ii)    Audit team shall prepare checklist to cover all parts based on SHE legislations\n                           rules and regulations and BMRC requirements.\n\n                                     iii)    Audit team members shall verify the facts and findings leading to the identified\n                      gaps and weakness.\n\n                          iv)    Audit leader has overall responsibility for reaching a conclusion.\n\n\n          11.4.7    Reporting:\n\n\n          11.4.7.1  Audit report shall be prepared and directly sent to the Employer within 7 days of\n                   conducting the audit with a copy to the contractor.\n\n\n          11.4.8   Report contents:\n\n\n                                 i)    Executing summary - based on the finalized checklists as written the findings to\n                          the Employer by the audit team members, the audit leader  will compile a\n                        concise and accurate summary of observations and findings.\n\n                                    ii)    Introduction  -  this  will contain basic information regarding the  facilities or\n                          organization audited, the specific audit dates (inclusion of those for preparation\n                     and post-audit activities).\n\n                                     iii)    Principal positive findings - This will contain the summary of positive aspects as\n                       observed by the auditors.   It will also contain highlights of those issue, which\n                   may warrant dissemination as best practice regarding methodology used or\n                        achievement.\n\n\n                          iv)    Audit Findings - All audit findings as detailed in the audit checklists shall be\n                       grouped together as priority 1 and 2 as detailed below in a separate listing.\n\n                          a)      Priority  1: Actions  to  rectify gaps or weakness should generally be\n                            implemented within 2 – weeks, if risk potential is high or unacceptable.\n\n                          b)      Priority 2: Actions should be generally implemented or rectified with a\n                       maximum of 3 – 4 weeks, if not rectified would create a likelihood of minor\n                                    injury or business loss.\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >       "text": "i) \nAudit team members are required to gather information by observations through \ninterviews and by checks of hardware and documentation. \nii) \nAudit team shall prepare checklist to cover all parts based on SHE legislations \nrules and regulations and BMRC requirements. \niii) \nAudit team members shall verify the facts and findings leading to the identified \ngaps and weakness. \niv) \nAudit leader has overall responsibility for reaching a conclusion. \n \n11.4.7 \nReporting: \n \n11.4.7.1  Audit report shall be prepared and directly sent to the Employer within 7 days of \nconducting the audit with a copy to the contractor. \n \n11.4.8 \nReport contents: \n \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         130.55857849121094,
>         545.0994873046875,
>         515.88671875,
>         704.4518432617188
>       ],
>       "block_number": 6,
>       "text": "i) \nExecuting summary - based on the finalized checklists as written the findings to \nthe Employer by the audit team members, the audit leader will compile a \nconcise and accurate summary of observations and findings. \nii) \nIntroduction - this will contain basic information regarding the facilities or \norganization audited, the specific audit dates (inclusion of those for preparation \nand post-audit activities). \niii) \nPrincipal positive findings - This will contain the summary of positive aspects as \nobserved by the auditors.  It will also contain highlights of those issue, which \nmay warrant dissemination as best practice regarding methodology used or \nachievement. \n \niv) \nAudit Findings - All audit findings as detailed in the audit checklists shall be \ngrouped together as priority 1 and 2 as detailed below in a separate listing. \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         85.5599594116211,
>         707.7802124023438,
>         85.82657623291016,
>         708.681640625
>       ],
>       "block_number": 7,
>       "text": " \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         130.5598907470703,
>         711.8602294921875,
>         130.82650756835938,
>         712.7616577148438
>       ],
>       "block_number": 8,
>       "text": " \n"
>     },
>     {
>       "bbox": [
>         85.55957794189453,
>         717.899169921875,
>         515.8870849609375,
>         790.7316284179688
>       ],
>       "block_number": 9,
>       "text": "a) \nPriority 1: Actions to rectify gaps or weakness should generally be \nimplemented within 2 – weeks, if risk potential is high or unacceptable. \nb) \nPriority 2: Actions should be generally implemented or rectified with a \nmaximum of 3 – 4 weeks, if not rectified would create a likelihood of minor \ninjury or business loss. \n \n"
>     },

### J0bae92fd8baf7920

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 23.0 — Construction machinery|SHE 23.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF pp. 45, 46 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json#/clauses/6`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "23.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 45,
>       "text": "23.0     Construction machinery\n\n\n          23.1     Construction machineries may include dumpers and dump trucks,  lift trucks and\n                     telescopic handlers piling rigs, vibro hammers, rail welding equipments, mobile\n                    elevating work platforms, cranes, tipper lorries, lorry loaders, skip wagons, 360°\n                    excavators, 180° backhoe loaders, crawler tractors, scrapers, graders, loading\n                    shovels,  trenchers,  side  booms,  pavers,  planers,  chippers,  road  rollers,\n                    locomotives, tankers and bowsers, trailers, hydraulic and mechanical breakers\n                       etc.\n\n\n          23.2     Safe worthiness certificate\n\n\n          23.2.1   Every construction equipment shall be in sound mechanical working condition and\n                       certified by  either competent person under Factories Act  or manufacturers’\n                   warranty in case of brand new equipments or authorized persons / firms approved\n                 by Employer before induction to any site.\n\n\n          23.2.2   Every such  certificate  shall have  the  date  of  purchase, main  overhauling\n                  undertaken in the past, any accident to the equipment, visual examination details,\n                          critical components safety check, list of safety devises and its working condition,\n                   manufacturer’s maintenance checklist, past projects wherein the equipments were\n                 used etc as its minimum content.\n\n\n          23.3     Reverse Horns\n\n\n          23.3.1    All Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse alarms and maintained in\n               good working condition. Reversing  shall be done only when there  is\n                 adequate rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman\n\n\n          23.4     General operating procedures\n\n\n                                 i)     Drivers entering site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on\n                                site. These shall be verbal instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing\n                          the relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc.\n\n                                    ii)   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided  in\n                       accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations.\n\n                                     iii)   Working on gradients beyond any equipments capability shall not be allowed.\n\n                          iv)   Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed by providing\n                       wheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits,\n                             etc.\n\n                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded in excavators.\n\n                          vi)      If excavators operating on a gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be ensured\n                            that the working cycle is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far in the\n                          downhill direction, and that travel  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large\n                         excavator must never be permitted to travel in a confined area, or around people,\n                          without a banksman to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment\n                         close in to the machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled\n                         excavators, it is essential that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated.\n                                           If stabilizing devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is\n                          excavating."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 46,
>       "text": "vii)  When the front shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe\n               attachment shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking device in place.\n\n               viii)  When operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink\n                  into the surface of the ground, reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be\n           made for the stability of the machine. The loading shovel should always be lowered\n                 to the ground to stabilise the machine when the backhoe is employed.\n\n             ix)   The netting operation of the skip wagons should be carried out prior to lifting the\n                skip to reduce the risks of working on the rear platform\n\n           x)       If a tractor dozer is employed on clearing scrub or felling trees, it shall be provided\n                with adequate driver protection.\n\n             xi)   When two or more scrapers are working on the same job, a minimum distance of at\n                 least 25m shall be kept between them.\n\n              xii)   Incase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses shall be in good working\n                condition\n\n\n23.5       All wood working machines shall be fitted with suitable guards and devices such as top\n          guard, riving knife, push stick, guards for drive belts and chains, and emergency stop\n          switch easily accessible by the operator.\n\n\n23.6     Penalty\n\n\n23.6.1      If any of the above clauses are not adhered, penalty shall be imposed as per\n         relevant clause depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition."
>     }

### J5155320727bec14b

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity|SHE 26.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 49 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json#/clauses/9/fragments/3`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 49,
>   "text": "sheath and/or armour should be in addition to the earth core in the cable and shall not\n                be used as the protective conductor.\n\n\n          26.8.9   Armoured cables having an over-sheath of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) or an  oil\n                      resisting and flame retardant compound shall be used whenever there is a risk of\n                  mechanical damage occurring\n\n\n          26.9     Plugs, socket-outlets and couplers:\n\n\n          26.9.1   The contractor shall ensure plugs, socket-outlets, and couplers available in\n                  the construction  site as “splash proof” type. The minimum degree of\n                  Ingress Protection should be of IP44 in accordance with BS EN 60529.\n\n\n          26.9.2   Only plugs and fittings of the weatherproof type shall be used and they should be colour\n                 coded in accordance with the Internationally recognised standards for example as detailed\n                 as follows:\n\n                      (a)   110 volts : Yellow.\n\n                      (b)   240 volts : Blue.\n\n                       (c)   415 volts : Red.\n\n         26.10    Connections\n\n          26.10.1  Every joint and connection in a system shall be mechanically and electrically\n                   suitable  for  use  to  prevent  danger.  Proper  cable  connectors  as  per\n                    national/international standards shall only be used to connect cables.\n\n          26.10.2  No loose connections or tapped joints shall be allowed any where in the work\n                       site, office area, stores and other areas. Penalty as per relevant clause shall be\n                  put in case of observation of any tapped joints.\n\n\n         26.11    Portable and hand-held equipments:\n\n\n          26.11.1  The contractor shall ensure the use of double insulated or all-insulated portable\n                       electrical hand equipment may be used without earthing (i.e. two core cables), but\n                   they shall still be used only on 110V because of the risk of damage to trailing leads.\n\n\n         26.12    Other equipments:\n\n\n          26.12.1   All equipment shall have the provision for major switch/cut-off switch in the equipment\n                           itself.\n\n\n          26.12.2   All non-current carrying metal parts of electrical equipment shall be earthed through\n                    insulated cable\n\n\n          26.12.3   Isolate exposed high-voltage (over 415 Volts) equipment, such as transformer banks,\n                open switches, and similar equipment with exposed energized parts and prevent\n                   unauthorised access.\n\n\n          26.12.4  Approved perimeter markings shall be used to isolate restricted areas from designated\n                 work areas and entryways and shall be erected before work begins and maintained for\n                      entire duration of work. Approved perimeter marking shall be installed  with either red\n                      barrier tape printed with the words \"DANGER—HIGH VOLTAGE\" or a barrier of yellow\n                     or orange synthetic rope, approximately 1 to 1.5 meter above the floor or work\n                    surface.\n\n\n         26.13   Work on or near live conductors"

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity|SHE 26.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 47 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json#/clauses/9/fragments/1`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 47,
>   "text": "26.2.1   The contractor shall assess the size and location of the electrical loads and the\n                manner in which they vary with time during the currency of the contract.\n\n\n          26.2.2   The contractor shall elaborate as to how the total supply is to be obtained  /\n                   generated. The  details  of  the  source  of  electricity,  earthing  requirement,\n                    substation  / panel boards, distribution system shall be prepared and necessary\n                   approval from Employer obtained before proceeding of the execution of the job.\n\n\n          26.2.3   The main contractor shall take consideration, the requirements of the sub /\n                   petty contractors’ electric power supply and arrive at the capacity of main\n                 source of power supply from diesel generators.\n\n\n          26.2.4   As the sub / petty contractors’ small capacity generators create more noise\n               and safety hazard, no small capacity diesel generators shall be allowed for\n                 whatsoever the type of job to be executed under this contract.\n\n\n          26.2.5      If any unsafe noise making small capacity diesel generators are found used\n                by sub / petty contractors the main contractor shall only be penalised.\n\n\n          26.3    Work on site\n\n\n          26.3.1   The contractor shall also submit electrical single line diagram, schematic\n                diagram and the  details of the equipment  for  all temporary  electrical\n                     installation and these diagrams together with the temporary  electrical\n                equipment shall be submitted to the Employer’s for necessary approval.\n                   Failure to do so shall invite penalty as per relevant clause.\n\n\n          26.4     Strength and capability of electrical equipment\n\n\n          26.4.1   No electrical equipment shall be put into use where its strength and capability may\n                be exceeded in such a way as may give rise to danger.\n\n\n          26.5     Adverse or hazardous environments\n\n          26.5.1    Electrical equipment, which may reasonably foreseably be exposed to-\n\n                      (a)   mechanical damage;\n                      (b)   the effects of the weather, natural hazards, temperature or pressure;\n                       (c)   the effects of wet, dirty, dusty or corrosive conditions; or\n                      (d)   any flammable or explosive substance, including dusts, vapours or gases,\n                             shall be of such construction or as necessary protected as to prevent, so far\n                      as is reasonably practicable, danger arising from such exposure.\n\n\n\n          26.6      Distribution system:\n\n\n          26.6.1   The contractor shall provide distribution system for control and distribution of\n                        electricity from a main AC supply of 50Hz for typical appliances,\n\n\n                                 i)    Fixed plant – 400V 3 phase\n\n                                    ii)    Movable plant fed via trailing cable over 3.75 kW – 400 3 phase\n\n                                     iii)    Installation in site buildings – 230V single phase\n\n                          iv)   Fixed flood lighting – 230V single phase\n\n                      v)    Portable and hand tools – 115V single phase\n\n                          vi)    Site lighting  - 115V single phase\n\n                             vii)   Portable hand lamps – 115V single phase"

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          226\n\n21.6    The contractor shall also maintain a register containing a system of identification\n           of all tools and tackles, its date of purchase, safe working load, competent person\n         date of examination etc.\n\n\n21.7     Test and periodical examination of lifting appliances and gears\n\n\n21.7.1     All  lifting appliances including  all parts and gears  thereof, whether  fixed or\n        movable shall be thoroughly tested and examined by a competent person once at\n           least in every six months or after it has undergone any alterations or repairs liable\n           to affect its strength or stability. Within the validity,  if the lifting appliances are\n           shifted to a new site, re-examination by the same competent person for ensuring\n              its safety shall also be done.\n\n21.7.2    Contractors can  utilise the services of any competent person as defined  in\n          Factories Act, 1948 and approved by Chief Inspector  of Factories with the\n         permission of the Employer.\n\n\n21.7.3     All alarms and signals  like automatic safe load indicators (SLI), boom angle\n           indicators, boom extension indicators, over lift boom alarm, swing alarm, hydraulic\n          safety valves, mechanical radius indicators, load moment indicators etc. shall be\n           periodically examined and maintained always in working condition\n\n\n21.8     Automatic safe load indicators\n\n\n21.8.1   As stipulated in Rule 78 of BOCWKR 2006, no lifting appliances gear or any\n         other material handling appliance is used, if:\n\n                i)     the  Inspector  having  jurisdiction  is  not  satisfied  with  reference  to a\n                   certification of test or examination or to an authenticated record maintain as\n               provided under these rules; and\n\n                  ii)     in the view of such Inspector, the lifting appliance, lifting gear or any other\n                material  handling  appliance  is  not  safe  for use  in  building  or  other\n                construction work; and\n\n                  iii)   no pulley block is used in building or other construction work unless the safe\n               working load and its identification are clearly marked on such block.\n\n\n21.9      Qualification of operator of lifting appliances and of signaller etc\n\n\n21.9.1   The contractor shall not employ any person to drive or operate a lifting machine\n            like crane, hydra etc whether driven by mechanical power or otherwise or to give\n          signals to work as a operator of a rigger or derricks unless he\n\n                i)      is above twenty-one years of age and possesses a valid heavy transport\n                vehicle driving licence as per Motor Vehicle Act and Rules.\n\n                  ii)     is absolutely competent and reliable\n\n                  iii)   possesses the knowledge of the inherent risks involved in the operation of\n                      lifting appliances by undergoing a formal  training  at any  institution  of\n                national importance acceptable to Employer\n\n             iv)     is medically examined periodically as specified in schedule VII of BOCW\n               Rules.\n\n\n21.10    General requirements of appliances\n\n\n21.10.1   Out-of level\n\n\n21.10.1.1 One of the most severe effects of being out-of fit level is that side loads develop in\n          the boom. Because of side loads all mobile cranes lose capacity rapidly as the\n         degree of out-of-level increases and therefore\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >       "text": "sheath and/or armour should be in addition to the earth core in the cable and shall not \nbe used as the protective conductor. \n \n26.8.9 \nArmoured cables having an over-sheath of polyvinyl chloride (PVC) or an oil \nresisting and flame retardant compound shall be used whenever there is a risk of \nmechanical damage occurring  \n \n26.9 \nPlugs, socket-outlets and couplers: \n \n26.9.1 \nThe contractor shall ensure plugs, socket-outlets, and couplers available in \nthe construction site as “splash proof” type. The minimum degree of \nIngress Protection should be of IP44 in accordance with BS EN 60529.    \n \n26.9.2 \nOnly plugs and fittings of the weatherproof type shall be used and they should be colour \ncoded in accordance with the Internationally recognised standards for example as detailed \nas follows: \n(a) \n110 volts : Yellow. \n(b) \n240 volts : Blue. \n(c) \n415 volts : Red. \n \n26.10 \nConnections \n \n26.10.1 \nEvery joint and connection in a system shall be mechanically and electrically \nsuitable for use to prevent danger. Proper cable connectors as per \nnational/international standards shall only be used to connect cables. \n \n26.10.2 \nNo loose connections or tapped joints shall be allowed any where in the work \nsite, office area, stores and other areas. Penalty as per relevant clause shall be \nput in case of observation of any tapped joints. \n \n26.11 \nPortable and hand-held equipments: \n \n26.11.1 \nThe contractor shall ensure the use of double insulated or all-insulated portable \nelectrical hand equipment may be used without earthing (i.e. two core cables), but \nthey shall still be used only on 110V because of the risk of damage to trailing leads. \n \n26.12 \nOther equipments: \n \n26.12.1 \nAll equipment shall have the provision for major switch/cut-off switch in the equipment \nitself.  \n \n26.12.2 \nAll non-current carrying metal parts of electrical equipment shall be earthed through \ninsulated cable \n \n26.12.3 \nIsolate exposed high-voltage (over 415 Volts) equipment, such as transformer banks, \nopen switches, and similar equipment with exposed energized parts and prevent \nunauthorised access. \n \n26.12.4 \nApproved perimeter markings shall be used to isolate restricted areas from designated \nwork areas and entryways and shall be erected before work begins and maintained for \nentire duration of work. Approved perimeter marking shall be installed  with either red \nbarrier tape printed with the words \"DANGER—HIGH VOLTAGE\" or a barrier of yellow \nor orange synthetic rope, approximately 1 to 1.5 meter above the floor or work \nsurface. \n \n26.13 \nWork on or near live conductors \n \n"

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          244\n           v)    Drainage shall be effectively provided and waste water shall be disposed after\n               proper treatment\n\n             vi)   Time office, canteen, drinking water,  toilet and rest place shall be suitably\n                located  for the easy access to workers.  All the  facilities shall be properly\n              cleaned and maintained during the entire period of operation.\n\n              vii)   Manual handling of cement shall be avoided to a larger extent. Whenever  it is\n                absolutely necessary the workmen shall be given  full body protection, hand\n                protection and respiratory protection as a basic measure of ensuring better\n                 health.\n\n               viii)  The PPEs provided to cement handling workmen shall conform to international\n               standards.\n\n             ix)   Access roads and internal circulation roads shall be well laid and maintained\n                properly at all time.\n\n           x)    Non-adherence to any of the above provision shall be penalised as per relevant\n                penalty clause.\n\n39.0     Personal Protective Equipments (PPEs)\n\n\n39.1    The contractor shall provide required PPEs to workmen to protect against safety and /\n          or health hazards. Primarily PPEs are required for the following protection\n\n\n                i)    Head Protection (Safety helmets)\n                  ii)    Foot Protection (Safety footwear, Gumboot, etc)\n                  iii)   Body Protection (High visibility clothing (waistcoat/jacket), Apron, etc)\n             iv)   Personal fall protection (Full body harness, Rope-grap fall arrester, etc)\n           v)   Eye Protection (Goggles, Welders glasses, etc)\n             vi)   Hand Protection (Gloves, Finger coats, etc)\n              vii)   Respiratory Protection. (Nose mask, SCBAs, etc)\n               viii)  Hearing Protection (Ear plugs, Ear muffs, etc)\n\n\n39.2    The PPEs and safety appliances provided by the contractor shall be of the\n         standard as prescribed by Bureau of Indian Standards  (BIS).  If materials\n        conforming to BIS standards are not available, the contractor as approved by\n         the Employer shall procure PPE and safety appliances.\n\n\n39.3      All construction workers should be provided with high visibility jackets with\n          reflective tapes confirming to the requirement specified under BS EN 471: 1994\n        as most of viaduct /tunnelling/station and depot works are executed either\n        above or under right-of-way. The conspicuity of workmen at all times shall be\n         increased so as to protect them from speeding vehicular traffic.\n\n39.4    The contractor shall provide safety helmet, safety shoe and high visibility clothing\n            for all employees including workmen, traffic marshal and other employees who are\n        engaged for any work under this contract as per the following requirement.\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          242\n\n36.7     Regulatory signs\n\n\n36.7.1    Regulatory signs impose legal restriction on all traffic.  It is essential, therefore, that\n         they are used only after consulting the local police and traffic authorities.\n\n\n36.8     Warning signs\n\n\n36.8.1   Warning signs in the traffic control zone shall be utilised to warn the drivers of specific\n         hazards that may be encountered.\n\n\n36.8.2   The contractor shall place detour signage at strategic locations and install appropriate\n         warning signs.  In order to minimize disruption of access to residences and business,\n          the contractor shall maintain at least one entrance to a property where multiple\n         entrances exist.\n\n\n36.8.3   A warning sign as given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/012 shall be installed\n        an at all secondary road which merges with the primary road where the construction\n         work is in progress at sufficient distance before it merges with the primary road so as\n           to alert the road users regarding the ‘Metro Work in Progress’.\n\n\n36.8.4    Materials hanging over / protruded from the chassis / body of any vehicle especially\n          during material handling shall be indicated by red indicator (red light/flag) to indicate\n          the caution to the road users.\n\n\n36.9      Delineators\n\n        The delineators are the elements of a total system of traffic control and have two\n            distinct purposes:\n\n                i)    To delineate and guide the driver to and along a safe path\n\n                  ii)   As a taper to move traffic from one lane to another.\n\n\n36.9.1   These channelizing devices such as cones, traffic cylinders, tapes and drums shall be\n         placed in or adjacent to the roadway to control the flow of  traffic. These should\n          normally be retro-reflectors complying to IRC: 79 - Recommended Practice for Road\n          Delineators.\n\n\n36.9.2    Traffic cones and cylinders\n\n\n36.9.2.1  Traffic cones of 500mm, 750mm and 1000mm high and 300mm to 500mm in diameter\n          or in square shape at base and are often made of plastic or rubber and normally have\n           retro-reflectorised red and white band shall be used wherever required.\n\n36.9.3   Drums\n\n36.9.3.1  Drums about 800mm to 1000mm high and 300mm in diameter can be used either as\n          channelising or warning devices. These are highly visible, give the appearance of\n         being formidable objects and therefore command the respect of drivers.\n\n\n36.9.4    Barricades\n\n\n36.9.4.1  Full height fence, barriers, barricades etc. shall be erected around the site in order to\n         prevent the working area from  the  risk  of  accidents due  to speedy  vehicular\n        movement. Same the way barricades protect the road users from the danger due to\n          construction equipment and other temporary structures.\n\n\n36.9.4.2  The structure dimension of the barricade, material and composition, its colour scheme,\n      BMRC logo and other details shall be in accordance with specifications laid down in\n          tender document.\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 54 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n243\n          36.9.4.3  All barricades shall be erected as per the design requirements of the Employer,\n                 numbered, painted and maintained in good condition and also Barricade in-charge\n                   maintains a barricade register in site.\n\n\n          36.9.4.4  All barricades shall be conspicuously seen in the dark/night time by the road\n                 users so that no vehicle hits the barricade. Conspicuity. shall be ensured by\n                     affixing retro reflective stripes of required size and shape at appropriate angle at\n                  the bottom and middle portion of the barricade at a minimum gap of 1000mm. In\n                   addition minimum one red light or red light blinker should be placed at the top\n                   of each barricade.\n\n\n          36.9.5   The contractor shall ensure that all his construction vehicles plying on public roads\n                         (like dump trucks, trailers, etc.) have proper license to ply on public roads from the\n                    State Transport Authority. Drivers holding proper valid license as per the requirements\n                      of Motor Vehicles Act shall drive these vehicles\n\n\n          36.9.6   The contractor shall not undertake loading and unloading at carriageways obstructing\n                    the free flow of vehicular traffic and encroachment of existing roads by the contractor\n                    applying the excuse of work execution.\n\n\n          36.9.7   Tow away vehicle\n\n\n          36.9.7.1  The contractor shall make arrangements keeping tow away van / manpower to\n                tow away any breakdown vehicle in the traffic flow without loosing any time at\n                   his cost.\n\n          36.9.8   Cleaning of roads\n\n\n          36.9.8.1  The contractor shall ensure the cleanliness of roads and footpaths by deploying\n                 proper manpower for the same. The contractor shall have to ensure proper\n                 brooming, cleaning washing of roads and footpaths on all the time throughout\n                  the entire stretch till the currency of the contract including disposal of seepage.\n\n          37.0    Work to adjacent railways\n\n          37.1     Whenever work is to be conducted in close proximity to the live railways then the\n                     following measures shall need to be addressed:\n\n                      (a)  The rules provided for in the Railway’s manual should be followed.\n\n                      (b)  No persons are allowed to encroach onto the railway unless the owner has\n                         given specific authority.\n\n                       (c)   Adequate protection in accordance with the railway owner’s requirements shall\n                     be followed. (Provision of Block Inspectors, Flagmen and Lookouts)\n\n                      (d)    All persons shall wear high visibility clothing at all times.\n\n                      (e)  Any induction training requirements of the railways shall be strictly observed\n\n\n          38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\n\n\n                                 i)    The batching plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of\n                         unloading and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\n                             plant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\n                          loading the segments to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be\n                         avoided.\n\n                                    ii)   The batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a compulsory\n                  PPE zone\n\n                                     iii)      If in case of material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same\n                             shall be segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate\n                            barrications.\n\n                          iv)    Electrical system  shall also be suitably planned so that location  of diesel\n                          generator,  if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning of area\n                              lighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and pose danger.\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 55 of 114",

### J58b0ef7d929794ef

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part4#Clause 54.0 — Hazardous Waste Management|SHE 54.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 79 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_4_environmental_management_corrected/environment_clauses.json#/clauses/7`)

> {

>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 79,
>       "text": "54.0     Hazardous Waste Management\n\n          54.1         If encountered or generated as a result of Contractor’s activity, then waste classified\n                 as hazardous under the “Hazardous Wastes (Management & Handling) Rules, 1989,\n                amendments 2000, 2003” shall be disposed off in a manner in compliance with the\n                  procedure given in the rules under the aforesaid act.\n\n\n          54.2     Chemicals classified as hazardous chemicals under “Manufacture, Storage and Import\n                      of Hazardous Chemical Rules, 1989 of Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 shall be\n                  disposed off in a manner in compliance with the procedure given in the rules under the\n                    aforesaid act.\n\n\n          54.3    The contractor shall identify the nature and quantity of hazardous waste generated as\n                a result of his activities and shall file a ‘Request for Authorisation’ with Bangalore\n                     Pollution Control Board along with a map showing the location of storage area.\n\n\n          54.4     Outside the storage area, the contractor shall place a ‘display board’, which  will\n                    display quantity and nature of hazardous waste, on date. Hazardous Waste needs to\n                be stored in a secure place\n\n\n          54.5         It shall be the responsibility of the contractor to ensure that hazardous wastes are\n                     stored, based on the composition, in a manner suitable for handling, storage and\n                      transport. The labelling and packaging is required to be easily visible and be able to\n                   withstand physical conditions and climatic factors.\n\n\n          54.6    The contractor shall approach only Authorised Recyclers of Hazardous Waste for\n                    disposal of Hazardous Waste, under intimation to the Employer.\n\n\n          54.7      Submittal of all environment related documents and records pertaining to monitoring\n                and trend analysis on key parameters such as but not limited to consumption/efficient\n                 use of resources such as energy, water, material such as cement, fly ash, iron and\n                       steel, recycle/reuse of waste etc that shall have demonstrated continual improvement\n                        in the implementation of Environmental management System. Failure to do so the\n                  employer shall impose appropriate penalty as indicated under penalty clause."
>     }

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                            264\n                      PART - V: PENALTY AND AWARDS\n\n\n   56.0     Charges to be recovered from contractor for unsafe act or condition\n\n\n   56.1    BMRC has built an image of safety conscious organisation meticulously over a period\n              of seven years. Any reportable accident (fatality / injury) results in loss of life and/or\n             property damage. These accidents not only result in loss of life but also damage the\n             reputation of BMRC. Most of the accidents are avoidable and caused preliminary due\n              to contractors’ negligence. Hence BMRC shall recover the cost of damages from the\n             contractors for every reportable incident (fatality / injury).\n\n\n   56.2      In addition every BMRC work  site  is exposed to public scrutiny as the work  is\n            executed just on the right-of-way. Any unsafe act  / unsafe condition observed by\n              public further damages our reputation. The\n                 charges shall be in comparison with that of the similar offence indicated in clause\n                     56.3.\n\n\n          57.0     Stoppage of work\n\n\n          57.1    The Employer shall have the right to stop the work at his sole discretion, if in his opinion the\n                 work is being carried out in such a way that  it may cause accidents and endanger the\n                    safety of the persons and / or property, and / or equipments. In such cases, the contractor\n                      shall be informed in writing about the nature of hazards and possible injury / accident.\n\n\n          57.2    The contractor shall not proceed with the work until he has complied with each direction to\n                    the satisfaction of Employer.\n\n          57.3    The Contractor shall not be entitled for any damages / compensation for stoppage of work,\n                due to safety reasons and the period of such stoppage of work shall not be taken as an\n                   extension of time for Completion of the Facilities and will not be the ground for waiver of\n                    levy of liquidated damages.\n\n\n          58.0    Awards\n\n                The following categories will be considered for awards as per the scheme in practice of\n                 Employer\n\n                                 i)    For every safe million man hour working without any reportable incidents\n\n                                    ii)    Zero fatality contracts\n\n                                     iii)   100% adherence to voluntary reporting of all accidents throughout the currency of\n                           contract\n\n                          iv)    Safest project team of the year.\n\n                      v)    Best SHE team of the year.\n\n                          vi)    Safest Contractor of the year.\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >       "text": " \n56.4 \nWithout limiting to the unsafe acts and or conditions mentioned above in clause 56.3 \nthe Employer shall have the right to deduct charges for any other unsafe act and or \ncondition depending upon the gravity of the situation on a case-to-case basis. The \ncharges shall be in comparison with that of the similar offence indicated in clause \n56.3. \n \n57.0  \nStoppage of work  \n \n57.1 \nThe Employer shall have the right to stop the work at his sole discretion, if in his opinion the \nwork is being carried out in such a way that it may cause accidents and endanger the \nsafety of the persons and / or property, and / or equipments. In such cases, the contractor \nshall be informed in writing about the nature of hazards and possible injury / accident. \n \n57.2 \nThe contractor shall not proceed with the work until he has complied with each direction to \nthe satisfaction of Employer. \n57.3 \nThe Contractor shall not be entitled for any damages / compensation for stoppage of work, \ndue to safety reasons and the period of such stoppage of work shall not be taken as an \nextension of time for Completion of the Facilities and will not be the ground for waiver of \nlevy of liquidated damages. \n \n58.0 \nAwards \nThe following categories will be considered for awards as per the scheme in practice of \nEmployer \ni) \nFor every safe million man hour working without any reportable incidents \nii) \nZero fatality contracts \niii) \n100% adherence to voluntary reporting of all accidents throughout the currency of \ncontract \niv) \nSafest project team of the year. \nv) \nBest SHE team of the year. \nvi) \nSafest Contractor of the year. \n"

>   "text": "56.0     Charges to be recovered from contractor for unsafe act or condition\n\n\n   56.1    BMRC has built an image of safety conscious organisation meticulously over a period\n              of seven years. Any reportable accident (fatality / injury) results in loss of life and/or\n             property damage. These accidents not only result in loss of life but also damage the\n             reputation of BMRC. Most of the accidents are avoidable and caused preliminary due\n              to contractors’ negligence. Hence BMRC shall recover the cost of damages from the\n             contractors for every reportable incident (fatality / injury).\n\n\n   56.2      In addition every BMRC work  site  is exposed to public scrutiny as the work  is\n            executed just on the right-of-way. Any unsafe act  / unsafe condition observed by\n              public further damages our reputation. Because of the non-voluntary compliance of\n             contractors to the condition of contract on SHE and project SHE manual, BMRC has\n           been forced to establish safety-enforcing organisation. >       "text": "ATTACHMENT -16\n\n                   Statement of Integrity, Eligibility and Social and Environmental\n                                            Responsibility\n\n                               (To be submitted on Tenderer’s letterhead)\n\n\n\n      To\n       The Managing Director,\n        Third floor, BMTC Complex\n     KH Road, Shantinagar, Bangalore-560027.\n\n       Dear Sir,\n\n       Subject: (Name of work) ------------------------------------\n\n       Tender No--------------------------------------------\n\n\n1.    We hereby certify that neither we nor any other member of our Joint venture (if applicable) or any of our\n        Subcontractors are in any of the following situations:\n\n1.1)    being bankrupt, wound up or ceasing our activities, having our activities administered by the courts, having\n        entered  receivership, reorganization or being  in any analogous  situation  arising from any  similar\n        procedure.\n\n1.2)    having been convicted, within the past five years by decision of a court, which has the force of residential\n         jurisdiction in the country where the project is implemented, of one of the acts mentioned in sections 5.1 to\n        5.4 below or of any other offense committed during the procurement or performance of a contract.\n\n1.3)    being listed for financial sanctions by the United Nations, the European Union and/or France for the\n       purposes of fight-against-terrorist financing or threat to international peace and security.\n\n1.4)    having committed serious professional misconduct within the past five years during the procurement or\n       performance of a contract.\n\n1.5)    not having fulfilled our obligations regarding the payment of social security contributions or taxes in\n       accordance with the legal provisions of either the country where we are established or the Contracting\n         Authority's country.\n\n1.6)    being subject to an exclusion decision of the World Bank since 30 May 2012, and being listed on the\n        website http://www.worldbank.org/debarr; or any other international financing agencies.\n\n1.7)    having committed misrepresentation in documentation requested by the Beneficiary as part of the contract\n       procurement procedure.\n\n2.    We hereby certify that neither we, nor any of the members of our joint venture or any of our subcontractors\n        are in any of the following situations of conflict of interest:\n\n 2.1)   being an affiliate controlled by the Contracting Authority or a shareholder controlling the Contracting\n         Authority, unless the stemming conflict of interest has been brought to the attention of the Board of\n        Directors of Contracting Authority and resolved to its satisfaction.\n  2.2)  having a business or family relationship with a Contracting Authority's staff involved in the selection\n       procedure or the supervision of the resulting contract, unless the stemming conflict of interest has been\n        brought to the attention of Board of Directors of Contracting Authority and resolved to its satisfaction.\n\n  2.3)  being controlled by or controlling another bidder or being under common control with another bidder, or\n        receiving from or granting subsidies directly or  indirectly to another bidder, having the same legal\n        representative as another bidder, maintaining director indirect contacts with another bidder which allows"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 63,
>       "text": "us to have or give access to information contained in the respective bids, influencing them or influencing\n        decisions of the Contracting Authority;\n\n  2.4)  being engaged in a consultancy activity, which, by its nature, may conflict with the assignments that we\n       would carry out for the Contracting Authority;\n\n  2.5)   in the case of a works or goods procurement procedure:\n\n               i.     having prepared or having been associated with a consultant who prepared  specifications,\n              drawings, calculations and other documentation that are subject of the bid;\n\n               ii.    having been recruited (or being proposed to be recruited) ourselves or any of our affiliates, to carry\n              out works supervision or inspection for this contract;\n\n3.           If we are a government-owned entity, we certify that we have legal and financial autonomy and that we\n       operate under commercial laws and regulations.\n\n4.    We undertake to bring to the attention of the BMRCL, any change in situation with regard to points 1 to 3\n       here above.\n\n5.       In the context of procurement and performance of the contract:\n\n5.1)  We have not and we will not engage in any dishonest conduct (act or omission) deliberately intended to\n       deceive others, to intentionally conceal items, to violate or vitiate someone’s consent, to make them\n       circumvent legal or regulatory requirements and/or to violate their internal rules in order to obtain\n         illegitimate profit.\n\n5.2)  We have not and we will not engage in any dishonest conduct (act or omission) contrary to our legal or\n        regulatory obligations or our internal rules to obtain illegitimate profit.\n\n5.3)  We have not promised, offered or given and we will not promise, offer or give, directly or indirectly to(i) any\n       person who holds a legislative, executive, administrative or judicial mandate within the State of the\n        Contracting Authority regardless of whether that person was nominated or elected, regardless of the\n       permanent or temporary, paid or unpaid nature of the position and regardless of the hierarchical level the\n       person occupies,(ii) any other person who performs a public function, including for a State institution or a\n       State-owned company, or who provides a public service, or  (iii) any other person defined as a Public\n         Officer by the national laws of the Contracting Authority, an undue advantage of any kind, for himself or for\n       another person or entity, for such Public Officer to act or refrain from acting in his official capacity.\n\n5.4)  We have not promised, offered or given and we will not promise, offer or give, directly or indirectly to any\n        private person who occupies an executive position in a private sector entity or works for such an entity,\n        regardless of the nature of his/her capacity, any undue advantage of any kind, for himself or another\n       person or entity for such private person to perform or refrain from performing any act in breach of its legal,\n        contractual or professional obligations.\n\n5.5)  We have not and we will not engage in any practice likely to influence the contract award process to the\n        detriment of the Contracting Authority and, in particular, in any anticompetitive practice having for object or\n         for effect to prevent, restrict or distort competition, namely by limiting access to the market or the free\n        exercise of competition by other undertakings.\n\n5.6)    Neither we nor any of the members of our joint venture or any of our subcontractors shall acquire or\n       supply any equipment nor operate in any sectors under an embargo of the United Nations, the European\n       Union or France.\n5.7)  We commit ourselves to comply with and ensure that all of our subcontractors comply with international\n       environmental and labour standards, consistent with laws and regulations applicable in the country of\n       implementation  of the contract, including the fundamental conventions  of the  International Labour\n        Organization (ILO) and international environmental treaties, Moreover, we shall implement environmental\n      and social risks mitigation measures such as specified in the environmental and social management plan\n         or, if appropriate, in the environmental and social impact assessment notice provided by the Contracting\n         Authority."
