>       "text": "4.0      Contractor SHE Policy and Plan\n\n          4.1     The contractor as per Section 39 of the BOCW Act shall formulate a SHE policy and\n                    get it approved by DG respectively and display it at conspicuous places at work sites\n                        in Kannada, Hindi and other languages understood by the majority of construction\n                   workers.\n\n\n          4.2       Within 4 weeks of the notification of acceptance of the tender, the Contractor shall\n                  submit a detailed and comprehensive Contract specific SHE Plan. The SHE Plan shall"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 14,
>       "text": "include detailed policies, procedures and regulations which, when implemented, will\n         ensure compliance  of the contract  provisions. The SHE Plan  shall include the\n          following but not be restricted to:\n\n\n                i)   A statement of the Contractor’s policy, organisation and arrangements for SHE\n\n                  ii)   The name(s) and experience of person(s) within the Contractor’s proposed\n            management who shall be responsible for co-ordinating and monitoring the\n                Contractor’s SHE performance;\n\n                  iii)   The number  of SHE  staff who  shall be employed on  the Works,  their\n                  responsibilities,  authority  and  line  of  communication  with  the  proposed\n                Contractor's agent;\n\n             iv)   A statement  of the Contractor’s policy and procedures  for  identifying and\n                estimating hazards, and the measures for addressing the same;\n\n           v)   A list of SHE hazards anticipated for this Contract and sufficient information to\n              demonstrate the Contractor’s proposals for achieving effective and  efficient\n                health and safety procedures;\n\n             vi)   A description of the SHE training courses and emergency drills which shall\n\n             be provided by the Contractor, with an outline of the syllabus to be followed;\n\n              vii)   Details of the safety equipment which shall be provided by the Contractor,\n                including personal protective equipment;\n\n               viii)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring that\n                Contractor's Equipment used on the Project Site are maintained in a safe\n                condition and are operated in a safe manner;\n\n             ix)  A statement of the Contractor’s policy and procedures for ensuring that sub-\n                contractors comply with the Contractor's safety plan;\n\n           x)   A statement of the Contractor’s disciplinary procedures with respect to SHE\n                 related matters, and\n\n             xi)  A statement of the Contractor’s procedure for reporting and investigating\n                accidents, dangerous occurrences or occupational illnesses\n\n\n4.3     The Contractor shall, from time to time and as necessary are required by the\n         Employer to produce supplements to the SHE Plan such that  it is at all times a\n           detailed, comprehensive and contemporaneous statement by the Contractor of his\n            site safety, industrial health and environment obligations, responsibilities, policies\n        and procedures relating to work on Site. Any and all submissions of supplements\n           to the SHE Plan shall be made to the Employer in accordance with the agreed\n         procedures.\n\n4.4           If at any time the SHE plan is, in the Employer’s opinion, insufficient or requires\n           revision or modification to ensure the security of the Works and the safety of all\n        workmen upon and visitors to the Site, the Employer may instruct the Contractor\n           to revise the SHE plan and the Contractor shall within 7 days submit the revised\n          plan to the Employer for review.\n\n\n4.5     Any omissions, inconsistencies and errors in the SHE Plan or the Employer’s\n         acceptance or rejection of the SHE Plan and/or supplements thereto shall be\n          without prejudice  to the Contractor's  obligations with respect  to  site  safety,\n           industrial health and environment and  shall not excuse any  failure by the\n          contractor  to adopt proper and recognised  safety  practices throughout  the\n          execution of the Work.\n\n\n4.6     The Contractor  shall adhere  to the SHE Plan and  shall ensure, as  far as\n           practically possible, that  all sub-contractors of  all tiers require that contracting\n           parties each have a copy of the Site SHE Plan and comply with its provisions.\n\n\n4.7     The details of contents to be covered in the site SHE plan are given in Appendix\n         No.: 3."

>       "text": "10.0    SHE Inspection\n\n\n          10.1     The contractor shall evolve and administer a system of conducting SHE inspections\n                 and other risk management analysis on a periodical basis.\n\n\n          10.2     The purpose of SHE inspection is to identify any variation in construction activities and\n                    operations, machineries, plant and equipment and processes against the SHE Plan\n                 and its supplementary procedures and programs.\n\n\n          10.3      Following SHE inspections program shall be adopted.\n\n                                 i)    Planned General Inspection\n\n                                    ii)    Routine Inspection\n\n                                     iii)    Specific Inspection\n\n                          iv)   Other Inspection\n\n\n          10.3.1   Planned General Inspection\n\n\n          10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections are performed at predetermined intervals and  it usually\n                    involves the representation from both Contractor and the Employer.\n\n\n          10.3.1.2  Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program are:\n\n                                 i)    Monthly contractor and sub-contractors site safety committee Inspection.\n\n                                    ii)    Weekly safety inspection by construction supervisors (Contractors and Sub-\n                            contractors).\n\n                                     iii)    Daily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team.\n\n\n          10.3.2    Routine Inspection\n\n\n          10.3.2.1  Routine inspections are often referring to the inspection of work site, equipment and\n                  temporary structures performed by site and equipment operators and temporary\n                     structure erectors.\n\n                    Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program are:\n\n                                 i)     Daily Inspection of plant and equipment by operator\n\n                                    ii)    Weekly Inspection of scaffold by scaffolding supervisor\n\n                                     iii)   Monthly Inspection of electrical hand tools by competent electrical supervisor\n\n                          iv)    Quarterly Inspection of temporary electrical systems by competent electrical\n                          supervisor"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 22,
>       "text": "v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances, equipment and\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\n\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants, equipment, powered  tools and any other\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators and workmen.\n\n\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\n\n\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections for ensuring an activity whether it\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules; method statement submitted or\n         developed procedures.\n\n\n        The following are examples that will be commonly performed as required on the\n          construction site:\n\n\n                i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\n\n                  ii)    Inspection performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\n\n                  iii)    Inspection performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\n\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork before concreting by formwork erector.\n\n\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor shall ensure that a\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\n\n\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\n\n         Other inspections include the following:\n\n                i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\n\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE management team\n\n\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist for  all activity\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian standards,\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\n\n\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection and Routine Inspection will be used\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings."

### Ja911fab00f3bad38

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Clause 11.0 — SHE Audit|SHE 11.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF pp. 22, 23, 24, 25, 26 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_1_she_management/she_management_clauses.json#/clauses/10`)

> {
>   "clause_id": "11.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 22,
>       "text": "11.0    SHE Audit\n\n\n11.1     General\n\n\n11.1.1   The purpose and scope of SHE audit is to assess potential risk, liabilities and the\n         degree of compliance of construction Safety, Health and Environmental plan and its\n         supplementary  procedures and programs  against  applicable and  current SHE\n           legalisation regulations and requirements of the employer.\n\n\n11.1.2    Project Manager holds the ultimate responsibility in ensuring implementation of SHE\n          audit program during the construction work.\n\n\n11.2     Monthly Audit Rating Score (M A R S)\n\n\n11.2.1   Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) will be performed once in a month. A team\n         consisting of Project manager and Employer representative based on the pre-\n        designed score-rating format will conduct  it. The details of the pre-designed\n        monthly audit score rating formats are given in the Project SHE manual."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 23,
>       "text": "11.2.2    This Monthly SHE Audit Rating Score (MARS) report will enable the Employer to\n                   evaluate the general compliance by the Contractor with the Conditions of Contract, the\n                  Employer’s Project SHE Manual and the Contractor’s site specific SHE Plan.\n\n\n          11.2.3   Monthly Audits  will be conducted in accordance with BMRC Guidelines.  The\n                    Project Manager accompanied by the Employer’s representatives shall carry out\n                    the Audit. The Contractor’s senior manager and SHE in-charge should also be\n                      invited to attend.\n\n\n          11.2.4   Timing\n\n\n                The Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) should be conducted at least 7 days\n                       prior to the scheduled date of Monthly SHE Committee meeting.\n\n\n          11.2.5   Evaluation\n\n\n          11.2.5.1  The numerical scoring has been weighed on a 1-10 scale. The audit team will use\n                        their observations noted in evaluating the points to be awarded against each of\n                    the elements of the audited section. Wherever some topics and sub-topics are not\n                    applicable the score rating need not be given. The overall audit ratings shall be\n                  achieved by:\n\n\n                    Overall Audit rating  =    Actual Score Achieved   X 100\n\n                                  Maximum Possible Score\n\n\n          11.2.5.2  The criticality of the required actions for the respective sections of the Audit will be\n                      classified as:\n\n\n                          Sl.   Score          Description                          Action\n                   No.\n\n                 1    < 60%   Immediate               Require Contractor to rectify within 24\n                                                          hours\n\n                 2    < 75%   Improvement             Contractor rectification within 7 days and\n                                Necessary               confirmed in writing to Employer\n\n                 3    < 90%   Improvement Desirable    Contractor rectification within one month\n                                                    and confirmed in writing to Employer\n\n\n          11.2.6   Report\n\n              A copy of each Audit Report will be sent to Employer and to all subcontractors,\n                     with whom  it  will then be discussed in detail at the Monthly SHE Committee\n                  Meeting in order to ensure that any corrective actions are agreed upon.\n\n\n          11.3     Monthly Electrical Safety Audit\n\n\n          11.3.1   A team comprising of contractor’s senior SHE (Electrical) engineer and Employer’s\n                    representative shall conduct monthly electrical safety audit covering the following and\n                  submit the report to Employer.\n\n\n                                 i)     Electrical accidents investigation findings and remedy\n\n                                    ii)   Adequacy of power generation and power requirements\n\n                                     iii)   Power distribution and transmission system in place\n\n                          iv)   Updated electrical single line diagram showing the current condition of power\n                        source and distribution including the IP44 DBs arrangement.\n\n                      v)     Electrical protection devices – selection, installation and maintenance.\n\n                          vi)   Earth or ground connection and earth pit maintenance details"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 24,
>       "text": "vii)   Education and training of electrical personnel undertaken\n\n               viii)  Routine electrical inspection details\n\n             ix)    Electrical maintenance system and register.\n\n           x)   Name plate details of major electrical equipment\n\n             xi)    Classified zones in the site, if any.\n\n11.4   External SHE Audi\n\n\n11.4.1    External SHE audits are  to be conducted by  external agencies  that are\n        competent with ISO qualified auditors with the prior approval of the Employer.\n\n\n11.4.2   Areas of competence of Audit team\n\n\n11.4.2.1  Practical understanding of BOCW Act and Rules, statutory requirements on\n         health/medical and welfare of workmen, construction hazards and its prevention\n        and control, traffic management, electrical safety, rigging, safety of construction\n        equipment and environment management.\n\n\n11.4.2.2  Audit shall be conducted as per the guidelines of ISO, ILO, and national\n         standards. Audit report shall also be presented as per the above formats.\n\n\n11.4.3    External SHE audit shall be conducted on a quarterly basis throughout the\n         currency of the contract.\n\n\n11.4.4    Targets of SHE Audit:\n\n\n        The contents and coverage of the external audit shall include the following items\n\n\n11.4.4.1 SHE management:\n\n\n                i)     Organization\n\n                  ii)    Communication and Motivation\n\n                  iii)   Time office\n\n             iv)    Inspection\n\n           v)   Emergency preparedness\n\n             vi)   Budget allocation\n\n              vii)   Education and Training\n\n               viii)  Work permit system\n\n\n11.4.4.2  Technical:\n\n\n                i)     Building and Structure\n\n                  ii)    Construction operational safety\n\n                  iii)    Material safety\n\n             iv)   Hand tools and Power tools\n\n           v)     Electrical system\n\n             vi)    Safety Appliances\n\n              vii)   Fire prevention and control\n\n               viii)  Housekeeping\n\n             ix)   Maintenance and Machinery safety\n\n           x)     First-aid and Medical Facilities\n\n             xi)   Welfare measures\n\n              xii)   Environmental Management"

>       "text": "11.4.5   Audit Documents:\n\n\n          11.4.5.1  Contractor shall make the below listed documents available for the review by\n                  the Audit team.\n\n\n                                 i)   SHE policy\n\n                                    ii)   SHE manual\n\n                                     iii)   SHE Rules and Regulation\n\n                          iv)  SHE organization chart\n\n                      v)    Annual SHE objectives / programs\n\n                          vi)   Accident / near miss statistics and analysis\n\n                             vii)  SHE Training program / records for all personnel\n\n                               viii)  Operating manuals and maintenance manual of all equipments\n\n                          ix)   Safe worthiness certificates of all lifting appliances and gears\n\n                      x)    Medical fitness record for all personnel\n\n                          xi)   Risk identification, assessment and control details\n\n                             xii)   Environmental management reports\n\n                               xiii)  Emergency management records including mock drill\n\n\n          11.4.6    Audit Preparation:\n\n\n                                 i)     Audit team members are required to gather information by observations through\n                           interviews and by checks of hardware and documentation.\n\n                                    ii)    Audit team shall prepare checklist to cover all parts based on SHE legislations\n                           rules and regulations and BMRC requirements.\n\n                                     iii)    Audit team members shall verify the facts and findings leading to the identified\n                      gaps and weakness.\n\n                          iv)    Audit leader has overall responsibility for reaching a conclusion.\n\n\n          11.4.7    Reporting:\n\n\n          11.4.7.1  Audit report shall be prepared and directly sent to the Employer within 7 days of\n                   conducting the audit with a copy to the contractor.\n\n\n          11.4.8   Report contents:\n\n\n                                 i)    Executing summary - based on the finalized checklists as written the findings to\n                          the Employer by the audit team members, the audit leader  will compile a\n                        concise and accurate summary of observations and findings.\n\n                                    ii)    Introduction  -  this  will contain basic information regarding the  facilities or\n                          organization audited, the specific audit dates (inclusion of those for preparation\n                     and post-audit activities).\n\n                                     iii)    Principal positive findings - This will contain the summary of positive aspects as\n                       observed by the auditors.   It will also contain highlights of those issue, which\n                   may warrant dissemination as best practice regarding methodology used or\n                        achievement.\n\n\n                          iv)    Audit Findings - All audit findings as detailed in the audit checklists shall be\n                       grouped together as priority 1 and 2 as detailed below in a separate listing.\n\n                          a)      Priority  1: Actions  to  rectify gaps or weakness should generally be\n                            implemented within 2 – weeks, if risk potential is high or unacceptable.\n\n                          b)      Priority 2: Actions should be generally implemented or rectified with a\n                       maximum of 3 – 4 weeks, if not rectified would create a likelihood of minor\n                                    injury or business loss."

>       "text": "11.4.9    Conformity Report & Action by Employer\n\n\n11.4.9.1  The auditor shall inspect the site after 14 days of conducting initial audit for checking\n          the adequacy of implementation of items maintained under priority 1 by the contractor\n        and shall submit a conformity / non-conformity report to the Employer with a copy to the\n          contractor.\n\n\n11.4.9.2  The auditor shall again inspect after 28 days of conducting initial audit for checking the\n        adequacy of implementation of items mentioned under priority 2 by the contractor and\n           shall submit a conformity / non-conformity report to the Employer with a copy to the\n          contractor.\n\n\n11.4.9.3  In case of non-conformity of items mentioned by auditor, the Employer shall take\n         necessary steps including stoppage of work and or imposing any penalty for getting the\n          item implemented.\n\n\n11.4.10   Failure of contractor to conduct External SHE Audit\n\n\n11.4.10.1 If the contractor fails to conduct the external SHE audit in time, the Employer at\n         the cost of contractor shall get it done."

>       "text": "13.0    SHE Submittals to the Employer\n\n\n13.1    The contractor’s SHE management should send the following reports to the Employer\n           periodically:\n\n                i)     Daily Reporting of total no of workmen (as given in Clause 13.2 )\n\n                  ii)    Monthly SHE Report (as given in Clause 13.3 )\n\n                  iii)   SHE Committee Meeting Minutes (as given in Clause 7.9.1)\n\n             iv)  SHE Inspection Reports\n\n           v)   SHE Audit Reports\n\n                a)    Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) report\n\n                b)    External SHE Audit\n\n                 c)     Electrical Safety Audit\n\n             vi)    Air and Noise Quality monitoring report\n\n\n13.2     Daily Reporting of total number of workmen"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 27,
>       "text": "13.2.1   The contractor shall report to the Employer the total number of workmen\n                engaged by all including any subcontractor within 2 hours of starting of any\n                      shift in any day. This reporting shall be the primary duty of the Chief SHE\n               Manager of the contractor and reporting shall be through tele-fax / email. The\n               onus of checking the receipt of the same by the Employer  lies with the\n                   contractor. If the information is not received or received more than 2 hrs after\n                    starting of the shift, penalty shall be levied as per relevant clause.\n\n\n          13.3     Monthly SHE Report\n\n\n          13.3.1   The contractor shall prepare a monthly SHE report consisting of the following and\n                  submit 3 copies within 7th of next month to the Employer as specified in the Project\n             SHE manual.\n\n\n                                 i)    Monthly man-hour details as specified in the Project SHE manual\n\n                                    ii)    Monthly accident / incident details as specified in the Project SHE manual\n\n                                     iii)   SHE committee details\n\n                          iv)    Details of SHE training conducted in the month\n\n                      v)   SHE Inspection\n\n                          vi)  SHE internal audit details like electrical audit etc.\n\n                             vii)  SHE Communication activities under taken in the month indicating the number\n                            of posters displayed and balance availability in stock.\n\n                               viii)   Air quality / Noise monitoring details\n\n                          ix)   Toolbox talks details\n\n                      x)   PPE details: Quantity purchased, issued to the workmen and stock available.\n\n                          xi)    Details on IP 44 panel boards, lighting poles, welding and cutting equipments,\n                        Ladders, Hoists, tools & tackles.\n\n                             xii)   Monthly Lux meter study results\n\n                               xiii)  Housekeeping\n\n                        xiv)  Barricade maintenance details\n\n                     xv)  No of critical excavations\n\n                        xvi)  Health & Welfare activities\n\n                          xvii)  Safety walk conducted by Contractors’ Project Manager in the month\n\n                           xviii) SHE Activities Planned for next month"

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          208\n              vii)   Education and training of electrical personnel undertaken\n\n               viii)  Routine electrical inspection details\n\n             ix)    Electrical maintenance system and register.\n\n           x)   Name plate details of major electrical equipment\n\n             xi)    Classified zones in the site, if any.\n\n11.4   External SHE Audi\n\n\n11.4.1    External SHE audits are  to be conducted by  external agencies  that are\n        competent with ISO qualified auditors with the prior approval of the Employer.\n\n\n11.4.2   Areas of competence of Audit team\n\n\n11.4.2.1  Practical understanding of BOCW Act and Rules, statutory requirements on\n         health/medical and welfare of workmen, construction hazards and its prevention\n        and control, traffic management, electrical safety, rigging, safety of construction\n        equipment and environment management.\n\n\n11.4.2.2  Audit shall be conducted as per the guidelines of ISO, ILO, and national\n         standards. Audit report shall also be presented as per the above formats.\n\n\n11.4.3    External SHE audit shall be conducted on a quarterly basis throughout the\n         currency of the contract.\n\n\n11.4.4    Targets of SHE Audit:\n\n\n        The contents and coverage of the external audit shall include the following items\n\n\n11.4.4.1 SHE management:\n\n\n                i)     Organization\n\n                  ii)    Communication and Motivation\n\n                  iii)   Time office\n\n             iv)    Inspection\n\n           v)   Emergency preparedness\n\n             vi)   Budget allocation\n\n              vii)   Education and Training\n\n               viii)  Work permit system\n\n\n11.4.4.2  Technical:\n\n\n                i)     Building and Structure\n\n                  ii)    Construction operational safety\n\n                  iii)    Material safety\n\n             iv)   Hand tools and Power tools\n\n           v)     Electrical system\n\n             vi)    Safety Appliances\n\n              vii)   Fire prevention and control\n\n               viii)  Housekeeping\n\n             ix)   Maintenance and Machinery safety\n\n           x)     First-aid and Medical Facilities\n\n             xi)   Welfare measures\n\n              xii)   Environmental Management\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >       "text": "vii) \nEducation and training of electrical personnel undertaken \nviii) \nRoutine electrical inspection details \nix) \nElectrical maintenance system and register. \nx) \nName plate details of major electrical equipment \nxi) \nClassified zones in the site, if any. \n11.4 \nExternal SHE Audi \n \n11.4.1 \nExternal SHE audits are to be conducted by external agencies that are \ncompetent with ISO qualified auditors with the prior approval of the Employer.  \n \n11.4.2 \nAreas of competence of Audit team \n \n11.4.2.1  Practical understanding of BOCW Act and Rules, statutory requirements on \nhealth/medical and welfare of workmen, construction hazards and its prevention \nand control, traffic management, electrical safety, rigging, safety of construction \nequipment and environment management. \n \n11.4.2.2  Audit shall be conducted as per the guidelines of ISO, ILO, and national \nstandards. Audit report shall also be presented as per the above formats. \n \n11.4.3 \nExternal SHE audit shall be conducted on a quarterly basis throughout the \ncurrency of the contract.  \n \n11.4.4 \nTargets of SHE Audit: \n \n"
>     },

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n213\n                 such appliances, gear, hoist, machinery or equipment and the site of such occurrence\n                       shall, as far as practicable, be kept undisturbed until inspected by the Authorities;\n\n\n          14.2.7   Every notice given for fatal accidents or dangerous occurrences shall be followed by a\n                      written report to the concerned Authorities under Section 39 of BOCWA and the\n                     Director General in the specified Form XIV of BOCWR.\n\n\n          14.3     Accident investigation\n\n\n          14.3.1   General\n\n\n          14.3.1.1  Investigations  should be  conducted  in an open and  positive atmosphere  that\n                 encourages the witnesses to talk freely. The primary objective is to ascertain the facts\n                     with a view to prevent future and possibly more serious occurrences\n\n\n          14.3.1.2  Accidents and Dangerous Occurrences which result in death, serious injury or serious\n               damage must be investigated by the Contractor immediately to find out the cause of the\n                   accident/occurrence so that measures can be formulated to prevent any recurrence.\n\n\n          14.3.1.3  Near misses and minor accidents should also be investigated by the Contractor as\n                 soon as possible as they are signals  that there are inadequacies  in the safety\n                management system.\n\n\n          14.3.2   Procedure of incident investigation\n\n\n          14.3.2.1   It is important after any accident or dangerous occurrence that information relating to\n                    the incident is gathered in an organised way. The following steps shall be followed;\n\n                     a)    take photographs and make sketches\n\n                     b)   examine involved equipment, workplace  or  material and the environmental\n                          conditions\n\n                      c)    interview the injured, eye-witnesses and other involved parties\n\n                     d)    consult expert opinion where necessary\n\n                     e)    identify the specific contractor or sub-contractor involved.\n\n\n          14.3.2.2  Having gathered information, it is then necessary to make an analysis of incident\n\n                     a)    establish the chain of events leading to the accident or incident\n\n                     b)    find out at what stage the accident took place\n\n                      c)    consider all possible causes and the interaction of different factors that led up to\n                         the accident, and identify the most probable cause The cause of an accident\n                        should never be classified as carelessness. The specific act or omission that\n                      caused the accident must be identified.\n\n\n          14.3.2.3  The next stage is to proceed with the follow-up action\n\n                     a)    report on the findings and conclusions\n\n                     b)    formulate preventive measures to avoid recurrence\n\n                      c)    publicise the findings and the remedial actions taken\n\n\n          14.4     Employers’ independent incident investigation\n\n\n          14.4.1    In case of fatal / dangerous occurrence the Employer shall also conduct independent\n                      investigation. Contractor and his staff shall extend necessary co-operation and testify\n                  about the accident.\n\n\n          14.4.2   The contractor shall take every effort to preserve the scene of accident till the Employer\n                  completes the investigation.\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 25 of 114",

### J29be2765809f0aac

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          212\n14.2.1    In addition to the above verbal and written reporting to the Employer, as per Rule 210\n           of BOCWR, notice of any accident to a worker at the building or construction site that:\n\n\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\n\n          b)    disables a worker from working for a period of 48 hours or more immediately\n                 following the accident;\n\n           c)     shall forthwith be sent by telegram, telephone, fax, or similar other means\n                including special messenger within four hours in case of fatal accidents and 72\n              hours in case of other accidents, to:\n\n                          i)     the Regional Labour Commissioner, wherein the contractor has registered\n                     the firm/work\n\n                            ii)    the board with which the worker involved was registered as a beneficiary;\n\n                             iii)    Director General and\n\n                     iv)    the next of kin or other relative of the worker involved in the accident;\n\n\n14.2.2    Further, notice of accident shall be sent in respect of an accident which\n\n\n          a)   causes loss of life; or\n\n          b)    disables the injured worker from work for more than 10 days to\n\n                          i)     the officer-in-charge of the nearest police station;\n\n                            ii)    the District Magistrate or, if the District Magistrate by order so desires, to\n\n                             iii)    the Sub-Divisional Magistrate\n\n\n14.2.3    In case of an accident causing minor injury, first-aid shall be administered and the\n           injured worker shall be immediately transferred to a hospital or other place for medical\n          treatment.\n\n14.2.4   Where any accident causing disablement that subsequently results in death, notice in\n           writing of such death, shall be sent to the authorities mentioned in clause 14.2.1 and\n          14.2.2 above within 72 hours of such death.\n\n\n14.2.5    Reporting of dangerous occurrences:\n\n\n14.2.5.1  The following classes of dangerous occurrences shall be reported to the Inspector\n         having jurisdiction, whether or not any disablement or death caused to the worker,\n         namely:\n\n\n          a)    collapse or  failure  of  lifting appliances,  or  hoist,  or conveyors, or  similar\n              equipment for handling of building or construction material or breakage or failure\n                 of rope, chain or loose gears; or overturning of cranes used in construction\n               work;\n\n          b)     falling of objects from height;\n\n           c)    collapse or subsidence of soil, tunnel, pipe lines, any wall, floor, gallery, roof or\n             any other part of any structure, launching girder, platform, staging, scaffolding or\n            means of access including formwork;\n\n          d)    explosion of receiver or vessel used  for storage of pressure greater than\n               atmospheric pressure, of any gas or gases or any liquid or solid used as\n                 building material;\n\n          e)     fire and explosion causing damage to any place on construction site where\n                 building workers are employed;\n\n               f)     spillage or leakage of any hazardous substance and damage to their container;\n\n          g)    collapse, capsizing, toppling or collision of transport equipment;\n\n          h)    leakage or release of harmful toxic gases at the construction site;\n\n\n14.2.6    In case of failure of launching girder, lifting appliance, loose gear, hoist or building and\n          other construction work, machinery and transport equipment at a construction site,\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 24 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n211\n          13.2.1   The contractor shall report to the Employer the total number of workmen\n                engaged by all including any subcontractor within 2 hours of starting of any\n                      shift in any day. This reporting shall be the primary duty of the Chief SHE\n               Manager of the contractor and reporting shall be through tele-fax / email. The\n               onus of checking the receipt of the same by the Employer  lies with the\n                   contractor. If the information is not received or received more than 2 hrs after\n                    starting of the shift, penalty shall be levied as per relevant clause.\n\n\n          13.3     Monthly SHE Report\n\n\n          13.3.1   The contractor shall prepare a monthly SHE report consisting of the following and\n                  submit 3 copies within 7th of next month to the Employer as specified in the Project\n             SHE manual.\n\n\n                                 i)    Monthly man-hour details as specified in the Project SHE manual\n\n                                    ii)    Monthly accident / incident details as specified in the Project SHE manual\n\n                                     iii)   SHE committee details\n\n                          iv)    Details of SHE training conducted in the month\n\n                      v)   SHE Inspection\n\n                          vi)  SHE internal audit details like electrical audit etc.\n\n                             vii)  SHE Communication activities under taken in the month indicating the number\n                            of posters displayed and balance availability in stock.\n\n                               viii)   Air quality / Noise monitoring details\n\n                          ix)   Toolbox talks details\n\n                      x)   PPE details: Quantity purchased, issued to the workmen and stock available.\n\n                          xi)    Details on IP 44 panel boards, lighting poles, welding and cutting equipments,\n                        Ladders, Hoists, tools & tackles.\n\n                             xii)   Monthly Lux meter study results\n\n                               xiii)  Housekeeping\n\n                        xiv)  Barricade maintenance details\n\n                     xv)  No of critical excavations\n\n                        xvi)  Health & Welfare activities\n\n                          xvii)  Safety walk conducted by Contractors’ Project Manager in the month\n\n                           xviii) SHE Activities Planned for next month\n\n\n          14.0     Accident reporting and investigation\n\n\n          14.1     Reporting to Employer\n\n\n          14.1.1    All accidents and dangerous occurrences  shall immediately be informed\n                   verbally to the Employer. This will enable the Employer to reach to the scene of\n                  accident  / dangerous occurrences to monitor/assist any rescue work and/or\n                     start conducting the investigation process so that the evidences are not lost.\n\n\n          14.1.2   Reports of all accidents (fatal / injury) and dangerous occurrences shall also be\n                  sent within 24 hours as per format provided in the Employer’s Project SHE\n                 manual.\n\n          14.1.3   No accident   / dangerous occurrences  is exempted from reporting to the\n                 Employer.\n\n\n          14.1.4   Any wilful delay in verbal and written reporting to the Employer shall be\n                  penalised as per relevant clause.\n\n\n          14.2     Reporting to Govt. organisations\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. ### Jf2bd3cd66c8c5306

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 26.0 — Site Electricity|SHE 26.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 48 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json#/clauses/9/fragments/2`)

> {
>   "pdf_page": 48,
>   "text": "26.7      Electrical protection circuits\n\n26.7.1    Precautions shall be taken, either by earthing or by other suitable means, to prevent\n         danger arising when any conductor (other than a  circuit conductor) which may\n         reasonably foreseeable become charged as a result of either the use of a system, or a\n            fault in a system, becomes so charged. A conductor shall be regarded as earthed\n        when conductors of sufficient strength and current-carrying capability to discharge\n           electrical energy to earth connect it to the general mass of earth.\n\n                If a circuit conductor is connected to earth or to any other reference point, nothing\n         which might reasonably be expected to give rise to danger by breaking the electrical\n           continuity or introducing high impedance shall be placed in that conductor unless\n          suitable precautions are taken to prevent that danger.\n\n\n26.7.2    Appropriate electrical protection shall be provided for all circuits, against over load,\n          short circuit and earth fault current.\n\n\n26.7.3   The contractor shall provide sufficient ELCBs (maintain sensitivity 30 mA) / RCCBs for\n              all the equipments (including Potable equipments), electrical switchboards, distribution\n         panels etc. to prevent electrical shocks to the workers.\n\n\n26.7.4     All protection devices shall be capable of interrupting the circuit without damage to any\n         equipments and circuits in case of any fault may occur.\n\n\n26.7.5    Rating of fuses and circuit breakers used for the protection of circuits should be\n          coordinate with equipment power ratings.\n\n\n26.7.6    Protection against lightning shall be ensured to all equipment kept in open at sites.\n\n\n26.8     Cables:\n\n\n26.8.1   Cables shall be selected after full consideration of the condition to which they shall be\n        exposed and the duties for which they are required. Supply cable up to 3.3 kV shall be\n            in accordance with BS 6346.\n\n\n26.8.2   For supplies to mobile or transportable equipment where operating of the equipment\n          subjects the cable to flexing, the cable shall conform to any of these codes BS 6007 /\n       BS 6500 / BS 7375.\n\n\n26.8.3    Flexible cords with a conductor cross sectional area smaller than 1.5 mm2 shall not be\n        used and insulated flexible cable shall conform to BS 6500 and BS 7375.\n\n\n26.8.4   Where low voltage cables are to be used, reference shall be made to BS 7375. The\n          following standards shall also be referred to particularly for under ground cables BS\n        6346 and BS 6708\n\n\n26.8.5   Cables buried directly in the ground shall be of a type incorporating armour or metal\n         sheath or both. Such cables shall be marked by cable covers or a suitable marking\n         tape and be buried at a  sufficient depth to avoid  their being damaged by any\n          disturbance of the ground. Cable routes shall be marked on the plans kept in the site\n           electrical register.\n\n26.8.6    Cabling passing under the walk way and across way  for transport and mobile\n         equipment shall be laid in ducts at a minimum depth of 0.6 meters.\n\n26.8.7   Cables that need to cross open areas, or where span of 3m or more are involved, a\n         catenary wire on poles or other supports shall be provided for convenient means of\n         suspension. Minimum height shall be 6 m above ground.\n\n\n26.8.8   Cables carrying a voltage to earth in excess of 65V other than supply for welding\n         process shall have metal armour or sheath, which has been effectively earthed and\n         monitored by the contractor. In case of flexible and trailing cables such earthed metal"
> }

### J69a83e3638331cdc

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Clause 38.0 — Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout|SHE 38.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF pp. 59, 60 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json#/clauses/21`)

>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 59,
>       "text": "38.0     Batching Plant and Casting Yard layout\n\n\n                                 i)    The batching plant / casting yard shall be effectively planned for smooth flow of\n                         unloading and stacking the aggregates reinforcements and cement, batching\n                             plant, transport of concrete, casting the segment, stacking the segment and\n                          loading the segments to the trucks. As far as possible the conflicts should be\n                         avoided.\n\n                                    ii)   The batching plant / casting yard shall be barricaded and made as a compulsory\n                  PPE zone\n\n                                     iii)      If in case of material unloading area is not maintainable as PPE zone, the same\n                             shall be segregated properly and made as a non-PPE zone with appropriate\n                            barrications.\n\n                          iv)    Electrical system  shall also be suitably planned so that location  of diesel\n                          generator,  if any, location of DBs, routing of cables and positioning of area\n                              lighting poles/masts does not infringe on any other utility and pose danger."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 60,
>       "text": "v)    Drainage shall be effectively provided and waste water shall be disposed after\n               proper treatment\n\n             vi)   Time office, canteen, drinking water,  toilet and rest place shall be suitably\n                located  for the easy access to workers.  All the  facilities shall be properly\n              cleaned and maintained during the entire period of operation.\n\n              vii)   Manual handling of cement shall be avoided to a larger extent. Whenever  it is\n                absolutely necessary the workmen shall be given  full body protection, hand\n                protection and respiratory protection as a basic measure of ensuring better\n                 health.\n\n               viii)  The PPEs provided to cement handling workmen shall conform to international\n               standards.\n\n             ix)   Access roads and internal circulation roads shall be well laid and maintained\n                properly at all time.\n\n           x)    Non-adherence to any of the above provision shall be penalised as per relevant\n                penalty clause."
>     }

If the Employer\n                          considers,  the  contractor  shall  provide  well-equipped  boat  or  launch,\n                    manned with trained personnel at the work place.\n\n                      v)   Open side or opening where worker, equipment, vehicle or lifting appliance\n                   may fall at a building or outside shall be guarded suitably except in places of\n                           free access by reasons of nature of work.\n\n                          vi)    Suitable safety net shall be provided at places of material / man falling is\n                          possible in accordance with national standards.\n\n\n          21.0      Lifting Appliances and Gear\n\n\n          21.1       Lifting appliances means a crane, hoist machinery, derrick, winch, gin pole, sheer\n                      legs, jack, hoist drum, slewing machinery, slewing bearing fasteners,  loffing\n                  machinery sheaves, pulley blocks, hooks or other equipment used       characteristics are considered against:\n\n\n                                 i)     the weights, dimensions and lift radii of the heaviest and largest loads\n\n                                    ii)    the maximum lift height, the maximum lift radius and the weight of the loads\n                            that must be handled at each\n\n                                     iii)    the  vii)   whether loads will have to be walked or carried\n\n                               viii)  whether loads will have to be suspended for lengthy periods\n\n                          ix)    the site conditions, including the ground where the machine will be set up,\n                       access roads and ramps it must travel, space for erection and any obstacles\n                            that might impede access or operation\n\n\n          21.3    The contractor shall ensure that a valid certificate of fitness issued as per clause\n                   21.5  is available for all lifting for launching process.\n\n                       xix)  Proper access ladders/stairways shall be maintained for safe ascending  /\n                       descending of workmen / engineers.\n\n\n          22.3     Non-adherence to any of the clauses mentioned above shall be viewed\n                   seriously by the Employer and penalty levied as per relevant clause.\n\n\n          23.0     Construction machinery\n\n\n          23.1     Construction machineries may include dumpers and dump trucks,  lift trucks and\n                     telescopic handlers piling rigs, vibro hammers, rail welding equipments, mobile\n                    elevating work platforms, cranes, tipper lorries, lorry loaders, skip wagons, 360°\n                    excavators, 180° backhoe loaders, crawler tractors, scrapers, graders, loading\n                    shovels,  trenchers,  side  booms,  pavers,  planers,  chippers,  road  rollers,\n                    locomotives, tankers and bowsers, trailers, hydraulic and mechanical breakers\n                       etc.\n\n\n          23.2     Safe worthiness certificate\n\n\n          23.2.1   Every construction equipment shall be in sound mechanical working condition and\n                       certified by  either competent person under Factories Act  or manufacturers’\n                   warranty in case of brand new equipments or authorized persons / firms approved\n                 by Employer before induction to any site.\n\n\n          23.2.2   Every such  certificate  shall have  the  date  of  purchase, main  overhauling\n                  undertaken in the past, any accident to the equipment, visual examination details,\n                          critical components safety check, list of safety devises and its working condition,\n                   manufacturer’s maintenance checklist, past projects wherein the equipments were\n                 used etc as its minimum content.\n\n\n          23.3     Reverse Horns\n\n\n          23.3.1    All Vehicles shall be fitted with audible reverse alarms and maintained in\n               good working condition. Reversing  shall be done only when there  is\n                 adequate rear view visibility or under the directions of a banksman\n\n\n          23.4     General operating procedures\n\n\n                                 i)     Drivers entering site shall be instructed to follow the safe system of work adopted on\n                                site. These shall be verbal instructions or, preferably, written instructions showing\n                          the relevant site rules, the site layout, delivery areas, speed limits, etc.\n\n                                    ii)   No passengers shall be carried, unless specific seating has been provided  in\n                       accordance with the manufacturers’ recommendations.\n\n                                     iii)   Working on gradients beyond any equipments capability shall not be allowed.\n\n                          iv)   Prevention of dumper and dump truck accidents should be managed by providing\n                       wheel stops at a sufficient distance from the edges of excavations, spoil heaps, pits,\n                             etc.\n\n                      v)   The manufacturer’s recommended bucket size must not be exceeded in excavators.\n\n                          vi)      If excavators operating on a gradient which cannot be avoided, it must be ensured\n                            that the working cycle is slowed down, that the bucket is not extended too far in the\n                          downhill direction, and that travel  is undertaken with extreme caution. A large\n                         excavator must never be permitted to travel in a confined area, or around people,\n                          without a banksman to guide the driver, who should have the excavator attachment\n                         close in to the machine, with the bucket just clear of the ground. On wheeled\n                         excavators, it is essential that the tyres are in good condition and correctly inflated.\n                                           If stabilizing devices are  fitted, they should be employed when the machine  is\n                          excavating.\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          230\n              vii)  When the front shovel of the 1800 backhoe loaders is being employed, the backhoe\n               attachment shall be in its “travel” position, with the safety locking device in place.\n\n               viii)  When operating the backhoe in poor ground conditions, the stabilisers tend to sink\n                  into the surface of the ground, reducing stability. Therefore frequent checks shall be\n           made for the stability of the machine. The loading shovel should always be lowered\n                 to the ground to stabilise the machine when the backhoe is employed.\n\n             ix)   The netting operation of the skip wagons should be carried out prior to lifting the\n                skip to reduce the risks of working on the rear platform\n\n           x)       If a tractor dozer is employed on clearing scrub or felling trees, it shall be provided\n                with adequate driver protection.\n\n             xi)   When two or more scrapers are working on the same job, a minimum distance of at\n                 least 25m shall be kept between them.\n\n              xii)   Incase of hydraulic breakers, hydraulic rams and hoses shall be in good working\n                condition\n\n\n23.5       All wood working machines shall be fitted with suitable guards and devices such as top\n          guard, riving knife, push stick, guards for drive belts and chains, and emergency stop\n          switch easily accessible by the operator.\n\n\n23.6     Penalty\n\n\n23.6.1      If any of the above clauses are not adhered, penalty shall be imposed as per\n         relevant clause depending upon the gravity of the unsafe act and or condition.\n\n\n24.0    Machine and general area guarding\n\n\n24.1    The contractor shall ensure at the construction site all motors, cogwheels, chains and\n            friction gearing,  flywheels,  shafting, dangerous and moving parts  of machinery are\n          securely fenced or legged. The fencing of dangerous part of machinery is not removed\n          while such machinery is in motion or in use.\n\n\n25.0    Manual lifting and carrying of excessive weight\n\n\n25.1    The  contractor  shall ensure  at  his  construction  site  of a  building  or other\n          construction work that no building worker lifts by hand or carries overhead or over\n           his back or shoulders any material, article, tool or appliances exceeding in weight\n         as said below as per Rule 38 of BOCWR, Unless aided by another building worker\n          or device.\n\n                      Person      Maximum weight in\n                                                 kg.\n\n                          Adult man             55\n\n                          Adult                 30\n                  woman\n\n\n25.2    No building worker aided by other building worker shall lift or carry weight higher\n         than or exceeding the sum of total of maximum limits set out for each building\n         worker separately as mentioned in the table above.\n\n\n26.0      Site Electricity\n\n26.1     Competency of Electrical personnel:\n\n26.1.1   The contractor shall employ qualified and competent electrical personnel as\n         specified in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/001.\n\n\n26.2     Assessment of power\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 42 of 114",

### Ja8a8e991df7dd274

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part2#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part II: Safety|SHE vol3_part2]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF p. 44 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_2_safety/safety_clauses.json#/source_page_context/13`)

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          228\n21.11.9  No close working to any  live overhead power  line  is permitted without the\n         operation of a strict Permit to Work.\n\n\n21.11.10 Minimum lighting is to be ensured at all lifting operations.\n\n\n21.12    Failure to do any of the above shall attract penalty from the Employer as per\n         relevant clause\n\n\n22.0     Launching Operation\n\n22.1    As launching operation  is one of the  riskiest job, the contractor shall take utmost\n          precaution  at  all stages  like; planning, establishing casing yard, casting segments,\n          transporting segments,  fabrication and  erection  of launching  girders, launching  of\n         segments, pre-stressing, auto launching of girders and dismantling of launching girders.\n\n\n22.2    The contractor shall prepare a comprehensive Method Statement  for the launching\n          operation, adhering to the SHE conditions laid down in conditions of contract on SHE and\n          project SHE manual. Particular reference shall be made to the provisions on working at\n           height. As the entire process of launching has to be undertaken at an elevated level, the\n          safety of workers and the girder is paramount important. The following general guidelines\n           shall be adhered throughout the launching operation.\n\n\n                i)    Necessary ‘working platforms’ and fall protection anchorage arrangement shall be\n               provided in the launching girder itself.\n\n                  ii)    Provisions for mounting light fittings shall also be made available in the launching\n                  girder.\n\n                  iii)   The casting yard shall be established ensuring the provision given in clause 38.0\n\n             iv)   The workmen engaged in fabrication of reinforcement, concreting the segment\n                  shall be provided with necessary PPEs including compulsory hand protection\n                gloves.\n\n           v)    Casting and curing of segment shall be undertaken under the direct supervision of\n                the responsible engineer of the contractor.\n\n             vi)   Trucks  with  valid  registration,  licence, safe worthiness  certificate, Employer’s\n               approval certificate, and pollution under check certificate shall only be used for\n                transport of segments\n\n              vii)   Drivers engaged for driving these trucks, shall be trained once in 6 months at\n                specified locations as directed by the employer on defensive driving.\n\n               viii)   Drivers shall also have undergone proper medical examination as per relevant\n               clause mentioned under ‘Medical Facilities’.\n\n             ix)   The segments shall rigidly secured to the truck with necessary wooden wedges\n             and necessary red indicators/safety tapes provided so that the vehicle is clearly\n             seen by other road users both in day / night time.\n\n           x)    Every launching girder shall have a responsible engineer on duty all the time.\n\n             xi)    All the time from erection to dismantling the area between the two piers\n              wherein launching is in progress shall always be barricaded.\n\n              xii)   Unloading  of  segments  from  trucks,  lifting  of  segments,  shifting  of\n              segments, gluing shall be done under the direct supervision of the approved\n               engineer of the contractor.\n\n               xiii)  Auto launching shall be done only after approval from the Employer. After\n               every auto launching the stability of launching girder shall be ensured.\n\n            xiv)  The vertical deflection of launching girder shall be monitored at all critical\n               stages like with/without loads and after every auto launching.\n\n          xv)  A  register containing  all important operational  details from erection  to\n                dismantling of launching girders shall be maintained and made available to\n              Employer whenever called for.\n\n            xvi)  Test  certificate  for  all  lifting  gears  including  Macalloy  bars  shall be\n               maintained at a location closer to the launching girder itself so that it can be\n                referred during all inspections.\n\n             xvii)  Adequate lighting at all time shall be ensured in the entire area of operation.\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 40 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          238\n31.0      Fire prevention, protection and fighting system\n\n\n31.1    The  contractor  shall ensure  that  construction  site  is provided  with  fire\n         extinguishing  equipment  sufficient  to  extinguish  any  probable   fire  at\n         construction site. An adequate water supply is provided at ample pressure as\n         per national standard.\n\n\n31.2     Recharging of fire extinguishers and their proper maintenance should be ensured and\n         as a minimum should meet Indian National Standards\n\n\n31.3       All drivers  of vehicles, foreman, supervisors and managers  shall be trained on\n          operating the fire extinguishers and fire fighting equipment.\n\n31.4    The contractor shall also give consideration to the provision of adequate fire fighting\n         arrangements within the underground and tunnelling operations including the provision\n           of Fire Service compatible hose connections and emergency lighting\n\n\n31.5    As per the BOCWK Rules 2006, Rule 79(a)(vii), all lifting appliances’ driver cabin\n         should be provided with a suitable portable fire extinguisher.\n\n\n31.6     Combustible scrap and other construction debris should be disposed off site on a\n          regular basis. If scrap is to be burnt on site, the burning site should be specified and\n          located at a distance no less than 12 metres from any construction work or any other\n         combustible material.\n\n\n31.7     Every fire, including those extinguished by contractor personnel, shall be reported to\n          the Employer representatives.\n\n\n31.8     Emergency plans and Fire Evacuation plans shall be prepared and issued. Mock drills\n         should be held on a regular basis to ensure the effectiveness of the arrangements and\n         as a part of the programme, the Telephone Number of the local fire brigade should be\n          prominently displayed near each telephone on site.\n\n\n32.0     Corrosive substances\n\n\n32.1    As per BOCWR Rule 44, corrosive substances including alkalis and acids shall be\n          stored and used by a person dealing with such substances at a building / construction\n            site in a manner that it does not endanger the building worker and suitable PPE shall\n        be provided by the contractor to the worker during such handling and work. In case of\n           spillage of such substances on building worker, the contractor shall take immediate\n         remedial measures.\n\n\n33.0     Demolition\n\n33.1    The Contractor shall ensure that\n\n                i)       all  demolition  works be  carried  out  in a  controlled manner  under  the\n            management of experienced and competent supervision.\n\n                  ii)    the concerned department of the Government or local authority be informed and\n               permission obtained wherever required. Media shall also be informed regarding\n                   this concern.\n\n\n                  iii)     all glass or similar materials or articles in exterior openings are removed\n              before commencing any demolition work and all water, steam, electric,\n             gas and other similar supply lines are put-off and such lines so located or\n            capped with substantial coverings so as to protect it from damage and to\n               afford safety to the building workers and public..\n\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          246\n         Logo of the corresponding main contracting company for their employees and sub-\n           contracting company for their employees shall only be used.\n\n\n 39.5      In addition to the above any other PPE required for any specific jobs like, welding and\n            cutting, working at height, tunnelling etc shall also be provided to all workmen and also\n          ensure that all workmen use the PPEs properly while on the job.\n\n\n 39.6    The contractor shall not pay any cash amount in lieu of PPE to the workers/sub-\n          contractors and expect them to buy and use during work.\n\n\n 39.7    The contractor shall at all time maintain a minimum of 10% spare PPEs and\n          safety appliances and properly record and show to the Employer during the\n          inspections.  Failing  to do so  shall  invite appropriate penalty as per the\n          provisions of the contract.\n\n\n 39.8         It is always the duty of the contractor to provide required PPEs for all visitors. Towards\n             this required quantity of PPEs shall be kept always at the security post.\n\n\n 40.0      Visitors to site\n\n\n 40.1    No visitor is allowed to enter the site without the permission of the Employer. All\n          authorised visitors should report at the site office. Contractor shall provide visitor’s\n          helmet (White helmet with visitor sticker) and other PPEs like Safety Shoe, reflective\n            jacket, respiratory protection etc. as per requirement of the site.\n\n\n 40.2       All Visitors shall be accompanied at all times by a responsible member of the site\n          personnel.\n\n\n 40.3    The contractor shall be fully responsible for all visitors’ safety and health within the\n             site.\n\n\n 40.4    As indicated earlier in this Manual, the Engineer shall undertake regular audits at\n           quarterly intervals, of the Contractor’s onsite practices and procedures as a means of\n          assessing the ongoing performance of the Contractor.\n\n 40.5    The criteria against which the audits will be undertaken shall be derived from the\n          clauses within the Environment Protection Requirements (Appendix III herein above),\n           contract-specific Site Environmental Plan and previous site inspection results.\n\n 40.6      In addition to the quarterly audits by the Engineer, site inspection shall be undertaken\n         by the Contractor’s staff to inspect the construction activities in order to ensure that\n           appropriate environmental protection and pollution control measures are properly\n           followed and implemented.\n\n 40.7    The frequency of site inspection shall be at least once a week.\n\n 40.8    The Contractor shall prepare an ‘Environmental Inspection and Action Reporting\n          System’ and submit to the Engineer for approval and make amendments as\n          suggested.  It shall contain a contract specific comprehensive Environment Inspection\n           checklist as requirement of Site Environmental Plan.\n 40.9    The area of inspection shall not be limited to environmental compliance within the site\n           but areas outside the site which are likely to be affected, directly or indirectly by\n             activities at site.\n\n 40.10     Results of inspection shall be discussed with Engineer and his recommendations on\n           better environmental protection shall be notified to the Contractor for taking immediate\n           action and rapid resolution of identified non-compliance.\n40.11       If significant environmental problems are identified or if there is an environmental\n          complaint or as a part of investigation work, then the Engineer shall also carry out Ad\n         hoc site inspection which shall be attended by Contractor’s Representative.\n\n 40.12   REPORTING SYSTEM\n\n 40.12.1   reporting under  the Environmental Management System  will  contain  results  of\n\n\n Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. ### J44c81c9cdd51865e

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part3#Clause 42.0 — Medical Facilities|SHE 42.0]], `Vol3DLNP1.pdf`, PDF pp. 64, 65, 66 (`parsed_json/vol3/part_3_health_welfare/health_welfare_clauses.json#/clauses/1`)

>       "text": "42.0     Medical Facilities\n\n\n42.1     Medical Examination\n\n\n42.1.1   The contractor shall arrange a medical examination of all his employees including his\n          sub-contractor employees employed as drivers, operators of  lifting appliances and\n          transport equipment before employing, after illness or injury,  if  it appears that the\n           illness or injury might have affected his fitness and, thereafter, once in every two years\n        up to the age of 40 and once in a year, thereafter.\n\n\n                i)    The Contractor shall maintain the confidential records of medical examination or\n                the physician authorized by the Employer.\n\n                  ii)   No building or other construction worker is charged for the medical examination\n             and the cost of such examination is borne by contractor employing such building\n               worker.\n\n                  iii)   The medical examination shall include: -\n\n\n                a)     Full medical and occupational history.\n\n                b)     Clinical examination with particular reference to\n\n                                    i)    General Physique;\n\n                                       ii)     Vision:- Total visual performance using standard orthorator  like\n                         Titmus  Vision  Tester  should be  estimated and  suitability  for\n                         placement  ascertained  in accordance  with  the  prescribed  job\n                           standards.\n\n                                        iii)    Hearing:  - Persons with normal must be able to hear a forced\n                          whisper at twenty-four feet. Persons using hearing aids must be\n                           able to hear a warning shout under noisy working conditions.\n\n                             iv)    Breathing:- Peak flow rate using standard peak flow meter and the\n                        average peak flow rate determined out of these readings of the test\n                          performed.  The  results  recorded  at  pre-placement  medical\n                          examination could be used as a standard for the same individual at\n                           the same altitude for reference during subsequent examination.\n\n                        v)   Upper Limbs: - Adequate arm function and grip\n\n                             vi)    Spine: - Adequately flexible for the job concerned.\n\n                               vii)   Lower Limbs: - Adequate leg and foot concerned.\n\n                                 viii)   General: - Mental alertness and stability with good eye, hand and\n                              foot coordination.\n\n                 c)   Any other tests which the examining doctor considers necessary\n\n\n42.1.2.     If the contractor fails to get the medical examination conducted as mentioned above,\n          the employer will have the right to get the same conducted by through an agency with\n           intimation to the contractor and deduct the cost and overhead charges."
>     },

>       "text": "42.2     Occupational Health Centre\n\n          42.2.1   The contractor shall ensure at a construction site an occupational health centre,\n                 mobile or static is provided and maintained in good order. Services and facilities\n                as per the scale lay down in Schedule X of BOCWR. A construction medical\n                     officer appointed in an occupational health centre, possess the qualification as\n                     laid down in Schedule XI of BOCWR.\n\n\n          42.3    Ambulance van and room\n\n\n          42.3.1   The contractor  shall ensure  at a construction  site of a building or other\n                  construction work that an ambulance van and room are provided at such\n                  construction site or an arrangement is made with a nearby hospital for providing\n                such ambulance van for transportation of serious cases of accident or sickness\n                   of workers  to  hospital promptly and such ambulance van and room are\n                 maintained in good repair and is equipped with standard facilities specified in\n                Schedule IV and Schedule V of BOCWR.\n\n\n          42.4      First-aid boxes\n\n\n          42.4.1   The contractor shall ensure at a construction site one First-aid box for 100 workers\n                   provided and maintained for providing First-aid to the building workers. Every First-aid\n                 box  is  distinctly marked  “First-aid” and  is equipped with the  articles specified  in\n                 Schedule III of BOCWR.\n\n\n          42.5     HIV/ AIDS prevention and control\n\n\n          42.5.1   The contractor shall adopt the Employer’s Policy on “HIV  / AIDS Prevention and\n                    Control for Workmen Engaged by Contractors” and the copy of the policy is given in\n                Appendix No.: 4.\n\n          42.5.2   The Employer will engage a professional agency for implementing the guidelines laid\n               down in the policy and communicate to the contractor.\n\n          42.5.3   The Contractor shall extend necessary support to the appointed agency by deputing\n                    the workmen to attend the awareness creation programmes.\n\n          42.5.4   The contractor shall also extend necessary organizational support to the appointed\n                 agency  for the  effective implementation  of the Employers’ workplace  policy on\n                 HIV/AIDS for workmen of the Contractors.\n\n          42.5.5   As laid down in the policy the contractor shall identify peer educators (1 for every 100\n                   workers) and refer them for professional training to the Employers’ appointed agency\n                       for the purpose.\n\n          42.5.6   The peer educators on completion of the training shall serve as the focal point\n                    for any information, education and awareness campaign among the workmen\n                 throughout the contract period.\n\n          42.5.7   The peer educators will be paid a monthly honorarium as fixed by the Employer for\n                   rendering his services in addition to his regular duty.\n\n          42.5.8   The total number of peer educators (1 for 100 workers) shall always be maintained by\n                    the contractor.\n\n          42.5.9    In case if these peer educators leave the contractor by creating vacancy, then\n                  the contractor at his own expense train the new replacement peer educator from\n                  the Employers’ appointed agency for the purpose.\n          42.5.10    It is suggested to the contractor that due care should be taken to select the peer\n                   educators from among the group of workmen so that they remain with the contractor\n                   throughout the contract period.\n\n          42.6     Prevention of mosquito breeding"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 66,
>       "text": "42.6.1   Measures shall be taken to prevent mosquito breeding at site. The measures to be\n         taken shall include:\n\n\n                i)    Empty cans, oil drums, packing and other receptacles, which may retain water\n                  shall be deposited at a central collection point and shall be removed from the\n                   site regularly.\n\n                  ii)      Still waters shall be treated at least once every week with oil in order to prevent\n              mosquito breeding.\n\n                  iii)    Contractor’s equipment and other items on the site, which may retain water,\n                  shall be stored, covered or treated in such a manner that water could not be\n                 retained.\n\n             iv)   Water storage tanks shall be provided.\n\n\n42.6.2    Posters in both Hindi, English and local language which draw attention to the dangers\n           of permitting mosquito breeding, shall be displayed prominently on the site.\n\n\n42.6.3   The contractor at periodic interval shall arrange to prevent mosquito breeding\n        by fumigation  / spraying of insecticides. Most  effective insecticides  shall\n         include SOLFAC WP 10 or Baytex, The Ideal Larvicide etc.\n\n\n42.7     Alcohol and drugs\n\n\n42.7.1   The contractor shall ensure at  all times that no employee  is working under the\n          influence of alcohol / drugs which are punishable under Govt. regulations.\n\n\n42.7.2   Smoking  at  public worksites by any employee  is also prohibited as per Govt.\n          regulations."

>       "pdf_page": 65,

>       "text": ""

>     },
